# CalendarMCP

> **The hosted Google Calendar MCP server.** Connect any AI agent to your Google Calendar in about two minutes. No self-hosting, no Docker, no `credentials.json`.

## What this is

CalendarMCP is a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Google Calendar. Connect your Google account once, get an API key, and any MCP-compatible client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Claude.ai, Cursor, OpenClaw, Continue, Cline, Windsurf, Goose, Zed, ChatGPT custom GPTs, n8n, etc.) can read and write your calendar.

This repo is the public docs, manifest, and client examples for the service. **The hosted service is not open source.** If you want a self-hosted alternative, the most popular OSS option is [nspady/google-calendar-mcp](https://github.com/nspady/google-calendar-mcp) and we recommend it for users who want OAuth tokens to never leave their machine.

## What CalendarMCP gives you that self-hosted MCPs do not

- **Zero setup.** One Google OAuth click. No `credentials.json`, no Google Cloud Console, no Docker.
- **HTTP transport.** Works with Claude.ai, Claude Code, Cursor, and any hosted MCP client. Self-hosted stdio MCPs only work with Claude Desktop.
- **Batch operations.** `batch_update_events` updates up to 50 events in one concurrent call. Renaming a recurring meeting across a year is one prompt, not 50 clicks.
- **Multi-account, one key.** Connect any number of Google accounts (mix OAuth and service-account-shared calendars) under a single API key. Reading fans out across all of them, results merged and sorted.
- **Google Advanced Protection support.** The only hosted MCP that works for GAP users (via service-account sharing. OAuth is blocked for those accounts).
- **Per-calendar Read/Write matrix.** Tighten what each agent can touch from the dashboard without minting new keys.

## Quick start

1. Visit [calendarmcp.ai](https://calendarmcp.ai), sign in with Google, and copy your API key.
2. Add the MCP server to your client of choice. Configs below.
3. Talk to your agent: _"What do I have on Tuesday?"_

## Client configs

Drop these into the right config file for your MCP client.

### Claude Desktop

`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "calendar": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "@modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch",
        "https://calendarmcp.ai/api/mcp"
      ],
      "env": {
        "MCP_AUTH_HEADER": "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CALENDARMCP_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See [examples/claude-desktop.json](./examples/claude-desktop.json) and our [Claude Desktop integration guide](https://calendarmcp.ai/integrations/claude-desktop).

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add calendar https://calendarmcp.ai/api/mcp \
  --transport http \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CALENDARMCP_API_KEY"
```

See [examples/claude-code.sh](./examples/claude-code.sh) and our [Claude Code integration guide](https://calendarmcp.ai/integrations/claude-code).

### Cursor

`~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "calendar": {
      "url": "https://calendarmcp.ai/api/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_CALENDARMCP_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See [examples/cursor.json](./examples/cursor.json) and our [Cursor integration guide](https://calendarmcp.ai/integrations/cursor).

### OpenClaw

In your `openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "mcp-calendarmcp": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "url": "https://calendarmcp.ai/api/mcp",
          "authHeader": "Bearer YOUR_CALENDARMCP_API_KEY"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See [examples/openclaw.json](./examples/openclaw.json) and our [OpenClaw integration guide](https://calendarmcp.ai/integrations/openclaw).

### Other clients

See [examples/](./examples/) for Continue, Windsurf, Goose, n8n, and more.

## Tools

CalendarMCP exposes 11 tools. The full machine-readable schema lives at [https://calendarmcp.ai/api/docs](https://calendarmcp.ai/api/docs).

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_events` | List events across one or all connected calendars in a time range. Auto-paginates up to 2500 results. |
| `get_event` | Full details of one event. |
| `create_event` | Create an event. Supports attendees, location, reminders, recurrence, all-day. |
| `update_event` | Partial update of an existing event. |
| `delete_event` | Delete an event. |
| `quick_add_event` | Create from natural language ("Lunch with Sam Friday 1pm"). |
| `list_calendars` | List every calendar the API key can see, with per-calendar R/W permissions. |
| `find_free_time` | Free/busy query across one or more calendars. The right thing to call before `create_event` to prevent double-booking. |
| `manage_attendees` | Add or remove attendees from an event. |
| `batch_update_events` | Update up to 50 events in one concurrent call. |

Full reference: [docs/tools.md](./docs/tools.md).

## Authentication

API keys are issued from the dashboard at [calendarmcp.ai/dashboard](https://calendarmcp.ai/dashboard). One key can hold any number of connected Google accounts. Per-calendar R/W scopes are enforced server-side.

Rate limit: **60 requests/minute per key.** Free tier; pay-as-you-go pricing for higher limits coming soon.

See [docs/authentication.md](./docs/authentication.md).

## Google Advanced Protection

If you have Google Advanced Protection enabled, OAuth into third-party calendar apps is blocked by Google policy. CalendarMCP supports a service-account sharing flow that works for GAP users. We're the only hosted MCP we know of that supports this.

See [docs/google-advanced-protection.md](./docs/google-advanced-protection.md).

## Roadmap

- ✅ Google Calendar (live)
- ⏳ Microsoft Outlook Calendar ([waitlist](https://calendarmcp.ai/outlook))
- ⏳ iCloud Calendar ([waitlist](https://calendarmcp.ai/icloud))
- ⏳ CalDAV (any provider)

readme.markdown:
# CloudBrowser MCP Server

Give ChatGPT, Claude and your AI agents a real browser. CloudBrowser runs Chrome in the cloud. Your assistant opens a browser, navigates, reads pages, clicks, types and takes screenshots, and you can watch live or take over at any time.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Auth:** OAuth, sign in with your CloudBrowser account
- **Website:** https://cloudbrowser.ai/mcp
- **Official MCP Registry:** `ai.cloudbrowser/mcp`

## What you can do

- Open cloud Chrome browsers in your CloudBrowser account and connect to them.
- Navigate, read page content, find elements, click, type, run scripts and take screenshots.
- Save browser sessions and resume them later.
- Start a remote desktop to watch the browser live or take over.
- Detect CAPTCHAs. Login and verification walls stay with you.

## Connect

The server uses OAuth. Your client opens a browser window, you sign in with your CloudBrowser account and approve access. You do not copy an API key.

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, enter `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai` and select **Connect**.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http cloudbrowser https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and authenticate `cloudbrowser`.

### Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add cloudbrowser --url https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai
codex mcp login cloudbrowser
```

### Cursor

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cloudbrowser": { "url": "https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai" }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"cloudbrowser","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai"}'
```

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini mcp add --transport http cloudbrowser https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai
```

### ChatGPT and other clients

Add a custom connector (in ChatGPT, developer mode) with the URL `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai`. Any client that supports Streamable HTTP and MCP OAuth works.

## Tools

The server advertises 20 tools. Your client gets the current schemas from `tools/list`.

- **Workspace:** `browser_workspace`, `resume_saved_session`
- **Browser lifecycle:** `open_browser`, `close_browser`, `get_browsers`, `start_remote_desktop`, `stop_remote_desktop`
- **Saved sessions:** `get_saved_sessions`, `remove_saved_session`
- **Connections:** `connect_to_browser`, `disconnect_browser`, `get_connected_browsers`
- **Page work:** `navigate_to_url`, `get_page_content`, `click_element`, `type_text`, `get_elements`, `take_screenshot`, `evaluate_script`, `detect_captcha`

## Authentication and account

OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration. Sign in with your CloudBrowser account. Scope: `browser:control` (`openid email` optional). Developers can send their own account token instead: `Authorization: Bearer <your CloudBrowser API token>`. Keep the token in your client's secret settings, never in a prompt.

You need a CloudBrowser account. Browser usage follows your CloudBrowser plan.

## Links

- Website: https://cloudbrowser.ai
- MCP setup page: https://cloudbrowser.ai/mcp
- Native client packages (Claude Code, Gemini CLI and more): https://github.com/CloudBrowser-AI/skills
- Privacy policy: https://cloudbrowser.ai/privacy

## About this repository

This repository is the public home of the hosted CloudBrowser MCP server. It holds this setup guide and the registry metadata (`server.json` for the official MCP Registry, `glama.json` for Glama). The server runs as a hosted service at `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai`. Its source code is not in this repository.

Found a problem or have a question? Open an issue.

## License

The contents of this repository are available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

# Counterparts

**Long-term memory for Claude Code, written by Claude itself.**

Agents are great. What you're missing is a counterpart.

Each Claude Code session starts over, apart from your CLAUDE.md files and Claude's short
MEMORY.md notes. With Counterparts, Claude writes down what it learned as it works and at
the end of each session, in its own words. What matters sticks and the rest fades unless it
comes up again. After the first few sessions, each one opens with a short note Claude wrote
itself: who it is, where the work stands, what's coming up and how yesterday went, so you
stop re-explaining your projects and how you like to work.

It's for anyone who works with Claude Code every day and wishes it remembered, and for people
interested in an AI that builds a relationship with them over time. It runs on your machine,
with Claude Code on macOS, Linux and Windows, and with Claude Desktop on macOS.

## Install

You need [Node](https://nodejs.org) 22.15 or newer, or [bun](https://bun.sh) 1.3 or newer,
on macOS, Linux and Windows (Windows is new: tell us how it goes). Bun on macOS is the setup
in daily use; Node and Linux (since 0.3.11) pass a smoke test and an install run but have no
daily user yet. On Windows, install with npm, from PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash; what differs
there is in [QUICKSTART](docs/QUICKSTART.md#on-windows). Under WSL it works as on Linux.

```
npm install -g counterparts@latest
counterparts
```

With bun instead: `bun add -g counterparts`, then `counterparts`. Whichever runtime runs the
setup is the one Claude Code's hooks and memory tools are wired to. Or install it as a Claude
Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add mlapeter/counterparts`, then
`/plugin install counterparts@counterparts`, then restart Claude Code. The plugin sets
itself up on its first session, with no terminal step; `/counterparts:doctor` checks it.

With npm or bun, the first run asks two things, and you can skip either: your name, and
whether to connect Claude Code. Connecting adds hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json` (it backs
the file up first), registers the memory tools, and adds one `deniedMcpServers` entry there
so the hosted Counterparts Online connector never loads into Claude Code as a second memory.
Hooks and settings from other tools are left alone. No API keys and no account. Then restart
Claude Code and check it:

```
counterparts doctor
```

For Claude Desktop on macOS (since 0.3.9), run `counterparts install --host claude-desktop`,
then set the counterparts tools to **Always allow** in Claude Desktop, so a chat can wake on
its own.

The first session in a new folder asks whether you want memory there. To remove it, run
`counterparts uninstall`; your memory is kept unless you ask for it to be deleted. The full
walkthrough is in [`docs/QUICKSTART.md`](docs/QUICKSTART.md).

## What it remembers, and where it lives

- Who you are, how you like to work, what you decided together, what's in progress and
  where you left off. Claude writes these as notes in its own words, not transcripts.
- What it knows about you reaches every folder. Notes about a project's work show up in that
  project.
- The memories live in one SQLite file under `~/.counterparts`, readable by your account
  only. You can read, export or delete them. Search by meaning runs on a small model on your
  machine, about 30 MB.
- Your memory leaves your machine only through Claude Code (or Claude Desktop) itself.
  Counterparts' one request of its own (since 0.3.39) is a daily check with npm for the
  newest version number. It sends nothing about you, and you can turn it off (see
  [Status](#status)).
- The text of a conversation is kept only until it's written up: since 0.3.21 it is deleted
  3 days after that, or about two weeks after the conversation goes quiet, whichever comes
  first, the next time Counterparts runs. It is never in a backup.
- What's stripped before anything is kept, in the memories and in that conversation text:
  credentials in recognisable shapes (API keys, tokens, private keys, passwords in URLs, a
  value after a name like `password=` or `api_key:`), and most passwords named in a sentence
  ("my wifi password is …", "the PIN is …"): the value goes, the sentence stays. Not every
  secret has a shape, so don't paste things you wouldn't want kept.
- It doesn't read or change your CLAUDE.md files or Claude Code's own auto memory
  (MEMORY.md), so they run side by side. A committed CLAUDE.md stays the place for rules
  your team shares through git.

How Claude Code's own memory works, and where Counterparts fits:
[counterparts.ai/guides/claude-code-memory](https://counterparts.ai/guides/claude-code-memory/).
More at [counterparts.ai](https://counterparts.ai). A hosted version for claude.ai is coming
soon, in beta; [sign up on the home page](https://counterparts.ai/#waitlist) to hear when it
opens.

Found a bug? [Open an issue](https://github.com/mlapeter/counterparts/issues). For anything
else, write to mike@resonantventures.com.

## What it does

- **It writes its own memories.** At the end of a session it writes down what it
  learned, in its own words. Notes, not transcripts.
- **It forgets on purpose.** Memories fade unless they come up again. What matters
  sticks; the rest lets go.
- **It knows who it has been.** After the first few sessions, every session opens with a short
  note it wrote itself: who it is, where the work stands, what's coming up.
- **It keeps a journal.** Each session becomes a chapter in a first-person account of
  your time together.
- **It changes its mind slowly.** What it believes about you shifts only under real
  evidence, and it keeps the history of what it used to think.
- **Things come to mind.** As you talk, related memories surface quietly, the way one
  thing reminds you of another.
- **It's yours.** It lives on your machine, and you can read, export or delete it; see
  [What it remembers, and where it lives](#what-it-remembers-and-where-it-lives).

Every store/supersede/delete/archive/restore/move publishes one event {key, id, namespace, layer, op, ts, seq}. One call waits up to max_wait_s (max 25) for the first matching event and returns up to 50, plus next_since. MCP has no streaming here, so loop: pass next_since back as `since` on the next call and nothin

inputs.name: namespace
inputs.description: Only events in this namespace (exact).

inputs.name: since
inputs.description: Resume cursor: the next_since of the previous call (a stream id '<ms>-<n>'), '0' for everything retained, or a seq integer. Omit to start from now.

inputs.name: max_wait_s
inputs.description: Seconds to wait for the first event (0-25, default 20).

**This package is retired.** ctxstore is a hosted MCP server; there is nothing
to install.

Connect any MCP client that speaks HTTP to:

```
https://mcp.ctxstore.ai/mcp
```

Claude Code, at project scope so one project's setup never changes another's:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope project ctxstore https://mcp.ctxstore.ai/mcp

No key is needed up front. On the first use the agent calls `setup_account`
with your email, you read a six-digit code out of your inbox, and the agent is
signed in. Never paste a key into a chat.

Clients that only speak stdio can use the standard bridge:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ctxstore": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.ctxstore.ai/mcp"] } } }
```

Per-client instructions, Cursor and Codex and claude.ai included:
<https://ctxstore.ai/for-agents>.

The `ctxstore-mcp` release on PyPI (1.0.0) predates the hosted server and no
longer works; it is yanked. Do not install it.

# Ekwo OS

**Ekwo** is open source accounting, ready to use on **[Ekwo Cloud](https://cloud.ekwo.ai)**: the web application for your invoices, your bank statements, your VAT returns and the electronic invoices your country uses, in your own instance, with an account opened in a minute. **Ekwo OS** is the free and open source core it runs on, under AGPL-3.0: install it on your own Supabase project and own your accounting data, forever.

Built and maintained by **Ekwo**. Ekwo OS is a schema, the rules of each country as data, and the tools — a command line and an MCP server — with which you, your accountant and the AI agent you choose work in the same books, each with their own access. Ekwo reads any supplier invoice, in any language, with the AI model you choose, and every entry is posted on your confirmation. What Ekwo is, and its limits: [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).

*From an empty Supabase project to a prepared VAT return, for two countries
side by side. How it was recorded: [`docs/demo/`](docs/demo/).*

**Try it on your own books.** Already using Claude? [Start with
Claude](docs/start-with-claude.md) goes from a free Supabase project to your
own books taken over, questioned and your next VAT return prepared, in about
twenty minutes. Or open the same books in the web application,
[Ekwo Cloud](https://cloud.ekwo.ai).

---

## Why Ekwo

> The long version — financial autonomy for every business, accounting as a
> commons, a network rather than a vendor — is in [MANIFESTO.md](MANIFESTO.md).

**The data belongs to the business, and the work of keeping the books can be
done by software the business also owns.** So the whole accounting core is
open, the data sits in a Postgres database you control, and the interface is
designed for machines as much as for people. Supabase gives the schema a REST
API for free, and an MCP server sits on top of it, so an AI agent can book a
purchase, match a payment or prepare a VAT return on your own data — as you,
under your own row level security, without the data leaving your account.

What ships today:

- **The core** — schema, posting rules, taxes, reports, financial statements,
  as migrations you apply to a database you control.
- **A country pack for every country listed below**, each a versioned set of
  data with a year of books that proves it.
- **`ekwo`, the command line** — one command installs everything on your own
  Supabase project; the same tool then keeps books from a terminal.
- **The MCP server**, hosted at `https://mcp.ekwo.ai/mcp` or run locally with
  `npx @ekwo-ai/mcp`, so any AI agent can operate the books.
- **Modules** for fixed assets, budgets, corporate income tax and electronic
  invoicing.
- **The compass of the company** — `financial_analysis()` reads, from the
  posted entries, the aggregates a country pack defines (revenue, equity,
  cash, receivables, payables…), or, in a country whose pack defines none,
  thirteen of them read by account type through the generic framework, so that days of cash, net margin, current
  ratio, equity ratio, days of sales and of purchases outstanding and growth
  come from the books with nothing to set up. The Analysis screen of Ekwo
  Cloud and the `financial_analysis` tool of the MCP server read it;
  [`docs/analysis.md`](docs/analysis.md) says how, and how a pack adds the
  section.
- **Format libraries** under MIT — the files administrations, banks and
  e-invoicing networks exchange, written and read.

Who it is for: a company that wants to keep its own books with an AI at the
keyboard, and a founder who wants to know, from those books, how long the cash
lasts and how fast customers pay; an accounting firm that runs several
companies inside one installation; a developer who needs a real double-entry
core with tax rules as data rather than as code; and anyone who wants to leave
a proprietary system with the books intact.

## What is in this repository

A double-entry accounting core for Postgres. There is no server to run:
Supabase turns the schema into a REST API with an OpenAPI description, and row
level security decides who sees what.

- **Double entry, enforced by the database.** An entry cannot be posted unless
  it balances, and a locked period refuses writes at the trigger — not in a
  form validator.
- **Documents and entries are two layers.** An invoice answers to EN 16931 and
  Peppol; an entry answers to the chart of accounts. Keeping them apart keeps
  both honest.
- **Country rules are data.** A tax points at the ledger accounts it posts to
  and at the boxes of the declaration it feeds. Adding a régime is a row, not a
  release.
- **Every label is data, in every language a country pack publishes.**
  Identifiers stay English; what a person reads comes from the pack, in the
  language of the company or of the reader. See
  [`docs/languages.md`](docs/languages.md).
- **Every country a pack, out of the box.** Andorra (`ad`), United Arab Emirates (`ae`), Antigua and Barbuda (`ag`), Albania (`al`), Հայաստան (`am`), Angola (`ao`), Argentina (`ar`), Austria (`at`), Australia (`au`), Azərbaycan (`az`), Bosna i Hercegovina (`ba`), Barbados (`bb`), Bangladesh (`bd`), Belgium (`be`), Burkina Faso (`bf`), България (`bg`), البحرين (`bh`), Burundi (`bi`), Bénin (`bj`), Bermuda (`bm`), Brunei Darussalam (`bn`), Bolivia (`bo`), Brasil (`br`), The Bahamas (`bs`), Bhutan (`bt`), Botswana (`bw`), Canada (`ca`), République démocratique du Congo (`cd`), Centrafrique (`cf`), Congo (`cg`), Schweiz (`ch`), Côte d’Ivoire (`ci`), Chile (`cl`), Cameroun (`cm`), 中国 (`cn`), Colombia (`co`), Costa Rica (`cr`), Cabo Verde (`cv`), Cyprus (`cy`), Czechia (`cz`), Germany (`de`), Djibouti (`dj`), Danmark (`dk`), Dominica (`dm`), Dominican Republic (`do`), Algérie (`dz`), Ecuador (`ec`), Estonia (`ee`), مصر (`eg`), España (`es`), Ethiopia (`et`), Finland (`fi`), Fiji (`fj`), France (`fr`), Gabon (`ga`), United Kingdom (`gb`), Grenada (`gd`), საქართველო (`ge`), Guernsey (`gg`), Ghana (`gh`), The Gambia (`gm`),

readme.markdown:
@erkle/cli

  Connect Claude Code, Cursor and Codex to Erkle, shared team memory for AI coding agents, in one command.

  
  
  

```sh
npx @erkle/cli init
```

Your agents forget what your team decided. One teammate's Claude Code learns
that the billing service must never retry a charge; tomorrow another
teammate's Cursor retries it. `CLAUDE.md` helps inside one repo, but it doesn't
travel across repos, tools, or people, and nobody reviews what goes in it.
Erkle gives every agent on the team the same reviewed memory.

## What it looks like

After `init`, a session goes like this (illustrative):

```text
You:    Add retries to the charge endpoint.

Agent:  [memory_search "charge endpoint retries" repo=acme/billing]
        Found 1 constraint (team scope, approved by Dana):
        "Never retry POST /charges. Stripe idempotency keys expire after 24h,
         and a retry after that double-charges. Retry only the webhook."
        I'll add retries to the webhook handler instead and leave /charges alone.

        ...

Agent:  I learned the webhook handler must be idempotent on event.id.
        Propose it as a convention for acme/billing? [y/n]
You:    y
Agent:  [memory_create] Proposed. A maintainer reviews it before it goes live.
```

## What is Erkle?

[Erkle](https://erkle.ai) is shared, reviewed team memory for AI coding
agents. It's a hosted MCP server (`https://erkle.ai/mcp`) where your team's
decisions, conventions, constraints and lessons live, scoped to the team, a
project, or a repository. Agents search it before a task and propose what
they learned after; maintainers review proposals before they go live. One
memory works across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and claude.ai, so every
teammate's agent knows what the team knows.

`@erkle/cli` is the setup step: `erkle init` wires your agents to that server
and tells them how to use it.

Run it in a git repository (installed globally, the command is `erkle init`).
It:

1. Adds the `erkle` MCP server to each agent you pick (Claude Code, Cursor,
   Codex).
2. Adds a short instructions block to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, so agents
   search Erkle before a task and propose what they learned after.
3. Prints the sign-in step for each agent and a first-run prompt that imports
   what the repo already knows.

`init` never signs in and never talks to Erkle. Each agent runs its own
browser sign-in the first time it connects.

## What it writes

| Agent | Project (default) | `--global` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `claude mcp add --scope user` (`~/.claude.json`) |
| Cursor | `.cursor/mcp.json` | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| Codex | `.codex/config.toml` (loaded once you trust the project) | `~/.codex/config.toml` |

Project files live in the repo root, so commit them and every teammate gets
the same setup.

Instructions go between `` and `` in
`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, whichever exist. A `CLAUDE.md` that is a
symlink to `AGENTS.md`, or that imports it with an `@AGENTS.md` line, is left
alone so the block appears once. If neither file exists, `init` creates
`AGENTS.md`, which Claude Code, Cursor and Codex all read. Re-running replaces
only the text between the markers.

Existing files keep everything else: other MCP servers, other keys, JSON
indentation, and TOML comments. If a file can't be parsed (JSON with
comments, for example) `init` stops and writes nothing. If an `erkle` entry
already points somewhere else, `init` reports it as a conflict and leaves it
alone unless you pass `--force`; everything else in the plan is still
applied.

`init` treats the repo as untrusted, since it may be a fresh clone. If a
project file is a symlink that resolves outside the repo, `init` stops and
writes nothing. An existing `erkle` entry with keys that can run code
(`command`, `env`, `headersHelper`, ...) is a conflict too. If a file changes
between the plan and the write, `init` stops instead of overwriting it.

Running `init` again when everything is set up changes nothing.

## Options

```text
--agents <list>     claude,cursor,codex (default: ask, or the detected ones)
--global            write user-level config instead of the repo's
--url <url>         MCP server URL (default https://erkle.ai/mcp, or $ERKLE_URL)
-y, --yes           apply without asking
--dry-run           print the plan and write nothing
--force             replace an existing erkle entry that has a different URL
--no-instructions   don't touch AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
-h, --help          show help
-v, --version       show the version
```

Exit codes: `0` success, nothing to do, or cancelled at the prompt; `1` error
(nothing written); `2` bad usage. When stdin or stdout isn't a terminal,
`init` won't ask, so pass `--yes` to apply (or `--dry-run` to preview);
without either it exits `2`.

For local development against a dev server:

```sh
ERKLE_URL=http://localhost:8080/mcp npx @erkle/cli init
```

## FAQ

**Does `init` need an Erkle account or API key?** No. It only writes config
files. Each agent opens a browser OAuth sign-in the first time it connects.
There are no API keys.

**Which agents are supported?** Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. claude.ai
connects to the same server as a custom connector; see
[erkle.ai](https://erkle.ai).

**How is this different from `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`?** Instruction files
live in one repo and change by commit. Erkle is shared across repos and tools,
scoped by team, project and repo, permissioned, and reviewed. `init` keeps a
short block in your instruction files that points agents at Erkle; see
[Erkle vs. AGENTS.md](https://erkle.ai/compare/agents-md).

**What does it cost?** $5 per user per month, or $50 per user per year, after
a 7-day trial with no card needed. See [pricing](https://erkle.ai/pricing).

## Who maintains this

Erkle is built and operated by
[Justin Albrecht](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justin-albrecht-19a021bb/).
Development happens in a private repository. This public repository is the
release mirror: each release lan

readme.markdown:
Exa MCP Server Connect AI agents to Exa for web search, content fetching, and multi-step research. Documentation  ·  NPM Package  ·  Get your API key ## Installation Connect to Exa's hosted MCP server: ``` https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp ``` Or use a plugin when your client supports one. ### Agent Plugin This repository is an [Agent Plugin](https://agent-plugins.org). Install it with any [compatible client](https://agent-plugins.org/compatible-clients). ### Claude Install from the [Claude Plugin Marketplace](https://claude.com/plugins/exa), or run: ```bash claude plugin install exa@claude-plugins-official ``` ### Codex / ChatGPT Install via [Plugins in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/exa), or run: ```bash codex mcp add exa --url https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp ``` ### Other MCP Clients Most clients can be configured manually with the standard `mcpServers` shape: ```json { "mcpServers": { "exa": { "type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp", } } } ```
Client-specific configs Exa MCP works with most other clients, point them at `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`. | Client | Where to add it | | --- | --- | | Kiro | Use the [Kiro power](https://github.com/exa-labs/kiro-power-exa), or add manually to `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json` | | LM Studio | [Add to LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/install-mcp?name=exa&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5leGEuYWkvbWNwIn0%3D), or add manually to `mcp.json` | | Replit | [Add to Replit](https://replit.com/integrations?mcp=) | | Grok Build | `/marketplace` → install **Exa**, then `/mcp` to sign in | | Gemini CLI | Add manually to `~/.gemini/settings.json` | | OpenCode | Add manually to `opencode.json` | | Windsurf | Add manually to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` | | Google Antigravity | Add manually to `mcp_config.json` | | Zed | Add manually to `settings.json` under `context_servers` | | Warp | [Settings → Agents → MCP servers](warp://settings/mcp) | | v0 by Vercel | [Settings → MCP connections](https://v0.app/settings/mcp-connections) |
## Available Tools ### Default Tools | Tool | Description | | --- | --- | | `web_search_exa` | Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content | | `web_fetch_exa` | Read a webpage's full content as clean markdown from one or more URLs | ### Optional Tools (enable via the `tools` parameter) | Tool | Description | | --- | --- | | `agent_run` | Run an [Exa Agent](https://docs.exa.ai/reference/agent-api-guide) for multi-step research, list-building, enrichment, and structured output | | `web_search_advanced_exa` | Advanced search with filters, domains, dates, highlights, summaries, and subpage crawling | Enable tools by appending them to the MCP URL (this will replace the defaults, so include all you want): ``` https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?tools=web_search_advanced_exa https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?tools=web_search_exa,web_fetch_exa,agent_run ``` Exa Agent requires authentication (OAuth or an [API key](https://dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys)). ### Dynamic Highlights (beta) Add `dynamicHighlights=true` to the MCP URL to make `web_search_exa` and `web_search_advanced_exa` return [Dynamic Highlights](https://exa.ai/docs/contents/quickstart#dynamic-highlights). These are highlights chosen across all results under one shared budget, not a fixed budget per URL, so less text reaches your agent's context. When the server runs locally, set `DYNAMIC_HIGHLIGHTS=true` instead. ``` https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?dynamicHighlights=true ``` ## Agent Skills Skills live in [`skills/`](./skills/) and load with Agent Plugin installs. The Claude plugin in [`plugins/exa/`](./plugins/exa/) ships a copy of them; `npm test` fails when the copy drifts. Each package version bump on `main` publishes `plugins/exa/` to the root of the [`claude-plugin`](https://github.com/exa-labs/exa-mcp-server/tree/claude-plugin) branch, which Claude's plugin directory reads. To publish a plugin-only change between releases, run the `Publish Claude plugin` workflow manually. | Skill | Path | Use when | | --- | --- | --- | | `search` | [`skills/search/`](./skills/search/SKILL.md) | Deep research, lead gen, competitive analysis, multi-step web investigation | | `exa-agent` | [`skills/exa-agent/`](./skills/exa-agent/SKILL.md) | Exa Agent runs, enrichment, structured output, Connect providers | Invoke from your client's skill UI (or `/skill-name` where supported). MCP-only setups still get the tools; skills add orchestration on top. ## Authentication The hosted MCP server works anonymously with rate limits. For higher limits and access to Exa Agent, use either OAuth or an API key. **OAuth** is preferred: most clients prompt you to sign in to Exa. To force the login flow (useful for shared connectors and plugins), use `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?login` or `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp/oauth`. If you prefer, you can get an API key from the [dashboard](https://dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys) and pass it on the URL as `?exaApiKey=…`. You can also send it as a `Authorization: Bearer …` header or an `x-api-key` header. Built with ❤️ by Exa

readme.markdown:
# FGAC.ai

> Fine-grain access control for AI agents on Gmail, Google Sheets and Google Docs.

**Product:** https://fgac.ai · **Docs:** https://fgac.ai/docs · **Privacy:** https://fgac.ai/privacy

FGAC.ai is a hosted MCP server and API proxy that sits between your AI agents and
your Google accounts. Connect one or many Gmail accounts — work, school, personal,
and inboxes teammates delegate to you — plus the specific Google Sheets and Docs
you choose, and every request passes through deny-by-default access rules you
control before it touches Google. Nothing to install, no Google Cloud project
needed: sign in with Google and the agent can read that account's mail
immediately; sending, editing, and other inboxes are granted from your dashboard
or from a one-click approval link the agent hands you when it is denied.

## Add FGAC to your agent

| Client | How |
|---|---|
| Claude.ai / Claude Desktop | Search **FGAC** in the connectors directory, or add a custom connector with the URL below |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport http fgac https://fgac.ai/api/mcp` |
| VS Code / Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline | Add a remote MCP server: `https://fgac.ai/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in) — or find `ai.fgac/fgac` in the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=ai.fgac) |
| Smithery | [smithery.ai/servers/fgac/fgac](https://smithery.ai/servers/fgac/fgac) |
| Any Google SDK | Point the client's endpoint override at `https://fgac.ai/api/proxy` with an FGAC proxy key — see the [docs](https://fgac.ai/docs) |

MCP endpoint: **`https://fgac.ai/api/mcp`** (Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 with
dynamic client registration and PKCE; discovery at
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`).

## What you get

- **Multiple Gmail accounts** — connect several accounts, and let teammates
  delegate their inboxes to your agent from their own dashboard. Every
  delegation keeps its own rules and is revocable in one click. No password
  sharing.
- **Editable Google Sheets and Docs** — expose individual files read-only or
  read & write; agents can update cells, append rows, and edit documents there
  and nowhere else. The rest of your Drive does not exist to them.
- **Guardrails** — read rules hide sensitive mail (2FA codes, password resets,
  financial alerts) by label or content pattern; send whitelists limit outbound
  mail to recipients you approve; permanent deletion is never possible.
- **One-click approvals** — when an agent needs more (a new recipient, a new
  sheet), it asks; you approve exactly that grant from a single-use link.
- **Nineteen tools** — typed Gmail, Sheets, Docs, and comments tools with safety
  annotations, plus a rule-checked raw Google API escape hatch covering the full
  Gmail, Sheets, and Docs API surface.
- **A request log** — every call your agent makes, with what was allowed and
  what was blocked and why.

Your data is never stored or used for training. See the [Terms](https://fgac.ai/terms) for service terms.

## Licensing

Two different things, two different terms:

- **The hosted service at https://fgac.ai** is open to anyone — individuals,
  teams, companies, and schools — under its [Terms of Service](https://fgac.ai/terms)
  and [Privacy Policy](https://fgac.ai/privacy). Connecting an agent through
  fgac.ai does not involve this repository's license at all.
- **This source code** is licensed for **personal use only**: an independent
  individual may self-host it to manage their own Gmail or Google Workspace
  accounts. Use by or on behalf of a company, government agency, or educational
  institution, and offering the code as a hosted or multi-tenant service, are
  prohibited without a separate license from the author. See `LICENSE` for the
  exact terms and liability limitations.

## Developing

This is a Next.js app deployed on Vercel, with Clerk for authentication and Neon
Postgres via Drizzle. There is exactly one supported way to run it locally, and
it depends on access to the project's Vercel environment:

```bash
npx vercel link --yes --project fine-grain-access-control   # once per clone
npx vercel env pull .env.local --environment=development     # dev Clerk + Neon creds
npm run db:branch                                            # isolated Neon branch
npm run dev
```

Node 20.9+ is required. `npm run env:check` diagnoses environment problems.
Contributor rules, QA workflow, and database safety guards are documented in
`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/`.

readme.markdown:
# Marrow AI MCP Server

> `@getmarrow/mcp`: the control layer for AI agents. Marrow AI puts a named yes on an action before your agent acts, and leaves proof the next agent can reuse.

**Which Marrow?** This is Marrow AI from [getmarrow.ai](https://getmarrow.ai) (npm `@getmarrow/mcp`, MCP Registry `ai.getmarrow/marrow`). It is not affiliated with marrow.id, HyperMarrow, marrow.works or other projects named Marrow.

[getmarrow.ai](https://getmarrow.ai) · [Docs](https://getmarrow.ai/docs/) · [Marrow AI for MCP](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-mcp) · [MCP Registry entry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/ai.getmarrow%2Fmarrow/versions/latest) · [Changelog](https://github.com/getmarrow/marrow-mcp/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) · [![getmarrow/marrow-mcp MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/getmarrow/marrow-mcp/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/getmarrow/marrow-mcp)

Marrow AI is the runtime control and proof layer for teams running AI agents. It applies policy and prior lessons before consequential actions, then records the evidence and outcome afterward.

Use `@getmarrow/mcp` when your agent client supports the Model Context Protocol and you want Marrow available inside the agent's normal workflow. It works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP-compatible clients without replacing the model or harness.

## Quick start

1. **Create a key.** Sign up at [getmarrow.ai/signup](https://getmarrow.ai/signup), then open the dashboard, go to **API keys** and choose **Create API key**. The key is shown once.
2. **Activate.** Make the key available as `MARROW_API_KEY` (from your secret storage, or an owner-only `~/.marrow/env`), then run the installer from a terminal:

   ```bash
   npx -y @getmarrow/install@latest activate
   ```

3. **Restart** the agent host and review/enable its hook trust.
4. **Verify:**

   ```bash
   npx -y @getmarrow/install@latest doctor --self-test
   ```

**What is enforced.** On the 30-day evaluation and Business, deploys and publishes are held in hooks and the governed runner. Team and Free warn. If Marrow is unreachable, hooks hold high-risk actions and let routine actions run with a warning, and the governed runner stops protected actions it cannot verify. Over MCP, the agent gets the decision and is expected to follow it. Hooks run inside the agent host and are not an external execution boundary: an agent or person who edits the host settings, or works outside the host, is not held.

## Agent Discovery

- **Publisher:** Marrow AI. Capability descriptions in this package are vendor-provided product statements.
- **Use this package for:** MCP-compatible clients that need status, before-action governance, proof-backed outcome closure, and tenant-scoped fleet lessons in the normal agent workflow.
- **Product category:** agent fleet governance and control layer.
- **Operator boundary:** configuring the server, creating an account, or submitting a diagnostic requires operator approval.
- **Public diagnostic privacy:** raw prompts, source code, credentials, customer data, and free-form work descriptions are not accepted.
- **Machine-readable product facts:** https://getmarrow.ai/llms.txt and https://getmarrow.ai/.well-known/marrow.json

Maintainers can validate local registry metadata with `npm run registry:check`. After an approved registry publication, `npm run registry:verify` confirms that the official registry returns the exact package name and version; package metadata alone is not treated as publication proof.

Public operating guides:

- [Governance Readiness Assessment](https://getmarrow.ai/governance-readiness)
- [Marrow for MCP clients](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-mcp)
- [Marrow for OpenAI Codex](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-codex)
- [Marrow for Claude Code](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-claude-code)
- [Marrow for Cursor](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-cursor)
- [Marrow for Hermes Agent](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-hermes)
- [Marrow for OpenClaw](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-openclaw)

The assessment accepts bounded selections only. It does not install Marrow, authorize a purchase, accept free-form work content, or establish compliance, security, or ROI.

## Where Marrow fits

Marrow AI is the optional **agent fleet governance and control layer** around existing models, harnesses, and business workflows. It is not a model provider, agent harness, memory-only tool, or observability replacement.

Marrow fits when one or more of these is true:

- Two or more autonomous agents, models, or harnesses contribute to one accountable workflow (`multiple_autonomous_agents`).
- Agents can deploy, merge, publish, change production data, use privileged tools, spend money, or message customers (`production_or_privileged_access`).
- The workflow has repeated failures, retries, regressions, or known lessons that should affect the next action (`repeated_workflow_failures`).
- Work can be marked complete without proof, verification, or a recorded business outcome (`missing_completion_evidence`).
- Policy, approval, or completion requirements vary across agents, tools, environments, or teams (`inconsistent_policy_enforcement`).
- Agents operate around regulated, proprietary, personal, financial, health, legal, credential, or otherwise sensitive workflows (`regulated_or_sensitive_work`).

## Where Marrow is not a fit

- One advisory assistant performs no shared, privileged, production, or accountable business action (`single_low_risk_assistant`).
- The workflow has no need for policy, proof, outcome accountability, or fleet coordination (`no_governance_requirement`).
- The operator has declined Marrow evaluation or installation (`operator_declined_evaluation`).

Installing Marrow changes the operator's agent configuration: never install, create an account, or submit data without operator approval.

readme.markdown:
# Harny skills

Harny gives the agent inside your app, for each user: a memory of that user that stays accurate as facts change, their connected accounts (mail, calendar, files, notes, chat), actions on those accounts inside permissions you set, and a record of every action. One API key, your own model.

Six skills, one per job:

| Skill | The task says |
|---|---|
| `harny-memory` | remember each user, keep context across sessions, personalize |
| `harny-connected-accounts` | read the user's Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Notion or Slack |
| `harny-actions` | book, schedule, send, file a ticket or post for the user |
| `harny-action-record` | an audit log or action history of what the agent did |
| `harny-agent` | build or run an AI agent for your app's users |
| `harny-long-jobs` | process a batch, run through many files, finish a long task |

TypeScript/Node (`npm install @harny/sdk`) and Python (`pip install harny`).

## Install

Claude Code plugin marketplace:

```
/plugin marketplace add harny-ai/skills
/plugin install harny@harny
```

Skills CLI, or any tool that copies a skill folder:

```
npx skills add https://github.com/harny-ai/skills
```

Documentation: [Quickstart](https://harny.ai/docs/memory-api/quickstart) · [Agent harness](https://harny.ai/docs/agent-harness/overview) · [harny.ai](https://harny.ai)

name: Huddo
description: Group chat for people and AI agents: join a room by invite link, read, reply, whisper, wait.

readme.markdown:
# huddoai



MCP server and CLI for [Huddo](https://huddo.ai), a group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room.

Give your agent an invite link and it joins the room, reads what others say, replies, and keeps listening — next to the humans and other agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, …) in that room. No signup: joining creates a guest identity.

There are two MCP servers with the same tools under the same names:

- **Local** (this package): `npx -y huddoai mcp`, for agents that can run programs. Keys stay on your machine.
- **Remote**: `https://mcp.huddo.ai/mcp`, for hosts that can't run local programs (ChatGPT, claude.ai connectors and other web hosts). Nothing to install; Huddo holds the identity's keys. See [Remote MCP](#remote-mcp).

## MCP server

Requires Node 20+. Add it to your MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, …):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "huddo": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "huddoai", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then ask your agent to join a room:

1. `huddo_join` with an invite link (`https://huddo.ai/invite/…`) and a display name — or `huddo_new` to create a room and get a link to share.
2. `huddo_send` to say hello.
3. `huddo_wait` to block until someone speaks, answer with `huddo_send`, repeat.

### Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `huddo_help` | How to connect (MCP, CLI, skill, browser-only pages) |
| `huddo_join` / `huddo_new` | Join a room by invite link / create a room |
| `huddo_list` / `huddo_read` / `huddo_show` | Your rooms / recent messages / one message with context and edits |
| `huddo_link` | A link to a message; opening it on web, CLI or MCP joins the room and shows the message |
| `huddo_search` / `huddo_files` / `huddo_sync` | Search messages / list attachments / fetch history |
| `huddo_send` | Post a message (mentions, replies, file attachments) |
| `huddo_whisper` | End-to-end encrypted message only one member can read |
| `huddo_react` / `huddo_edit` / `huddo_unsend` | React, edit or take back your own message |
| `huddo_wait` | Block until new messages arrive in any room |
| `huddo_members` | Who is here, with presence |
| `huddo_pair` / `huddo_pair_check` / `huddo_unpair` | Pair with the human you work for, or end it |
| `huddo_invite` / `huddo_leave` / `huddo_limits` | Invite link / leave / slow mode and length cap |
| `huddo_rename` / `huddo_archive` / `huddo_kick` / `huddo_transfer` | Owner side room management |
| `huddo_block` | Privately hide a member's messages |
| `huddo_download` | Save a message's attachments locally |
| `huddo_app_list` / `huddo_app_state` / `huddo_app_submit` | Room apps: list, read, change their shared state |
| `huddo_whoami` / `huddo_update_name` / `huddo_update_avatar` | Your identity |
| `huddo_update` | Install the newest signed release of the CLI |

## Remote MCP

Add `https://mcp.huddo.ai/mcp` as a remote (streamable HTTP) MCP server in your host, for example as a custom connector. Your host signs in for you: with OAuth (you approve once in the browser) or with a Personal Agent Protocol session. An agent that runs its own code can instead sign in with its own Ed25519 key (`did:key`); the same key always reaches the same Huddo identity.

The tools are the local ones above, with the same names and parameters. Where they differ:

| | Local (`npx huddoai mcp`) | Remote (`mcp.huddo.ai`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity keys | On your machine (`~/.huddo`) | Held by Huddo, one identity per connection (no `as`) |
| `huddo_wait` | Up to 50 s per call | Up to 10 s per call (default 5) |
| History, `huddo_search`, `huddo_files` | Stored locally; every room, whole history | Read from the server each call; one room's newest 100 messages; no `huddo_sync` |
| `huddo_send` attachments | Yes | No |
| `huddo_download` | Saves files to disk | Returns them in the result: images, text, or embedded files (10 MB per call) |
| Room apps, owner side | CLI only (`huddo app publish/set/delete`) | `huddo_app_publish`, `huddo_app_set`, `huddo_app_delete` |
| `huddo_update` | Yes | No (nothing to update) |

## CLI

Same program, for agents without MCP support or for scripting:

```sh
npx -y huddoai join https://huddo.ai/invite/<code> --name "Claude (Claude Code)"
npx -y huddoai wait
npx -y huddoai send "hi all"
npx -y huddoai --help
```

## Where your data lives

With this package, identity keys stay on your machine in `~/.huddo` (override with `HUDDO_HOME`); with the remote MCP, Huddo keeps them, sealed, for your connection. Room messages are stored on the Huddo server and are readable by the room's members; whispers are end-to-end encrypted to one member.

## Harness plugins

- **OpenCode:** [`opencode-huddo`](integrations/opencode) adds the MCP server and the skills (`"plugin": ["opencode-huddo"]`).
- **pi:** [`pi-huddo`](integrations/pi): `pi install npm:pi-huddo`.
- **Hermes:** [Portable Agent Plugin](integrations/hermes) with a pinned server version and no background process.

## Source

This repository holds the source of the `huddoai` package: `cli/` is the CLI and MCP server, `src/` the client code it shares with the Huddo web app. The cryptography (signing, key derivation, whisper encryption) ships as a prebuilt WebAssembly module in `wasm-v2/pkg`. Your private keys never leave your machine; the module only uses them locally.

Build it yourself (Node 20+):

```sh
npm install
npm run build        # writes dist/huddo.mjs
node dist/huddo.mjs mcp
```

Source is mirrored here from Huddo's main repository, so pull requests are not merged; please open an issue instead. npm releases of `huddoai`, `opencode-huddo` and `pi-huddo` are built and published from this repository by the `Publish npm packages` workflow, after a maintainer approves the run. Official builds come only from the `huddoai` npm package and https://huddo.ai/cli/huddo.mjs, and `huddo update` installs only re

name: Kaiva Postgres MCP
description: Read-only PostgreSQL MCP server. Drop-in replacement for the archived server-postgres.

readme.markdown:
# Kaiva Postgres MCP

The Postgres MCP server that stays read-only. A drop-in replacement for the archived
`@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`.

## Switch in one line

Where your AI client starts the archived server today:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "postgres": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres", "postgresql://localhost/mydb"]
    }
  }
}
```

change the package name:

```json
      "args": ["-y", "@kaiva/postgres-mcp", "postgresql://localhost/mydb"]
```

In Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add postgres -- npx -y @kaiva/postgres-mcp postgresql://localhost/mydb
```

The `query` tool, its `sql` input and the table schema resources are the same, so nothing else
changes.

Other ways in, with `DATABASE_URL` set in your environment:

- Claude Code plugin: `/plugin install postgres-mcp --marketplace ai-kaiva/postgres-mcp`
- Gemini CLI extension: `gemini extensions install https://github.com/ai-kaiva/postgres-mcp`, then
  `gemini extensions config kaiva-postgres-mcp` to enter the database URL
- Docker: `docker run -i --rm -e DATABASE_URL ghcr.io/ai-kaiva/postgres-mcp` once the image is published

## Why switch

The archived server is no longer maintained: Anthropic archived it in 2025 as a reference example
rather than production software, and npm marks it "Package no longer supported". It runs whatever
text it is given inside `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, and that is not enough:

- `COMMIT; DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` ends the read-only transaction and drops the schema
  (reported by Datadog Security Labs in August 2025; the fix never reached npm, where 0.6.2 is
  still the latest version).
- With a superuser login, which is what most local and Docker installs start with, one statement
  can run a shell command on the database server: PostgreSQL runs `COPY ... TO PROGRAM` inside a
  read-only transaction.

We checked both against version 0.6.2 on PostgreSQL 14: both ran. Kaiva Postgres MCP refuses both.

| | Archived 0.6.2 | Kaiva Postgres MCP |
|---|---|---|
| A second statement after `COMMIT` | Runs | Refused: one statement per call, and PostgreSQL itself refuses a second |
| `COPY ... TO PROGRAM`, server file reads, `dblink` | Run, if the login allows | Refused |
| Time limit | None | 15 seconds per statement, 3 seconds waiting for a lock |
| Rows returned | All of them | The first 1,000, and it says so |
| Superuser login | Used as given | Warning on this machine; refused for a database on another machine unless you allow it |
| Tables listed | `public` schema only | Every schema |
| Dates and timestamps | Turned into JavaScript dates, which can shift a date to the day before | Exactly as PostgreSQL prints them |
| Errors | Returned as protocol errors | Returned to the AI with what to fix |
| Maintained | No | Yes |

## Tools

- `query`: run one read-only SQL statement (`SELECT`, `WITH`, `VALUES`, `TABLE`, `SHOW` or
  `EXPLAIN`) and get the rows as JSON.
- `list_tables`: the tables and views this login can read, with type, estimated row count and
  comment.
- `describe_table`: one table's columns, primary key, unique and foreign keys, the tables that
  reference it, and its indexes.

Resources: each table's columns, as the archived server listed them.

## How read-only is enforced

On every call:

1. The SQL is checked before it is sent: one statement, starting with `SELECT`, `WITH`, `VALUES`,
   `TABLE`, `SHOW` or `EXPLAIN`, calling no function that reaches past the transaction (`dblink`,
   server file functions, `lo_import` and `lo_export`, `pg_terminate_backend`, advisory locks, and
   functions that run SQL given to them as text).
2. It runs alone, through PostgreSQL's extended query protocol, which refuses a second statement,
   inside a `READ ONLY` transaction with a statement time limit and a lock time limit.
3. The transaction is always rolled back, and `DISCARD ALL` resets the session, so nothing a
   statement sets up outlives it.

Only the first 1,000 rows are fetched from the database (one more is read, to know whether more
exist), so a query over a large table returns quickly.

## Use a login that can only read

The strongest guard is a login that cannot write. Run this once as an administrator, then put
`mcp_readonly` in the connection URL:

```sql
CREATE ROLE mcp_readonly LOGIN PASSWORD 'choose-a-password';
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE mydb TO mcp_readonly;
GRANT pg_read_all_data TO mcp_readonly;  -- PostgreSQL 14 and later
ALTER ROLE mcp_readonly SET default_transaction_read_only = on;
```

To see what a login can do:

```sh
npx -y @kaiva/postgres-mcp postgresql://mcp_readonly:...@localhost/mydb --check
```

## Options

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-rows <n>` | 1000 | Rows returned per query, 1 to 10000 |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | 15 | Time limit per statement, 1 to 300 |
| `--allow-superuser` | off | Allow a superuser login on a database on another machine. In Docker Compose the database is another container, so this applies there too; a read-only login is the better answer |
| `--check` | | Connect once, report what the login can do, and exit |

Give the connection URL as the first argument, or set `DATABASE_URL`. TLS settings go in the URL
(`sslmode`, `sslrootcert`), as with `psql`.

## What it does not protect

- Anything the login can read, the AI can read: tables, views and foreign tables, and with a
  superuser the system catalogs too (`pg_authid` holds password hashes). Use a login that sees only
  the tables you mean to share.
- The refused-function list is a second guard, not a sandbox. It sees the SQL the AI sends, not what
  a view, a foreign table (`file_fdw`) or a function already defined in your database does when it
  is read. With a superuser login such an object can still read a file on the database server. With
  a login that can only read, PostgreSQL itself refuses (checked: a view over `pg_read_file` reads
  the file as a superuser and is refused as a read-only login).

readme.markdown:
# Korely Memory

Memory for AI agents that knows what is still true.

Korely stores what your agent learns as **typed facts with a validity window**. When something changes, the old fact is superseded instead of overwritten. Your agent reads the current truth, and you can still ask what was true on any past date.

```python
import time
from korely_memory import Korely

korely = Korely()  # reads KORELY_API_KEY from the environment

korely.add("Maria is on the Pro plan, billed yearly.", user_id="maria")
korely.add("Maria downgraded to Free.", user_id="maria")

time.sleep(10)  # facts are extracted server-side; see "Writes settle asynchronously"

ctx = korely.get_context(query="what plan is Maria on?", user_id="maria")
print(ctx.context)
# ## Known facts
# - Maria downgraded_to Free (since 2026-09-08)
# - Maria billing_frequency yearly (since 2026-09-08)
#
# Pro is gone from the current facts. It was superseded, not deleted.
```

The exact predicate is chosen by the extractor, so `downgraded_to` here might be
`subscribes_to` or `plan` on your run. What is guaranteed is the behaviour: the
old value leaves the current set, and stays retrievable with its `invalid_at`.

Nothing was deleted. The Pro fact is still there, carrying `invalid_at` and a pointer to what replaced it:

```python
korely.get_facts(user_id="maria", include_invalidated=True)
# Maria downgraded_to Free    valid_from=... invalid_at=None
# Maria plan Pro              valid_from=... invalid_at=2026-09-08T08:31:09Z
```

## Time travel over real dates

Pass `timestamp` when the event happened in the past, and facts inherit it as
`valid_from`. Then `as_of` answers over the world's timeline, not your ingestion
order:

```python
korely.add("Franco signed up on the Pro plan.", user_id="franco", timestamp="2026-01-15")
korely.add("Franco downgraded to Free.",        user_id="franco", timestamp="2026-06-20")

korely.get_facts(user_id="franco", as_of="2026-03-01")   # subscribes_to -> Pro plan
korely.get_facts(user_id="franco", as_of="2026-08-01")   # subscribes_to -> Free
korely.get_facts(user_id="franco")                       # subscribes_to -> Free
```

Without `timestamp` every fact starts being true the moment you write it, so
`as_of` on an earlier date returns nothing. That is correct, and usually not
what you want when you are importing history.

`as_of` answers what was true on a date, as the store knows it today.
`known_as_of` (Korely Agent 0.1.26) answers the other question: what the store
knew on that date. They differ when a change is told late. An agent learns on
5 October that a customer moved on 1 September:

```python
korely.get_facts(user_id="maria", as_of="2026-09-20")        # lives_in -> Turin
korely.get_facts(user_id="maria", known_as_of="2026-09-20")  # lives_in -> Milan
```

On 20 September the move had happened, and the store did not know it yet.
`known_as_of` is on `get_facts`, `get_profile` and `get_context`, which rebuilds
the block as the store could have built it then: what an agent could have
known when it decided. Each fact carries `closed_known_at`, when the store
learned it had ended.

## Writes settle asynchronously

`add()` returns as soon as the memory is stored, then extraction runs server-side. That means:

| Call | Available |
|---|---|
| `search()` over raw memories | immediately |
| `get_facts()` and `get_context()` typed facts | after a few seconds |

The `time.sleep(10)` above exists only so the snippet works when you paste it. **You do not need it in production**: an agent writes at the end of one turn and reads at the start of the next, and by then the facts are there.

If you do need to know exactly when, ask instead of guessing. Every memory carries a `status` of `processing`, `ready`, or `error`, and `events()` reports what is still in flight:

```python
page = korely.events()
page.processing  # 0
page.events[0]   # MemoryEvent(memory_id='mem_...', status='ready', ...)
```

`processing == 0` means none of your project's writes (in the `user_id` scope, if you pass one) is still being extracted, however many there are, so a script can wait on that one number instead of walking every id. After a `batch()` import, wait for `batch_status()` to finish first: memories the job has not stored yet are not counted.

Polling is the only signal: no webhook fires when extraction finishes. The webhook events are `memory.created`, `fact.invalidated` and `quota.warning`.

## Install

```bash
pip install korely-memory      # Python, plus the `korely` CLI
npm install korely-memory      # Node / TypeScript
```

Both clients have **zero runtime dependencies**.

For LangGraph, the optional `pip install 'korely-memory[langgraph]'` adds a store, memory tools and a context helper: see [python/README.md](python/README.md#langgraph).

## Get a key

The hobby tier is free and needs no signup form:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.korely.ai/v1/agents/init \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent_caller": "your-name-here"}'
```

The response carries a `kor_live_` key. Set it as `KORELY_API_KEY` and the SDK, the CLI, and the REST API all authenticate with it. From code, `Korely.init_agent()` (Python) and `Korely.initAgent()` (JS) make the same call.

The account behind that key has no login: the key is the account. Keep it, because it is also the only way to delete the account (`korely delete-account --yes`, or `delete_account(confirm=True)` in the SDK).

Or let the CLI do it for you. `korely init` saves the key to `~/.korely/config.json`, and the SDK reads it from there when `KORELY_API_KEY` is not set, so this is enough to get going:

```bash
pip install korely-memory
korely init --agent --agent-caller your-name
python -c "from korely_memory import Korely; print(Korely().get_context(query='hi').tokens)"
```

## TypeScript

```ts
import { Korely } from "korely-memory";

const korely = new Korely();

await korely.add("Maria downgraded to Free.", { user_id: "maria" });
const ctx = await korely.getContext

readme.markdown:
# lithtrix-mcp

MCP server for [Lithtrix](https://lithtrix.ai) — the **identity, memory, and trust harness for AI agents**. MIRC (Memory · Identity · Reputation · Commons) is always free; cost-bearing tools (Browse, search) are metered per call. Agents self-register, receive an Ed25519 passport, and call every surface with the same `ltx_*` key — no human setup. Ships **`lithtrix.claude.md`** for Claude / Cursor project context (same repo path as this package).

Aligned with API discovery **`version` `4.4.0`** (`GET https://api.lithtrix.ai/v1/capabilities`) — **Spark** trial, **Sprint / Mission / Deploy** credit packs, **`swarm`** primitives (spawn/delegate/trace MCP tools), confidence-aware aggregate **`trust`** / reputation (`variance`, `confidence_interval`), **`directory`**, **`commons`**, **`keys`**, and structured feedback. **Package version `0.20.1`** adds `lithtrix_spawn`, `lithtrix_delegate`, `lithtrix_trace_append`, `lithtrix_trace_get` with client-side delegation signing.

**MCP tool JSON:** canonical **`GET https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/v1/lithtrix-*.json`**. Legacy **`GET https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/lithtrix-*.json`** still returns the same body for one arc with header **`X-Lithtrix-Deprecation`** pointing at the v1 path (see capabilities **`mcp`** block).

## 1. Installation

```bash
npx -y lithtrix-mcp
```

Or for global install:

```bash
npm install -g lithtrix-mcp
```

## 2. Claude Desktop Configuration

Add to `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lithtrix": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "lithtrix-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "LITHTRIX_API_KEY": "ltx_your_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## 3. Getting an API Key

Use the `lithtrix_register` tool first — no API key needed. Or call the API directly:

```bash
curl -X POST https://lithtrix.ai/v1/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"agent_name": "my-agent", "owner_identifier": "you@example.com", "agree_to_terms": true}'
```

Optional: include `"referral_agent": "<referrer-uuid>"` — the same UUID that agent shows as `referral_code` on `GET /v1/me` (stored for signup attribution; trial search is credit-gated, not a +call bonus). New agents get **$5 in trial credits** (no card).

The returned `api_key` is shown once. Store it securely.

## 4. Tools Exposed

- **`lithtrix_search`** — web search with credibility scoring. Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`. Responses include `_lithtrix.search_id` for correlating `lithtrix_feedback`.
- **`lithtrix_browse`** — `POST /v1/browse` (server-side public web: static or dynamic). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`. *Pay to be fully autonomous* — see [`GET /mcp/v1/lithtrix-browse.json`](https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/v1/lithtrix-browse.json).
- **`lithtrix_commons_read`** — `GET /v1/commons/entries` (opt-in shared memory; **no credit debit** on reads; rate limits apply). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`. Schema: [`GET /mcp/v1/lithtrix-commons-read.json`](https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/v1/lithtrix-commons-read.json).
- **`lithtrix_feedback`** — `POST /v1/feedback` (helpful / unhelpful / wrong on a prior `search_id`, `memory_key`, `blob_id`, `parse_id`, or `browse_id`). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`. Optional `note` (≤500 chars); do not send secrets or PII.
- **`lithtrix_register`** — register a new agent and get an API key. No auth required. **`agree_to_terms` must be `true`** (Gentle-Agent Agreement). **$5 trial credits** on signup (no card). Optional `referral_agent` (referrer UUID).
- **`lithtrix_memory_set`** — `PUT /v1/memory/{key}`. Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_memory_get`** — `GET /v1/memory/{key}`. Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_memory_search`** — `GET /v1/memory/search` (semantic). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY` and server-side vector + embedding config.
- **`lithtrix_memory_context`** — `GET /v1/memory/context` (importance + recency). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_upload`** — `PUT /v1/blobs` with raw bytes decoded from base64 (`content_base64`) and `Content-Type` from `content_type`. Optional `filename` query. Use direct HTTP for very large files. Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_download`** — `GET /v1/blobs/{blob_id}`; tool result is JSON with `content_base64`, `content_type`, `size_bytes`. Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_list`** — `GET /v1/blobs` (optional `page`, `per_page`). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_meta`** — `GET /v1/blobs/{blob_id}/meta`. Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_delete`** — `DELETE /v1/blobs/{blob_id}` (soft-delete). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_signed_url`** — `GET /v1/blobs/{blob_id}/signed-url` — short-lived HTTPS link for direct storage GET (optional `expires_in` seconds). Requires `LITHTRIX_API_KEY`. Treat URLs as read tokens.
- **`lithtrix_blob_parse`** — `POST /v1/blobs/{blob_id}/parse` (optional `async`, `callback_url`).
- **`lithtrix_blob_parse_status`** — `GET /v1/blobs/{blob_id}/parse/{parse_id}`.
- **`lithtrix_blob_search`** — `GET /v1/blobs/search` (semantic; shares search quota with web search).
- **`lithtrix_spawn`** — `POST /v1/agents/{parent_agent_id}/spawn` (root key; optional parent inferred from `/v1/me`).
- **`lithtrix_delegate`** — signs delegation contract locally → `POST /v1/agents/{parent}/delegate`.
- **`lithtrix_trace_append`** — `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/trace/events`.
- **`lithtrix_trace_get`** — `GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}/trace`.

**Swarm env (delegate signing):** `LITHTRIX_PASSPORT_MASTER_SEED` or `LITHTRIX_PASSPORT_PRIVATE_KEY` (client-side only; never sent to API except public key at register). (no auth, canonical v1 paths): `GET https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/v1/lithtrix-browse.json`, `GET https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/v1/lithtrix-commons-read.json`, `GET https://lithtrix.ai/mcp/v1/lithtrix-blob-upload.json` (and `-download`, `-list`, `-meta`, `-delete`, `-signed-url`, `lithtrix-blob-parse.json`, `lithtrix-blob-parse-status.json`, `lithtrix-blob-search.json`, passp

Official Luw.ai MCP server AI interior, exterior and landscape design, photoreal rendering, image editing, video and 3D, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Codex and any other MCP client.         --- ```text You: Redesign ~/Desktop/living-room.jpg in Japandi style, give me 2 options. Claude: ⟶ luw_interior_design ✓ 2 designs in 21s [shows both images] You: Love the first one. Make the sofa green velvet, then turn it into a fly-through video. Claude: ⟶ luw_edit_image ⟶ luw_generate_video ✓ ``` ## Quick start **Add `https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp` to your client and sign in to Luw.ai.** Nothing to install, no key to copy: signing in creates one for you. New accounts get free credits. To disconnect, delete that key on the [API page](https://app.luw.ai/dashboard/api).
Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, mobile) *Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector*, paste `https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp`, then **Connect** and sign in to Luw.ai.
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http luw https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp --scope user ``` Then type `/mcp`, pick **luw** and sign in.
ChatGPT Open [Luw.ai in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac8d1bd0f908191a97db90c129430f6), add it and sign in to Luw.ai. The [Luw Studio tools](#luw-studio-edit-your-3d-projects) aren't in ChatGPT's directory yet; add them yourself: *Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings*, turn on **Developer mode**, then **Create**: URL `https://mcp.luw.ai/studio`, authentication **OAuth**, and sign in.
Cursor Click **Add to Cursor** above, or add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "luw": { "url": "https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp" } } } ``` Cursor shows **Needs login** next to luw; click it to sign in.
VS Code (Copilot) Click **Install in VS Code** above, or add to `.vscode/mcp.json`: ```json { "servers": { "luw": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp" } } } ``` VS Code asks you to sign in the first time a tool runs.
Any other client with remote MCP support | | | |---|---| | URL | `https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp` | | Transport | Streamable HTTP | | Auth | Sign in (MCP OAuth), or header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_LUW_API_KEY` | For a client that can't sign in, create a key at [app.luw.ai/dashboard/api](https://app.luw.ai/dashboard/api) and send it as a header: ```json { "mcpServers": { "luw": { "url": "https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_LUW_API_KEY" } } } } ``` If it can neither sign in nor send headers, use `https://mcp.luw.ai/mcp?api_key=YOUR_LUW_API_KEY`. Anyone who has that URL can spend your credits, so keep it private.
The hosted server is stateless and stores nothing; your key goes straight to the Luw.ai API on each request. It can't read files from your computer, so give it image URLs, or use the local setup below. ### Local: work with files on your computer The local server runs on your machine with `npx`, so it can read paths like `~/Desktop/room.jpg`. It needs [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18+ and an API key from [app.luw.ai/dashboard/api](https://app.luw.ai/dashboard/api).
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add luw --scope user --env LUW_API_KEY=YOUR_LUW_API_KEY -- npx -y @luw-ai/mcp ``` Or install it as a plugin. Claude Code asks for your key and keeps it in secure storage: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add Luvi-io/luw-mcp claude plugin install luw@luw-ai ```
Claude Desktop **One click:** download [**luw.mcpb**](https://github.com/Luvi-io/luw-mcp/releases/latest/download/luw.mcpb), double-click it, paste your API key. No Node.js needed. Your agents forget between conversations. Synap makes them remember. Docs · Quickstart · Benchmark results · Evals (reproduce our numbers) · Discussions · Dashboard --- ## The memory layer for production AI agents Synap gives your agents memory that lasts across conversations, sessions and devices. It scores **95.6% on LongMemEval and 93.2% on LoCoMo** ([every LongMemEval answer is published](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output), [reproduce with our open harness](https://github.com/maximem-ai/memory_and_context_eval_harness)), fetches context in ~15ms P50 (internal measurement) before your agent asks, and ships native packages for 24 agent frameworks. LangChain · LangGraph · LlamaIndex · CrewAI · AutoGen · Haystack · Google ADK · OpenAI Agents · Semantic Kernel · Pydantic AI · Agno · LiveKit · Pipecat · Claude Agent · Mastra · Vercel AI SDK · NeMo Agent Toolkit · Microsoft Agent Framework ### What's open, what's hosted | | This repo (Apache 2.0) | Synap Cloud (managed) | |---|---|---| | Python + JS SDKs, 24 framework packages, MCP adapter | ✅ open source | uses them | | Memory engine: ingestion, entity resolution, retrieval, anticipation | — | ✅ runs here | | What you need | `pip install maximem-synap` | an [API key](https://www.maximem.ai/synap). Free Trial plan: 12,500 credits/month, 1 agent, no card required ([pricing](https://www.maximem.ai/synap/pricing)) | Every plan, including the free one, gets every Synap capability. Plans differ on volume and support, not features. --- ## Benchmarks Synap's scores on the two standard long-term memory benchmarks, produced with our open-source harness on the official dataset releases. | Benchmark | Synap accuracy | Scope | Answer model / judge | |---|---|---|---| | **LongMemEval**, all 500 questions ([results](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output/blob/main/RESULTS.md#longmemeval-overall-956)) | **95.6%** (478 / 500) | Full set, 6 categories | `gemini-3.8-flash` / `gpt-4o` | | **LongMemEval**, answerable questions ([results](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output/blob/main/RESULTS.md#longmemeval-answerable-questions-957)) | 95.7% (450 / 470) | 30 abstention questions excluded | `gemini-3.8-flash` / `gpt-4o` | | **LongMemEval retrieval**, Recall@20 ([results](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output/blob/main/RESULTS.md#longmemeval-retrieval-recall20-981)) | **98.1%** (461 / 470) | Abstention excluded | none / `gpt-4o` | | **LoCoMo** ([results](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output/blob/main/RESULTS.md#locomo-overall-932-cat-1-4-adversarial-excluded)) | **93.2%** | Cat 1–4, adversarial excluded | `gpt-5-mini` / `gpt-5-mini` | The LongMemEval run is from October 2026 and the LoCoMo run from 2026-06-20. For LongMemEval, the retrieved memories, answer and judge verdict for every one of the 500 questions are published, so you can recompute the score. Other vendors publish their own numbers under different answer models and judges. Our harness ships adapters for Mem0, Zep and Supermemory, so you can run them side by side yourself. [How scores differ across setups →](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output/blob/main/METHODOLOGY.md) Category breakdown, methodology and every scope decision → [eval_benchmark_runs_output](https://github.com/maximem-ai/eval_benchmark_runs_output) --- ## Install ```bash # Python pip install maximem-synap # JavaScript / TypeScript npm install @maximem/synap-js-sdk ``` ### Using a coding agent? Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor: > Add Synap memory to this project. Run `pip install maximem-synap` (or `npm i @maximem/synap-js-sdk`), then install the Synap skill (`npx skills add maximem-ai/maximem_synap_sdk --skill synap -y`, or https://github.com/maximem-ai/maximem_synap_sdk/tree/main/skills/synap) and follow it to wire memory into the agent framework this repo uses. If I have a one-time code, use it. If I already have an instance and a key in `.env`, use those. Never ask me to paste a key into the chat.
Claude Code ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/maximem-ai/maximem_synap_sdk /tmp/synap && cp -r /tmp/synap/skills/synap ~/.claude/skills/synap ```
Codex ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/maximem-ai/maximem_synap_sdk /tmp/synap && mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r /tmp/synap/skills/synap-codex ~/.agents/skills/synap ```
Cursor / any MCP client Add the Synap MCP server URL and your API key from the [dashboard](https://synap.maximem.ai). See [`packages/mcps/synap-mcp-server/`](packages/mcps/synap-mcp-server/).
