readme.markdown:
# ai-netcafe

Hosted tools your agent can call over MCP — and a claim you can check in one command:

```bash
curl "https://ainetcafe.com/t/china_reachability?url=https://github.com"
```

```json
{
  "url": "https://github.com",
  "tested_from": "mainland China (China Mobile backbone)",
  "verdict": "unreachable: timeout (common signature of blocking or a very slow route)"
}
```

That request was answered by a machine actually sitting on a Chinese backbone network. A monitor
hosted anywhere else can only tell you GitHub is up *where it is* — which is not the question you
were asking. That is the kind of thing we host: capabilities that are hard to get, rather than
wrappers around ones that aren't.

## Four focused servers

One agent profile rarely needs both spreadsheet cleanup and the Chinese lunar calendar, and every
tool description costs tokens on every session. So the catalogue is served as four focused MCP
endpoints — connect the one you need and pay the context cost of nothing else.

| Pack | URL | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Tables** | `https://ainetcafe.com/mcp/table` | Messy CSV in, clean checkable table out. Dedupe, merge, transpose, wide→long, find what differs between two tables, reconcile two ledgers. |
| **Dev kit** | `https://ainetcafe.com/mcp/dev` | JSON↔YAML, validate JSON, line diff, regex test, JWT decode, SQL dialect transpile, timezone and unit conversion. |
| **Doc flow** | `https://ainetcafe.com/mcp/paper` | Markdown → PDF / Word / PowerPoint / EPUB / HTML. PDFs merged, split, rotated, watermarked. |
| **China facts** | `https://ainetcafe.com/mcp/cn` | Mainland reachability from a real backbone, statutory holidays **including make-up workdays (调休)**, offline ID and mobile validation, lunar calendar. |

All four are in the [official MCP registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as
`com.ainetcafe/netcafe-tables`, `-devkit`, `-docflow` and `-china`.

**Nothing in these four calls a language model or a third-party API.** They compute on our own
servers, so results are deterministic and repeatable — and they cannot break because someone else
changed their API.

## Numbers come with their own proof

Anything involving counts or money returns an arithmetic check computed in code, not asserted by a
model:

```jsonc
// reconcile_ledger: your books vs the bank statement
{
  "total_a": 105.30, "total_b": 106.80, "gap": -1.50,
  "only_in_a":  [{ "key": "B",  "amount": 5.00 }],
  "only_in_b":  [{ "key": "C",  "amount": 7.00 }],
  "mismatched": [{ "key": "A3", "a": 100.00, "b": 99.50, "diff": 0.50 }],
  "arithmetic_check": {
    "formula": "A 105.3 − B 106.8 = -1.5; differences explain -1.5",
    "checks_out": true
  }
}
```

If `checks_out` is false, the response says the result is untrustworthy instead of handing back a
table that looks finished. Amounts are compared in integer cents, so `0.1 + 0.2` never invents a
difference for someone to go chase.

## Connect it

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http netcafe-tables https://ainetcafe.com/mcp/table
```

DeepSeek Harness:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mario03690/dsh-netcafe
```

Everything is also a plain GET — no MCP client, no SDK, no key:

```bash
curl "https://ainetcafe.com/t/cn_holiday?date=2026-10-01"
curl "https://ainetcafe.com/t/diff_text?a=one%0Atwo&b=one%0Athree"
```

Charts come back as images you can paste straight into a README:

That image is rendered on request, right now, by the same service this page describes.

## Model cost is measured, not quoted

```bash
npx ai-netcafe compare "dedupe a JS array preserving order"
```

```
MODEL              COST       LATENCY
deepseek-v4-flash  $0.00012    7.6s
gemini-3.5-flash   $0.000341   10.0s
GLM5.2             $0.001828   9.0s

cheapest: deepseek-v4-flash   fastest: deepseek-v4-flash
15.2× between cheapest and priciest
```

Every number is read from the upstream `usage` response, not derived from a published price list.
That distinction matters more than it sounds — while building this we found the obvious conversion
formula was wrong for several models (one off by ~9×, another by ~3×), and only billing-delta
measurement matched reality.
[Full method and data.](https://ainetcafe.com/lab/llm-real-cost-comparison?s=github)

## Heavier skills

The main endpoint (`https://ainetcafe.com/mcp`) also carries tools that do call a model, and say so:

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `extract_invoices` | A batch of invoices → one ledger-ready table. Every row checked in code (net + tax = gross); the batch total re-added independently. Mixed currencies get no batch total on purpose — adding them would be an accounting error. |
| `extract_statement` | Bank statement PDF → transactions, with reconciliation (opening + credits − debits = closing). If it doesn't balance it says where the running total first breaks. |
| `transpile_sql` | SQL between dialects via a real parser, not a model — same input, same output, and syntax errors come back with line and column. |
| `check_resume` | Whether an ATS can actually parse a résumé. Rule-based and reproducible. |
| `remember` / `recall` | Cross-session memory, keyed to your AllRouter key or an anonymous workspace token. |
| `create_task` | Hand a recurring job to a hosted runner; it notifies you only when the result actually changes. |

Full catalogue: <https://ainetcafe.com/tools?s=github>

Backed by open-source projects — PDFMathTranslate, GPT Academic, GPT Researcher, NextChat, LobeChat
— hosted pre-configured so you can try them without installing Docker, Python, or supplying a key.

## CLI

```bash
npx ai-netcafe compare "<prompt>"   # multi-model comparison with real costs
npx ai-netcafe ask "<prompt>"       # single model
npx ai-netcafe apps                 # hosted apps + source repos
npx ai-netcafe models               # models with per-million prices
npx ai-netcafe install              # MCP config for your agent
```

## Quota

Anonymous calls get a free allowance — enough to try everything here,

…

readme.markdown:
# Free Public REST APIs - AI SENSE AS

No API key | No sign-up | No cost

Provided by **[AI SENSE AS](https://aisenseapi.com)** (Oslo, Norway).
Full endpoint reference: [`API.md`](API.md) | Repo: [github.com/aisenseapi/aisense-free-public-rest-apis](https://github.com/aisenseapi/aisense-free-public-rest-apis)

**Base URL:** `https://aisenseapi.com/services/v1/`

## Free public MCP endpoints

The AI SENSE MCP server is at:

`https://aisenseapi.com/mcp`

The AI SENSE MCP server covers Heartbeat, Lease, Agent Wake tasks, Agent
Inbox, human approval, webhook capture, temporary storage, URL shortening,
time and UUIDs. It needs no account or API key. Heartbeat uses
`create_heartbeat`, `read_heartbeat` and `ping_heartbeat`. Lease uses
`create_lease_namespace`, `acquire_lease`, `renew_lease`, `release_lease` and
`complete_lease`. Agent Inbox uses `create_agent_inbox` and
`read_agent_inbox`. See
[`MCP.md`](MCP.md) for the tool list, data boundary and client examples.

The Agent Queue tools use separate read, write and worker tokens issued at
creation. The semantic search tools use a read token and a write token in
the same way.

Start with [AGENT-GUIDE.md](AGENT-GUIDE.md) to choose tools, then
[AGENT-QUICKSTART.md](AGENT-QUICKSTART.md) for a complete Queue workflow and
retry decisions. [examples/comfyui](examples/comfyui/README.md) runs image jobs through
ComfyUI from several machines on Agent Queue, Storage and Webhook capture,
with a fake renderer so the flow runs without ComfyUI.

The server reports version `1.26.1` and offers 87 tools: the workflow tools
and the REST utility endpoints below as tools, apart from AIQ, `ip_datetime`
and `ping`, which stay on REST. The official MCP Registry lists
`com.aisenseapi/free-public-tools` version `1.26.1` as active and latest,
published 11 November 2026 at 09:34 UTC.

aamio has its own MCP endpoint at `https://aamio.at/mcp`, eleven tools for
ephemeral agent rendezvous: a thread with a secret read key and a public write
address, a receipt of hashes that outlives it, presence, and the open board of
needs and offers at `https://board.aamio.at/`. No account and no API key. The
official MCP registry lists it as `at.aamio/aamio`. The AI SENSE endpoint does
not proxy these tools either.

Verifyum has its own dedicated MCP endpoint at
`https://api.verifyum.com/mcp`. It exposes the three Verifyum proof operations
without an account or API key. File hashing still happens on the agent's
machine. The browser flow, public HTTP API and published protocol remain
available. The official MCP registry lists it as `com.verifyum/mcp` version
`0.1.0`. Finalized proofs also join hourly and daily Merkle checkpoints in
the [Verifyum Witness Layer](https://verifyum.com/witness). Nine records
surround each finalized proof.

| Tier | Records |
| --- | --- |
| Primary evidence | One finalized Solana Mainnet Memo transaction per proof |
| Independent corroboration | Hourly OpenTimestamps on Bitcoin, daily qualified EU timestamp, daily witness-cosigned Sigsum and daily Certificate Transparency certificate |
| Operator records and availability redundancy | Verifyum Ed25519 signature, GitHub checkpoint log, Software Heritage and Internet Archive |

The Solana transaction is the primary evidence. Deep Solana history generally
requires an archival provider. Glasklar, Mullvad and Tillitis cosign the
Sigsum digest with a quorum of two out of three. The qualified timestamp uses
RFC 3161. Its eIDAS Article 41(2) presumption covers the daily checkpoint root
alone. A Verifyum user proof is not a qualified electronic timestamp. Verifyum
is not a qualified trust service. Software Heritage and Internet Archive show
what was stored. They do not establish when the original file existed. The
number of channels is not a quality score.

Every finalized proof is also announced on
[Telegram](https://t.me/verifyum) and in the
[Atom feed](https://verifyum.com/feed.xml). These are announcement channels.
They are excluded from the nine evidence records. Their timestamps date the
announcement. They say nothing about the original file date.

An agent can also assemble one decision record locally from its instructions,
prompt, model, parameters, tool calls and output, then anchor only the
commitment. The proof shows that the exact record existed unchanged by the
block time. It does not prove that the model actually ran with the recorded
settings.

---

## Free public Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoint

Agents that speak Agent2Agent can reach five of these capabilities at:

`https://aisenseapi.com/a2a`

JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol revision 1.0, no account and no API key. The agent card
is a plain GET at `https://aisenseapi.com/.well-known/agent-card.json`.

A2A is the protocol for delegating work to another agent. MCP is the protocol
for exposing tools. Most of this service is tools, so only the five task-shaped
capabilities are offered over A2A: `agent-wake`, `human-approval`,
`agent-inbox`, `webhook-capture` and `agent-queue`. The other tools are not
reachable through it. MCP stays the richer workflow surface with its own tool
schemas. Over A2A the queue skill creates a queue and returns its three role
tokens; enqueueing, claiming and acknowledging stay on REST and MCP.

A2A puts no skill id on the wire, so the caller names the skill in a data part
of the message, as `{"skill": "agent-wake", "arguments": { ... }}`. That is a
convention this service documents, not a field the protocol defines, and a
message without it is refused. The card declares `streaming` and
`pushNotifications` false, so those methods answer `-32004` and `-32003`.
`ListTasks` returns an empty page, because nobody is authenticated and a task ID
is the only credential there is. See [`API.md`](API.md#agent2agent-a2a) for the
skills, task states, response shapes and error codes.

---

readme.markdown:
# 앱박스 AI 플러그인

앱박스(AppBox) 원격 MCP 서버를 Claude Code · Codex 에 연결하는 플러그인과, 그 플러그인을 담은 마켓플레이스 저장소입니다.
연결은 **앱박스 계정 로그인(OAuth)** 으로 하며, 토큰을 직접 다루지 않습니다.

> 사용자용 안내(Claude · Claude Code · Codex · Cursor 연결, 연결 화면 읽는 법, 문제 해결)는 **[앱박스 가이드 › AI 연결(MCP)](https://www.appboxapp.com/guide/setup/AI%20%EC%97%B0%EA%B2%B0%20%EC%8B%9C%EC%9E%91%ED%95%98%EA%B8%B0)** 에 있습니다. 이 README 는 설치 명령과 저장소 구성 중심입니다.

## 구성

```
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json            Claude 마켓플레이스 매니페스트 (이름: appbox-ai)
.agents/plugins/marketplace.json           Codex 마켓플레이스 매니페스트 (이름: appbox-ai)
plugins/appbox/.claude-plugin/plugin.json  Claude 플러그인 매니페스트 (이름: appbox)
plugins/appbox/.codex-plugin/plugin.json   Codex 플러그인 매니페스트 (표시 이름·설명·카테고리 포함)
plugins/appbox/.mcp.json                    원격 MCP 서버 설정 (Streamable HTTP, 주소만 — 토큰 없음)
plugins/appbox/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md   스킬: 시작 안내 — 지금 상태 진단 → 다음 한 단계
plugins/appbox/skills/setup-fcm/SKILL.md    스킬: FCM 발급·등록 단계 안내 (키 파일은 다루지 않음)
plugins/appbox/skills/check-setup/SKILL.md  스킬: 푸시 연동 점검 절차
plugins/appbox/skills/weekly-report/SKILL.md    스킬: 주간 성과 보고(운영 현황 조회 권한)
plugins/appbox/skills/campaign-review/SKILL.md  스킬: 캠페인 회고(운영 현황 조회 권한)
plugins/appbox/skills/credit-forecast/SKILL.md  스킬: 크레딧 소진 예측(운영 현황 조회 권한)
plugins/appbox/assets/                      아이콘(로고 · 작은 아이콘) — Codex 목록 표시용
```

- 서버: `https://mcp.appboxapp.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, POST 전용)
- 인증: **OAuth** — 처음 쓸 때 Claude Code 가 브라우저로 앱박스 로그인·허용 화면을 연다. 토큰은 Claude Code 가 받아 보관하고 자동으로 갱신한다(사용자는 토큰을 보지 않는다)
- 조회 도구: `appbox_get_onboarding_status` · `appbox_list_apps` · `appbox_check_app_setup` · `appbox_get_build_status`
- 운영 현황 조회 도구(연결할 때 받은 경우): `appbox_list_push_campaigns`, `appbox_get_push_campaign`, `appbox_get_dashboard`, `appbox_get_best_send_time`, `appbox_get_inapp_performance`, `appbox_get_billing`, `appbox_list_audiences`
- 추가 권한 도구(연결할 때 켠 경우만): `appbox_create_app` · `appbox_set_tester` · `appbox_send_test_push` · `appbox_send_test_inapp` · `appbox_list_inapp_campaigns` · `appbox_get_delivery_result` · `appbox_create_event_type` · `appbox_create_topic` · `appbox_create_segment` · `appbox_create_support_contact`
- 기기 도구: `appbox_find_device`(조회)
- 문서 도구(로그인 연결에 기본 포함, 서버에서 켜진 경우): `appbox_get_overview` · `appbox_search_docs` · `appbox_get_doc`(가이드) · `appbox_list_examples` · `appbox_get_example`(공개 샘플 소스) · `appbox_get_api_spec`(서버 API 명세)
- 이 저장소에는 **매니페스트와 스킬만** 둡니다. 서버 코드·자격 증명은 넣지 않습니다.

## 1. 설치

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add MobilePartnersCo/appbox-ai   # 마켓플레이스 등록 (이름: appbox-ai)
claude plugin install appbox@appbox-ai                   # 플러그인 설치
claude plugin list                                       # appbox@appbox-ai 가 enabled 인지 확인
```

- 업데이트를 자동으로 받으려면 Claude Code 의 `/plugin` → 마켓플레이스 `appbox-ai` 에서 자동 업데이트를 켭니다(서드파티 마켓플레이스는 기본 꺼짐).
- 이 저장소를 내려받은 위치에서 `claude plugin marketplace add ./` 로 로컬 등록할 수도 있습니다. 플러그인만 잠깐 써 보려면 `claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/appbox`.

제거: `claude plugin marketplace remove appbox-ai` (마켓플레이스와 그 플러그인을 함께 제거)

## 2. 연결 (앱박스 로그인)

1. Claude Code 세션에서 `/mcp` → `plugin:appbox:appbox` 서버를 고르고 **Authenticate**.
2. 브라우저에 앱박스 콘솔이 열리면 로그인합니다(이미 로그인돼 있으면 건너뜀).
3. 허용 화면에서 권한·**허용할 앱**(전체 또는 선택)을 확인하고, 외부 AI 전송 고지에 동의한 뒤 **허용**.
   - 앱 이름 아래 신원 표시를 확인하세요 — 「claude.ai 에서 확인된 앱」 · 「앱박스에 등록된 앱」 · 「확인되지 않은 앱」. 「확인되지 않은 앱」 인데 직접 시작한 연결이 아니라면 거부하세요.
4. 브라우저에 완료가 뜨면 Claude Code 로 돌아옵니다. `/mcp` 에서 connected 로 바뀝니다.

이후 스킬을 씁니다.

| 이럴 때 | 스킬 |
|---|---|
| "앱박스로 푸시 보내고 싶어요", "뭐부터 해야 하나요" | `/appbox:onboarding [앱 코드]` |
| "FCM 등록 어떻게 해요" | `/appbox:setup-fcm [앱 코드]` |
| "푸시가 안 와요" | `/appbox:check-setup [앱 코드]` |
| "지난주 푸시 성과 정리해 줘" | `/appbox:weekly-report [앱 코드]` |
| "어제 보낸 캠페인 어땠어?" | `/appbox:campaign-review [앱 코드] [캠페인 코드]` |
| "크레딧 언제 떨어져?" | `/appbox:credit-forecast [앱 코드]` |

도구의 전체 이름은 `mcp__plugin_appbox_appbox__appbox_list_apps` 형식입니다(권한 규칙에 쓸 때 이 이름 사용).

- 연결 확인·해제: 앱박스 콘솔 **계정 설정 › MCP 연결**. 해제하면 즉시 끊기고, 다시 쓰려면 2번을 다시 합니다.
- AI 앱에서 앱박스 서버(커넥터)만 삭제하면 앱박스 쪽 연결은 남습니다. 끊으려면 콘솔에서 해제하세요.
- 허용할 앱: 연결할 때 체크한 앱만 볼 수 있습니다('전체 앱'은 그때 목록의 전체 선택). 연결한 뒤 만든 앱을 쓰려면 콘솔 **계정 설정 › MCP 연결**의 「허용 앱 변경」에서 그 앱을 체크하고 저장합니다 — 다시 연결할 필요 없이 다음 요청부터 적용됩니다.
- 비밀번호를 바꾸거나 재설정하면 모든 MCP 연결이 해제됩니다(콘솔 알림으로 알려 줍니다).
- 30일 동안 쓰지 않은 연결은 자동으로 해제됩니다. 다시 쓰려면 다시 로그인합니다.

## 3. 다른 AI 앱에 연결

모두 **주소만** 넣으면 처음 쓸 때 앱박스 로그인이 열립니다. 토큰을 넣지 마세요. 앱별 화면 안내는 [가이드](https://www.appboxapp.com/guide/setup/AI%20%EC%97%B0%EA%B2%B0%20%EC%8B%9C%EC%9E%91%ED%95%98%EA%B8%B0).

| 앱 | 연결 |
|---|---|
| Claude (웹 · 데스크톱 · 모바일) | 설정 › 커넥터 › 탐색에서 **AppBox** → 연결. 보이지 않으면 커스텀 커넥터에 아래 주소 |
| Claude Code (플러그인 없이) | `claude mcp add --transport http appbox https://mcp.appboxapp.com/mcp` → `/mcp` 에서 appbox → Authenticate |
| Codex (플러그인) | `codex plugin marketplace add MobilePartnersCo/appbox-ai` → `codex plugin add appbox@appbox-ai` → `codex mcp login appbox` |
| Codex (플러그인 없이) | `codex mcp add appbox --url https://mcp.appboxapp.com/mcp` |

readme.markdown:
# ASR Memory

[한국어](README.ko.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md)

ASR Memory is shared memory for your AI tools, run as a hosted remote MCP server. Save a decision in one tool and find it, word for word, from another.

This repository holds documentation, agent instructions and examples. The server source is not public.

- Website: https://asrmemory.com
- MCP endpoint: `https://asrmemory.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1)
- Official MCP Registry: `com.asrmemory/asr`

## Connect in three steps

1. Add `https://asrmemory.com/mcp` as a remote MCP server (custom connector) in your AI tool.
2. Sign in when the login page opens (email, Google, Kakao or GitHub). No key to copy.
3. Ask the tool: "Save to ASR: we chose Postgres for billing." Then, in another tool: "What did we decide about billing?"

Tools that cannot open a login page can connect with an API key issued in the dashboard (https://asrmemory.com/app/). Step-by-step guides for each client: https://asrmemory.com/en/docs.html

To see the project dashboard without signing up, open the demo: https://asrmemory.com/madang/?demo

## Tools (22)

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `memory_save` | Save a memory as written, with who saved it and when it happened |
| `memory_search` | Search by meaning and keywords |
| `memory_card` | Show one memory in full |
| `memory_recall_daily` | Recall what happened on a date |
| `wake_up` | Brief a new session on recent work |
| `memory_stats` | Counts by drawer and tool |
| `memory_retag` | Change a memory's drawer |
| `memory_delete` | Move a memory to the trash |
| `memory_trash` | List the trash |
| `memory_restore` | Restore from the trash |
| `memory_purge` | Permanently delete (asks first) |
| `memory_export` | Export your memories as JSON Lines |
| `secret_save` / `secret_get` | Store and read an encrypted value |
| `promise_start` / `promise_list` / `promise_resolve` | Track a goal day by day; only you mark the result |
| `asr_send` | Send a task to another tool |
| `asr_handoff` | Hand off unfinished work when a session ends |
| `asr_inbox` | See and take tasks sent to you |
| `asr_done` | Close a task with its result |
| `asr_tidy` | Save a project status summary |

## Agent instructions

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is a set of rules to paste into `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `GEMINI.md` so long-running agents read memory at the start, save decisions as they go, and hand off work between tools. It also works without ASR. Korean: [AGENTS.ko.md](AGENTS.ko.md), Japanese: [AGENTS.ja.md](AGENTS.ja.md).

For chat apps (claude.ai project instructions, ChatGPT custom instructions), use the short 11-line version: https://asrmemory.com/en/docs.html#guide

## Your data

- Each account has its own memory space. Cross-account access tests run on every deployment, and the deployment stops if any fails.
- Deleted memories go to the trash first and can be restored. Permanent deletion is a separate, explicit step.
- You can export everything with `memory_export` and delete your account from the dashboard.
- Where data goes (database, server, embedding and classification providers): https://asrmemory.com/en/privacy.html
- Do not store passwords, keys or children's conversations as plain memories. Use `secret_save` for sensitive values.

## Price

Free during the beta, up to 1,000 memories per account. Searching, recall and export are not counted. Project summaries saved with `asr_tidy` do not count toward the limit.

## Feedback

Open an issue in this repository, or email idoweddings@naver.com.

## License

Documentation and agent instructions in this repository: CC BY 4.0. Example code in `examples/`: MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

name: Web Browser (kogiQA)

readme.markdown:
## kogiQA MCP Web Browser

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides browser automation capabilities using kogiQA. This server
enables LLMs to interact with web pages through natural language, bypassing the need for screenshots
or visually-tuned models.

### For what to use:
+ Debug style issues on your page
+ Automatically fix console errors.
+ Map and document the functionality of your web app
+ Automatically write end-to-end tests
+ Automate exploratory testing of your application

See example prompts [Usage Examples](#usage-examples)

### kogiQA MCP vs Playwright MCP

The kogiQA MCP Server provides a browser which incorporates the capabilities of the kogiQA browser control algorithm.
This enables agents to interact with pages without a selector, saving time and tokens.

### Installation

Auto install:

```bash
npx kogiqa-mcp@latest
```

#### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add kogiqa-browser npx kogiqa-mcp@latest
```

#### VS Code

Click one of the buttons below to install directly in vs code:

[](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode-insiders%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%7B%22name%22%3A%22kogiqa-browser%22%2C%22command%22%3A%22npx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22kogiqa-mcp%40latest%22%5D%7D) [](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode-insiders%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%7B%22name%22%3A%22kogiqa-browser%22%2C%22command%22%3A%22npx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22kogiqa-mcp%40latest%22%5D%7D)

Alternatively, install via the VS Code CLI:

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"kogiqa-browser","command":"npx","args":["kogiqa-mcp@latest"]}'
```

#### Cursor

[](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=kogiqa-browser&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IGtvZ2lxYS1tY3BAbGF0ZXN0In0=)

Alternatively, go to `Cursor Settings` → `MCP` → `Add new MCP Server` and enter the command
`npx kogiqa-mcp@latest`.

### Standard configuration

For any other MCP client, add the following to your MCP configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kogiqa-browser": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "kogiqa-mcp@latest"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
### Usage Examples
Once the server is configured, simply talk to your agent in natural language. Because kogiQA is selector-free, you describe what you want done — not how to find the elements.

#### Smoke-test a user flow
```text
Open http://localhost:3000, log in with the demo credentials, add the first product to the cart, and verify that the cart badge shows "1".
```
#### Debug a style issue
```text
Go to https://myapp.example.com/pricing and check why the "Pro" plan card overflows its container on a 1280px-wide viewport. Suggest a CSS fix.
```
#### Fix console errors
```text
Navigate to http://localhost:5173, open every page linked from the main menu, collect all console errors, and fix them in the source code.
```
#### Map and document your app
```text
Explore https://staging.example.com, follow all internal links up to two levels deep, and produce a Markdown document describing each page and its main features.
```
#### Generate end-to-end tests
```text
Walk through the sign-up flow at http://localhost:3000/signup and write Cypress end-to-end tests covering the happy path and validation errors.
```
#### Exploratory testing
```text
Do 10 minutes of exploratory testing on http://localhost:8080: try edge-case inputs in every form you find and report anything that looks broken or inconsistent.
```

### Requirements
+ Node.js 20 or newer
+ VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Goose, Junie or a other MCP client

readme.markdown: Atlassian MCP Server The official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Atlassian: a cloud-hosted bridge that gives your AI tools secure, real-time access to Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket, Compass, Loom, and the wider Atlassian platform — powered by your Teamwork Graph. Getting started · Supported tools · Security & admin · Community --- The **official Atlassian MCP Server** is a cloud-based bridge between your Atlassian Cloud site and compatible external tools. Once configured, it enables those tools to interact with **Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket, Compass, Loom, and Atlassian platform data (Projects, Goals, Teams, Focus, Talent, and the Teamwork Graph)** in real time. Authentication uses **OAuth 2.1** or **API tokens**, so every action respects the user's existing access controls. With the Atlassian MCP Server, you can: * **Summarize and search** Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Bitbucket, Projects, Goals, and more without switching tools. * **Retrieve and review** recordings of videos and meetings from Loom. * **Create and update** work items or pages based on natural language commands. * **Automate repetitive work**, like generating work items from meeting notes or specs. Connect once, then describe what you want — no tab switching and no copy-pasting. Your AI selects and runs the right actions. It's built for developers, content creators, and project teams who work in IDEs or AI tools and want to use Atlassian data without constantly switching context. > [!IMPORTANT] > **v2 is now the recommended version.** New setups should use `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`, which exposes more tools and more products. Existing v1 connections automatically start to expose and use v2 tools; incompatible clients may need to clear cached client IDs or `.well-known` credentials to keep authenticating. For setup steps, see [Getting started with the Atlassian MCP Server](https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server/docs/getting-started-with-the-atlassian-remote-mcp-server/). ## One-click setup Pick your AI client below to install the official Atlassian MCP Server. Each button uses your client's native install link, so you don't need to edit any JSON config by hand. Add to Cursor Reference issues and log work in your codebase. Add to VS Code Search and create Jira issues via GitHub Copilot. Add to ChatGPT Search, summarize, and create right from ChatGPT. Add to Claude Bring Jira and Confluence into Claude workflows. ### Let your agent do the setup Most AI coding agents can install, authenticate, and configure the server themselves. Copy and paste this prompt into your agent: ``` Set up Atlassian MCP for this agent using the official setup guide at https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server/docs/getting-started-with-the-atlassian-remote-mcp-server/ and the MCP server URL https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp. Contents * [One-click setup](#one-click-setup) * [Supported clients](#supported-clients) * [Plugin packaging and compatibility](#plugin-packaging-and-compatibility) * [Supported products and tools](#supported-products-and-tools) * [How the server exposes tools](#how-the-server-exposes-tools) * [MCP gateways](#mcp-gateways) * [Before you start](#before-you-start) * [Data and security](#data-and-security) * [How it works](#how-it-works) * [Example workflows](#example-workflows) * [Tips and tricks](#tips-and-tricks) * [Admin notes: managing access](#admin-notes-managing-access) * [Security](#security) * [Support and feedback](#support-and-feedback) * [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) --- ## readme.markdown:
# Autodesk AI Integrations

This repository is where Autodesk releases components that connect Autodesk products and services to AI
assistants and agents, such as [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) servers
and their registry metadata.

Each integration lives in its own folder with its own README, license, and release notes.

## Integrations

| Integration | Type | Folder | Registry name |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autodesk Product Help MCP | Hosted (remote), Streamable HTTP | [`product-help/remote-mcp-server`](./product-help/remote-mcp-server) | `com.autodesk.aps.api/product-help-mcp` |
| Autodesk Fusion MCP | Local, runs on your machine alongside Fusion | [`fusion/local-mcp-server`](./fusion/local-mcp-server) | `com.autodesk.aps.api/fusion-local-mcp` |

- **Product Help** gives AI clients read-only access to Autodesk Help and Support documentation. Autodesk
  hosts the service, so there is nothing to install.
- **Fusion** lets an MCP client create, modify, and inspect geometry in a running Autodesk Fusion session.
  Fusion must be installed and running.

## Repository layout

```text
.
├── product-help/
│   └── remote-mcp-server/   # Product Help MCP: server.json, README, LICENSE
├── fusion/
│   └── local-mcp-server/    # Fusion MCP: server.json, README, LICENSE, bundle
└── README.md
```

New integrations are added as `<product-or-area>/<integration-name>/`.

## Getting started

Open the README in the integration's folder for setup instructions for your MCP client.

## Support

Open an [issue](https://github.com/Autodesk/ai-integrations/issues) for problems with setup, registry
metadata, or documentation. Mention which integration it concerns. For questions about Autodesk products,
visit the [Autodesk Community forums](https://forums.autodesk.com).

To report a security vulnerability, follow the
[Autodesk Vulnerability Disclosure Policy](https://www.autodesk.com/trust/security/vulnerability-disclosure-policy)
and submit your report through [Autodesk on HackerOne](https://hackerone.com/autodesk). Do not open a
public issue for security reports.

## License and terms

Each integration is licensed separately. See the `LICENSE` file in its folder. Use of Autodesk products and
services is subject to the Autodesk
[Terms of Use](https://www.autodesk.com/company/terms-of-use/en/general-terms) and
[Privacy Statement](https://www.autodesk.com/company/legal-notices-trademarks/privacy-statement).

# Autoview MCP

Trade across [22+ exchanges and brokers](https://autoview.com/platforms/) from any MCP-capable AI agent. Autoview's MCP server is a hosted, remote endpoint, no install, no local server to run.

## Endpoint

```
https://api.autoview.com/mcp/
```

## Authentication

Generate a personal access token at [autoview.com/account/tokens/](https://autoview.com/account/tokens/) (Account menu -> MCP tokens). Set a label, an expiry, and the scopes you want, then copy the token when it appears -- it's shown once. Pass it as the `token` argument on every tool call.

## Tools

- **entry** -- place an order (dry-run by default; every call is a preview unless you explicitly set `live: true`)
- **events** -- read back the outcome of an entry call by its trace id

## Live trading coverage

Live (real-money) trading is currently available on Kraken and Crypto.com through the MCP. Every other supported exchange is simulation-only for now (Tradovate, OANDA Practice, Bybit Testnet/Spot Testnet, Crypto.com Demo, and more), so you can wire up an agent and watch it work before pointing it at a funded account.

## Full guide

The complete getting-started guide, including a step-by-step token walkthrough, request/response examples, and the custom-client connection handshake, lives at:

**[autoview.com/guides/mcp-getting-started/](https://autoview.com/guides/mcp-getting-started/)**

## About Autoview

[Autoview](https://autoview.com/) turns any webhook-driven signal (TradingView alerts, custom bots, AI agents) into live, automated execution across 22+ exchanges and brokers.

readme.markdown:
# BillingEngine MCP server

Create customers and invoices, look up open invoices and record payments in
[BillingEngine](https://www.billingengine.com) by talking to Claude, Cursor or any other
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client:

> "Create an invoice for Acme Painting over 100 euros."
>
> "Which invoices are overdue?"
>
> "Acme paid invoice 2610030028, record the payment."

BillingEngine is invoicing software for freelancers and small businesses with
[e-invoicing](https://www.billingengine.com/en/features) (EN 16931, XRechnung, ZUGFeRD / Factur-X).
The server is a thin layer over the [BillingEngine API](https://www.billingengine.com/en/api)
and runs on your computer.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer
- A BillingEngine account on a paid plan. The API is not available in the Free plan.
- Your API key from **Settings > API keys** in BillingEngine

## Setup

### Claude Desktop

Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "billingengine": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "billingengine-mcp"],
      "env": { "BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY": "your-api-key" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add billingengine --env BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY=your-api-key -- npx -y billingengine-mcp
```

### Cursor and other clients

Use the same `command`, `args` and `env` as above in the MCP settings of your client.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `find_customers` | Searches customers by company, name, email or identifier of another system |
| `create_customer` | Creates a customer |
| `update_customer` | Changes a customer |
| `create_invoice` | Creates a **draft** invoice for a customer |
| `update_invoice` | Changes a draft invoice |
| `list_invoices` | Lists invoices, filtered by status, type, customer, number, identifier or date |
| `get_invoice` | Returns one invoice with items, tax breakdown and status |
| `download_invoice` | Saves the PDF or the XML e-invoice to your Downloads folder |
| `record_payment` | Records a payment for sent invoices |
| `list_payments` | Lists payments, optionally for one invoice |

## What it does and does not do

- Invoices are created as **drafts**. Nothing is sent to your customers; you review and send
  the invoice in BillingEngine. Every result contains a link to open the draft.
- Prices are net or gross, as set in your account; every invoice says which. Amounts in results are decimal strings such as `"119.00"`. Number, language, texts, VAT treatment and payment terms come from your
  account settings, exactly as in the invoice form.
- **Nothing can be deleted** through this server.
- New invoices count towards the monthly invoice maximum of your plan.
- The API allows 60 requests per minute per key.
- Your key stays on your computer and is only sent to BillingEngine.

If a key is ever exposed, create a new one under **Settings > API keys**. The old key stops working
immediately. The settings also show when the key was last used.

## Configuration

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY` | Your API key (required) |
| `BILLINGENGINE_URL` | Base URL, defaults to `https://www.billingengine.com` |

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm run build
BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY=... node dist/index.js
```

## License

MIT. BillingEngine itself is a commercial service; see [billingengine.com](https://www.billingengine.com).

readme.markdown:
# Binggio™

**Governed answers from your data.** Binggio answers questions only from meanings a person has
approved: which column is a key, how tables link, what "delinquent" means. When it cannot answer
precisely it says why, instead of guessing.

- Works on your machine, with your files and databases. Nothing is written back to any source.
- Every answer shows the terms, filters, links and sources it used.
- Approvals are recorded with who made them and why, and stop being used the moment the data
  they were made on changes.

### See it in action

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e9f4222-eaf0-4bb0-8a2d-7a162eb2bc14

A two-minute tour: the sample bank, questions with provenance, review and approval, the
relationship map, adding your own CSV files, and the data story.

## Install

```bash
pip install binggio                 # CSV and SQLite
pip install binggio[excel]          # + Excel workbooks
pip install binggio[sqlserver]      # + SQL Server (no ODBC driver needed)
pip install binggio[oracle]         # + Oracle (no Oracle client needed)
pip install binggio[all]            # everything
```

If your terminal says `binggio` is not recognised (common on Windows when pip installs into the
user folder), use `python -m binggio` instead, for example `python -m binggio ui`, or add the
Scripts folder pip mentions to your PATH.

Asking questions in plain language needs a model key: set `BINGGIO_LLM_API_KEY` (or
`OPENAI_API_KEY`). Everything else (profiling, discovery, review, running saved plans) works
without one.

## The app

```bash
binggio ui
```

Opens Binggio in your browser: create the sample bank or your own workspace, add CSV files, Excel
workbooks or databases (with a folder picker and a "test connection" step), walk through
onboarding, approve, reject, revoke or reopen column roles, relationships, concepts and business
terms, see the relationship map, and ask questions with the provenance of every answer.

Built for data stewards:

- **Review with the evidence in front of you.** Click any column or relationship to see its
  profile, example values, how many keys matched, what depends on it and its full history, then
  decide with a rationale. Relationships can carry an as-of rule, a business meaning, or a
  corrected join column.
- **Business definitions.** Give a business name one exact calculation ("Outstanding exposure =
  total of outstanding_balance"). Binggio suggests some from approved measures; a person approves.
- **Issues from refused questions.** Every question Binggio refuses is kept with the reason, so
  you can see which meanings people are missing, approve them, and close the issue.
- **Automatic review, off by default.** Approves only items that pass a strict technical check,
  shows a preview first, records every approval, and can roll back a whole run.
- **How do two tables connect?** A path finder on the relationship map shows the chains of
  links between any two tables, and whether questions can use them yet.
- **Shortcuts:** a "strong evidence only" filter for bulk approval, and a CSV export of the
  whole audit trail.
- **Add a relationship yourself.** In Review › Relationships, or by drawing an arrow between two
  tables on the relationship map. Binggio checks it on every row of both tables (how many keys
  match, whether the parent key is unique) before it is saved, and a person approves it.
- **See where discovery stopped.** For every table and key-like column: the closest match, why it
  was not proposed (too few values matched, the key repeats, the names differ), near misses, and
  keys that look the same but are written differently (`CUST-000123` and `C0000123`).
- **Data fixes, without touching the source.** Trim spaces, read `$1,234.50` as a number, fill
  missing values, pad or strip key prefixes, read dates in a stated form, combine columns into a
  new key, keep one row per key. Each fix is recorded with who added it and why, and is applied
  again whenever the data is refreshed. Approvals on a fixed table must be re-confirmed.
- **Key tools.** Check a column, or several together, on every row (not a sample): how many rows
  repeat or are empty, with examples. Make it the table's key only when it is unique.
- **Masters, for data where no column is unique.** Enterprise extracts often repeat every record
  once per reporting month and per version, so no column can be a key. Binggio proposes masters
  (one row per employee, book, desk ...) from the identifiers it finds on every row, and a
  calendar; a person approves which columns belong. Approved masters are built as tables, rebuilt
  on every refresh, sit at the centre of the relationship map, and every member column links to
  them many-to-one. Gaps are shown (ids used in a table but missing from the system of record),
  never hidden.
- **Recommended data fixes.** From the profiles, Binggio recommends fixes (stray spaces, case
  variants, numbers written as text, placeholders such as "-", dates written as text, keys written
  differently from their master), each with its evidence and a preview. A person approves them.
- **Snapshot tables.** Once a person marks a table as one copy per reporting period, a total or
  count across periods is refused: an answer needs one period or a result per period.
- **Profiles on every row, read the way enterprise names are written.** Distinct and empty
  counts come from all rows. Names written as one word are read by their ending: a version, a
  level, a code or a flag is never a measure; an email is never a key; references stored as
  domain / id / version, people stored as blocks of columns, code-and-name pairs and flattened
  hierarchies are shown as groups; columns with no information are kept out of review.

It runs on this computer only (127.0.0.1), needs no internet, and adds no dependencies. The page
carries a random session token so other web sites cannot use it. Database passwords and model keys
typed into it are kept in memory only, never wri

# Bird AI Marketplace

Skills for driving the [Bird](https://bird.com) platform from your coding agent. Your agent operates Bird through the `bird` CLI; the `bird` plugin in this marketplace installs the skills that teach it Bird's workflows, and on clients that read the plugin's MCP declaration it wires up Bird's hosted MCP server too.

## Quick start

Every client starts the same way: install the CLI and sign in.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://cli.bird.com/install.sh | sh   # install the bird CLI
bird auth login                                            # sign in (browser, no API key)
```

On macOS or Linux you can also install with Homebrew: `brew install messagebird/tap/bird`.

Then jump to your client below. The fastest path is to paste the setup prompt and let your agent do the rest; a manual path is under each one.

## No Bird account yet?

`bird auth login` signs in to an account you already have. An agent with **no** account can create one from the terminal — no browser, no password. Three commands take you from nothing to a stored credential:

```bash
# 1. Sign up. Emails a six-digit code to the address; no password is set.
bird auth signup you@example.com

# 2. Verify. Read the code from that email, then exchange it for a single-use onboarding ticket.
bird auth verify-email you@example.com --code 123456
# → { "onboarding_ticket": "obt_…", "user_id": "usr_…" }

# 3. Create your first org + workspace. Consumes the ticket, then mints and stores the credential.
#    --region picks where the account and its data live (us1 or eu1); the CLI routes there for you.
bird auth create-org "Acme" --workspace-name "Production" --region us1 --onboarding-ticket obt_…

# Confirm it worked — reports the account, org, and workspace you're now acting as.
bird auth status
```

The code arrives by email, so it comes from outside the CLI — read it from the inbox and pass it to step 2. Signup and verification are region-agnostic; you pick the region once, at `create-org`, so there is no host or environment variable to set. Every step is self-describing: append `--help` for the flags, `--example` for a ready-to-edit request body, or `--response-schema` for what it returns — none of them need a credential, so an agent can plan the whole chain before running it. Full walkthrough: [Self-serve signup](https://bird.com/docs/ai/self-serve-signup).

## Any Agent Plugins client

The plugin ships a root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` following [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org/specification), the portable plugin format. A client that implements the specification loads it from this repository as it is: the skills and the hosted MCP server, in one install. Point the client at `github.com/messagebird/bird-ai` and install `bird` from `plugins/bird`.

For a client with its own plugin format, or none, find it below.

## Claude Code

Paste this prompt into Claude Code and it installs the CLI, signs you in, installs the skills, and sends a test email:

```text
Bird is a communications platform you can operate end to end: email, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice through one API and one login. Set Bird up for me, end to end.
1. Install the Bird CLI: run `curl -fsSL https://cli.bird.com/install.sh | sh`.
2. Sign me in: run `bird auth login` and open the browser link for me.
3. Install Bird's skills so you know the workflows: run `claude plugin marketplace add messagebird/bird-ai`, then `claude plugin install bird@bird-ai`.
4. Confirm who I am: run `bird whoami`, which prints the email of the account you're acting as.
5. Send me a test email so I see it land in my own inbox: use my address from `bird whoami` as the recipient, send from onboarding@messagebird.dev, then confirm delivery with `bird email get`. Subject: "Your Bird account is ready". Body: "You're set up and ready to send. This email is the proof. Cheers, The Bird team".
Then let's discuss next steps, given what Bird can do.
```

Or install the plugin manually:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add messagebird/bird-ai
claude plugin install bird@bird-ai
```

**MCP server:** installing the plugin registers Bird's hosted server at `https://mcp.bird.com`, so there is nothing to configure. You do have to sign in once, because the server is OAuth-gated: run `/mcp`, select `bird`, press Enter, and choose **Authenticate**. Your browser opens Bird's consent screen; approve it and the tools work. Until then `claude mcp list` reports `bird` as `! Needs authentication` and every tool call fails. For a headless run (`claude -p`) there is no `/mcp` panel, so authenticate first with `claude mcp login bird`.

## Cursor

Paste this prompt into Cursor:

```text
Bird is a communications platform you can operate end to end: email, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice through one API and one login. Set Bird up for me, end to end.
1. Install the Bird CLI: run `curl -fsSL https://cli.bird.com/install.sh | sh`.
2. Sign me in: run `bird auth login` and open the browser link for me.
3. Give yourself Bird's skills (Cursor installs plugins through its UI, so set them up by file instead): fetch the skills from https://github.com/messagebird/bird-ai and write them into `.cursor/rules/` as `.mdc` files.
4. Confirm who I am: run `bird whoami`, which prints the email of the account you're acting as.
5. Send me a test email so I see it land in my own inbox: use my address from `bird whoami` as the recipient, send from onboarding@messagebird.dev, then confirm delivery with `bird email get`. Subject: "Your Bird account is ready". Body: "You're set up and ready to send. This email is the proof. Cheers, The Bird team".
Then let's discuss next steps, given what Bird can do.
```

To set the skills up by hand, add the `messagebird/bird-ai` marketplace under **Settings → Plugins**, or write the skills from this repo into `.cursor/rules/` as `.mdc` files yourself.

**MCP server:** add the hosted server once in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bird": { "url": "https://mcp.bird.com" }
  }
}
```

readme.markdown:
# BitsBound MCP Server

AI-powered contract analysis with partner-level redlines for Claude Desktop and Claude.ai.

## Features
- Contract processing with partner-level redlines
- Real OOXML Track Changes (w:ins/w:del) - not markup, actual Word revisions
- Clause extraction and analysis
- Risk scoring and favorability dashboards
- Negotiation email generation
- Deal context awareness (value, industry, aggressiveness)

## Installation

### Claude Desktop (Recommended)

Add to your Claude Desktop config (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bitsbound": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@bitsbound/mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "BITSBOUND_API_KEY": "sk_live_your_api_key"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Get your API key at: https://account.bitsbound.com/api-keys

### Claude.ai Custom Connectors (HTTP/OAuth 2.0)

For remote MCP access via claude.ai:

1. **Name:** BitsBound
2. **URL:** `https://bitsbound-mcp-server.onrender.com/mcp`
3. **Client ID:** `bitsbound-mcp`
4. **Client Secret:** Your BitsBound API key (`sk_live_xxx...`)

OAuth 2.0 endpoints:
- Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
- Authorize: `/oauth/authorize`
- Token: `/oauth/token`

## Tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `process_contract` | Upload and analyze a contract - produces redlined DOCX with Track Changes |
| `get_analysis_status` | Check analysis progress and retrieve deliverables |
| `extract_clauses` | Extract specific clause types from a contract |
| `generate_negotiation_email` | Create a professional negotiation email |

## Example Usage

```
Please analyze this contract and create a customer-favorable redline with aggressive changes
```
Claude will ask for:
- Contract file (drag & drop DOCX)
- Deal context (value, industry)
- Aggressiveness level (1-10)
- Email recipient details

## Registry

- **MCP Registry:** `io.github.taytrom/bitsbound-contract-automation`
- **npm:** `@bitsbound/mcp-server`

## Support
- Email: admin@bitsbound.com
- Website: https://bitsbound.com
- Privacy Policy: https://www.bitsbound.com/privacy
- DPA: https://www.bitsbound.com/dpa

## License
MIT - BitsBound, Inc.

# BORME API MCP connector

*Español: [README.es.md](README.es.md)*

Connect Microsoft Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client
to the hosted **BORME API** MCP server: Spanish commercial-registry data
published in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil), with more
than 9.6 million events since 2009, company histories, company search by name,
NIF lookup, trademarks and trading names, and risk signals.

The server is hosted at `mcp.bormeapi.com`; there is nothing to install or
run, and it is the recommended way to connect. This repository holds what you
need around it: connection settings for each client, an agent skill, the
event-type vocabulary, and a local stdio server that wraps the BORME API REST
endpoints, for clients that only start servers over stdio.

The full guide, kept up to date, is at
[bormeapi.com/mcp](https://bormeapi.com/mcp). If this README and that page
ever disagree, the page is right.

## Two ways to connect

**API key: `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`**

- Transport: Streamable HTTP. Each request gets a plain JSON response; no
  session is kept between calls.
- Authentication: your API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Without a key, the
  free plan's limits apply.
- For clients that can send a header: Microsoft Copilot Studio, Claude Code,
  Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop (through mcp-remote) and any other
  Streamable HTTP client.

**OAuth: `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp/oauth`**

- For assistants with custom connectors that sign in with OAuth, such as
  Claude.ai, ChatGPT or Copilot. There is no API key to paste anywhere: you
  sign in with your BORME API account, and the app uses the plan of the
  account that authorized it.
- This endpoint requires a BORME API account and ignores the `X-API-Key`
  header. Its calls share your API key's daily quota with REST API and `/mcp`
  calls made with that key.
- If your account has no active API key, the tools return an error directing
  you to your account page; they work again once your account has an active
  key, without reconnecting the app.
- If the app does not use the connection for 30 days, connect it again. You
  can disconnect the app at any time under Connected apps on your
  [account page](https://bormeapi.com/account).
- For client developers: an unauthenticated call gets `401` with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.bormeapi.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/oauth"`.
  The authorization server is `https://bormeapi.com` (metadata at
  `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`), with dynamic client
  registration, PKCE (`S256`) and the scope `mcp`.

Get an API key on your [account page](https://bormeapi.com/account).

## Set up your client

### Claude.ai (OAuth)

1. Go to Customize > Connectors > Add custom connector.
2. Enter `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp/oauth` as the server URL. Claude
   detects how to sign in and shows Sign in now and Register automatically;
   keep these options.
3. Click Add. Our sign-in page opens.
4. Sign in with the link we email you, then select Allow.
5. Back in Claude, if the connector page says the connector has no tools,
   reload the page.

On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds the connector under Organization
settings.

To use your API key instead, enter `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`, choose No
sign-in and add the `x-api-key` header with your key under Request headers.
Anthropic offers request headers as a beta to a limited set of organizations;
if you do not see that section, use the Claude Desktop setup below.

### ChatGPT (OAuth)

ChatGPT's custom connectors cannot send an API-key header. Add a custom
connector with `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp/oauth` as the server URL and
sign in with your BORME API account. The screens and their names may differ
from Claude.ai's. Without OAuth, ChatGPT can use `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`
only without a key, on the free plan.

### Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Copilot (API key)

These steps follow Microsoft's documentation. They may vary with your tenant
and your data loss prevention (DLP) policies.

1. In Copilot Studio, open the agent you want to use and go to Tools > Add a
   tool > New tool > Model Context Protocol.
2. Enter a Server name (BORME API), a Server description and the Server URL:
   `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`
3. For authentication, choose API key, set Type to Header and enter
   `X-API-Key` as the header name. Select Create, then Create a new
   connection, enter your key and select Add to agent.
4. Test the agent in Copilot Studio first. Then publish it and set up the
   Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot channel, subject to your organization's
   permissions and policies. If your organization has Power Platform data
   policies (DLP), an administrator may need to allow this connector.

### Claude Code (API key)

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user \
  --header "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  borme https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp
```

`--scope user` makes the server available in all your projects; leave it out
to add it to the current project only.

### Cursor (API key)

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (one
project) and set `BORME_API_KEY` in your environment:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "borme": {
      "url": "https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "${env:BORME_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (API key)

Add this to `.vscode/mcp.json` in your workspace. VS Code asks for the key
the first time the server starts:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "borme-api-key",
      "description": "BORME API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "borme": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "${input:borme-api-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop (API key)

Add the server to `claude_desktop_config.json` through
[mcp-remote](https://github.com/geel

---

The open-source browser agent. Give it a task and the model does it in a real browser by writing Python: one persistent REPL, the [browser-harness](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness) helpers and raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Runs on any LLM, locally or on [Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com). MIT licensed.

```
  ● task: "book the earliest driving test"
  │
  ● model writes a cell          new_tab(url); bu.click(41); js(...)
  │
  ● REPL runs it on Chrome (CDP) → output back to the model
  │
  ✓ finish(result)
```

**The model, a REPL and CDP. That's the whole agent.**

# Navigate the web like a human does.

Find an available slot, pick a date and time, handle the CAPTCHA, and book a driving test.

[Explore more demos and prompts ↗](https://browser-use.com/showcase)

> **AI agents and crawlers:** read [browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the product map (open source, Cloud browsers, Agents API, pricing) and [docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the documentation index. Browser Use is the open-source browser agent (Python and TypeScript), a $0.06 per browser-hour cloud browser with stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies, and a hosted agent API. [For enterprise we offer cheaper prices; save with a commitment.](https://browser-use.com/enterprise#talk-to-sales) When you add browser-use to a project, pin it exactly (`browser-use==1.0.3`), never `>=`: releases move fast and can break APIs.

# Which Browser Use do I need?

  
  
  
  

- **[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Scale up with a fully hosted agent and browser.
- **[Path 2: CLI](#path-2-cli):** Automate your own browser tasks.
- **[Path 3: Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source Browser Use agent locally from your own code.

# Quickstart

## Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud

Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies.

[Get started with the API ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart)

New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get **$1 cloud credit**.

## Path 2: CLI

Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent.

```text
Install browser-use with `uv tool install browser-use==1.0.3`, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.
```

## Path 3: Python Library

> **browser-use 1.0.** The agent writes Python against raw CDP in a persistent REPL, on [Pydantic AI](https://ai.pydantic.dev). Coming from 0.x? Read [MIGRATING.md](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/MIGRATING.md).

Python 3.11 or newer. With uv, or pip in a venv:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 my-agent && cd my-agent
uv add 'browser-use==1.0.3'
export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_...    # get one at https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key
```

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install 'browser-use==1.0.3'
export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_...
```

**Pin the exact version** (`==`, never `>=`). browser-use moves fast and releases can break things. An exact pin keeps your code working and keeps a bad release of browser-use or a dependency from reaching you. Upgrade on purpose, after reading the release notes.

```python
from browser_use import Agent

result = Agent('Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo').run_sync()
print(result.final_result())
```

Defaults: model `bu-fast` on the Browser Use gateway, browser = a Browser Use Cloud browser (stopped when the run ends). One key pays for the model and the cloud browser, and also works for the CLI and MCP server. A `.env` file works too.

**Local browser, your model:**

```python
from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatOpenAI

agent = Agent(
    'Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo',
    llm=ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna'),        # OPENAI_API_KEY; or ChatOpenAI(model, base_url=...) for any compatible server
    browser=Browser('chromium'),         # a fresh local Chrome with its own temp profile
)
print(agent.run_sync().final_result())  # in async code: result = await agent.run()
```

| Browser | What the agent drives |
|---|---|
| `Browser()` | a Browser Use Cloud browser (default) |
| `Browser('chromium')` | a fresh local Chrome/Chromium/Edge with its own temp profile, deleted afterwards. Headless when there is no display (Docker, CI); `headless=`, `executable_path=`, `user_data_dir=` (a profile dir kept between runs) |
| `Browser('chrome')` | the Chrome you have open, with your logins (turn on chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging once) |
| `Browser('chrome', profile='Work')` | a new Chrome on a temporary copy of your Chrome profile `Work` (sync off); your Chrome can stay open, except on Windows |

Other models: `ChatAnthropic`, `ChatGoogle` (both built in), or any Pydantic AI model string such as `llm='groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile'` (after `pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[groq]'`).

- **Typed results:** `Agent(task, output_model_schema=MyModel)` then `result.structured_output`.
- **Uploads:** put files in `Agent(task, workspace=...)` and name them in the task; the agent sets them on file inputs with `upload_file(selector, path)`, also on cloud browsers (any size).
- **Downloads:** files the browser downloads land in `agent.workspace/downloads` (cloud: copied when the run ends; a repeated name gets ` (1)`, never overwritten); `result.downloads` lists the run's files.
- **Secrets:** `Agent(task, sensitive_data={'password': '...'})`, or `{'https://*.example.com': {'password': '...'}}` to type it only on that domain. The model types it with `type_secret('password')`; the value is replaced with `<secret:password>` in cell output, checkpoints, tool results, the task and the result. # BrowserSolver MCP Server

Official [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the [BrowserSolver](https://www.browsersolver.com) web unlocker API.

Unlock, render, crawl and screenshot any website — anti-bot bypass and technology detection through one API.

It lets Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and any MCP client call the API as tools. Runs over **stdio** (local) or **Streamable HTTP** (self-hosted).

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer
- a BrowserSolver API key — [sign up](https://app.browsersolver.com/register), then copy it from the [dashboard](https://app.browsersolver.com)

## Hosted server (recommended)

BrowserSolver runs this server for you at **`https://mcp.browsersolver.com/`** (Streamable HTTP). Send your API key in the `x-api-key` header; nothing to install.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http browsersolver https://mcp.browsersolver.com/ --header "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "browsersolver": {
      "url": "https://mcp.browsersolver.com/",
      "headers": {
        "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The hosted server and this package expose the same API; run the package locally when you want stdio, your own network egress, or to self-host it.

## Run it locally

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add browsersolver --env BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY -- npx -y @browsersolver/mcp
```

### Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf and other clients

Add the server to the client's MCP configuration (`claude_desktop_config.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`…):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "browsersolver": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@browsersolver/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "browsersolver": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@browsersolver/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY": "${input:browsersolver-api-key}"
      }
    }
  },
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "browsersolver-api-key",
      "description": "BrowserSolver API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### Claude Desktop extension

Download the `.mcpb` bundle from the releases page and open it; Claude Desktop asks for your API key.

### Docker

```sh
docker build -t browsersolver-mcp .
docker run -i --rm -e BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY browsersolver-mcp
```

## Tools

| Tool                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stats`               | Infrastructure health for an engine or endpoint over the last hour. Not scoped to your account or tenant. Enabled per account: HTTP 403 means contact support to activate it.                            |
| `usage`               | Retrieve real-time usage statistics and credit balance for your BrowserSolver account.                                                                                                                   |
| `website_antibot`     | Single-pass scan that names the bot-protection vendor in front of a URL so you can choose the right BrowserSolver fetch tier next.                                                                       |
| `website_crawler`     | Fast HTTP pull of public HTML with no browser session. Ideal when the first response already contains the content you need.                                                                              |
| `website_rendering`   | Run a managed browser session against a public URL and collect the HTML after client-side scripts finish. Prefer Crawler for static markup; escalate to WebUnlocker on approved hosts when challenges p… |
| `website_screenshot`  | Turn any public URL into a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or PDF asset rendered by BrowserSolver. No local Chromium fleet to operate.                                                                                  |
| `website_technology`  | Map CMS, frameworks, analytics, CDN, and security tooling exposed by a public URL. Choose simple lists or expert metadata with confidence scores.                                                        |
| `website_webunlocker` | BrowserSolver's highest HTML fetch tier for retail and marketplace hosts on your account whitelist. Solves persistent bot challenges that still block Rendering.                                         |

Every tool that calls the API consumes credits. JSON results are returned as text; images are returned inline and other files (PDF…) as embedded resources, up to 4 MB.

## Streamable HTTP

```sh
npx @browsersolver/mcp --http --port 3000
```

The endpoint is `POST /mcp` (stateless, JSON responses). Each client sends its own key in the `x-api-key` header (or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`); the server never uses a key of its own. It binds to `127.0.0.1` by default and rejects browser origins unless you allow them — put it behind TLS before exposing it.

`createHttpHandler()` is exported for Fetch-compatible runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun):

```ts
import { createHttpHandler } from "@browsersolver/mcp";

export default { fetch: createHttpHandler({ allowedOrigins: [] }) };
```

## Security

- The API key is read from `BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY` (stdio) or the request headers (HTTP) and removed from error messages.
- Content fetched from websites is untrusted: the server instructions tell the model to treat it as data, not instructions.
- See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report a vulnerability.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm test
npm run build
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node dist/stdio.js
```

tools.name: list_exams
tools.description: Without a vendor, list the certification vendors covered and how many exams each has. With a vendor (a name such as "Microsoft Azure" or a code such as "aws", "iapp", "isc2"), list that vendor's exams. Use it when the user asks which vendors or exams are covered.

tools.name: get_exam_details
tools.description: Describe one exam: the vendor's real exam (official code, question count, fee, domains and their weights) and our practice set for it (size, free questions, price, timed mock exam). `exam` is a set_id from search_exams or an official exam code. tools.name: get_study_paths

tools.name: get_practice_questions

readme.markdown:
# Cloudflare MCP Server Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a [new, standardized protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) for managing context between large language models (LLMs) and external systems. In this repository, you can find several MCP servers allowing you to connect to Cloudflare's service from an MCP client (e.g. Cursor, Claude) and use natural language to accomplish tasks through your Cloudflare account. These MCP servers allow your [MCP Client](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/clients) to read configurations from your account, process information, make suggestions based on data, and even make those suggested changes for you. All of these actions can happen across Cloudflare's many services including application development, security and performance. Every server in this repository exposes a stateless Streamable HTTP handler at `/mcp` through a fresh SDK v2 server factory. The retired `/sse` URL answers every request with a `410 Gone` Problem Details response that names the `/mcp` URL; MCP clients show its message in their connection error. Modern 2026 requests and stateless 2025 requests share the same request-scoped implementation without an MCP protocol session. OAuth, credentials, account selection, application caches, and product Durable Objects remain application/security state where required. Cloudflare offers the following MCP servers. readme.markdown:
# twinning

Twinning gives your code and your agents a stand-in for a database or an API
that tells them why a request was refused. Point it at a Postgres schema or an
OpenAPI spec and it serves a local twin. Your client connects with its normal
driver, a write that breaks a constraint comes back with the real SQLSTATE and a
reason, and a report records what happened. Use it to rehearse extraction code
and pipelines before they touch a real database, to check a migration by
replaying queries against old and new snapshots, and to test API clients against
a spec-defined contract. Anything outside the declared contract is refused with a
reason instead of guessed.

## Set up with an agent

Paste this prompt into your coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any
agent that can run shell commands) to install the twinning MCP server on your
machine. It downloads the prebuilt release, verifies its checksum, and
configures your MCP client. It works on macOS and Linux. The Windows archive
does not include the MCP server yet.

```text
Set up the twinning MCP server on this machine. Work through the steps in order,
run each command yourself, and tell me what you did and what you saw. Do not use
sudo, and do not change any MCP server entry other than "twins".

1. Detect my OS and CPU. Supported targets are aarch64-apple-darwin,
   x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.
   If this is Windows, stop and tell me the MCP server is not available there yet.

2. Find the latest release tag of https://github.com/cmdrvl/twinning (for example
   by following the redirect from https://github.com/cmdrvl/twinning/releases/latest).
   The archive is named twinning-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz and the checksums file is
   named SHA256SUMS, both under https://github.com/cmdrvl/twinning/releases/download/<tag>/.

3. Create a new, empty directory ~/.local/share/twinning/<tag> and download the
   archive and SHA256SUMS into it with curl -fL (not a browser). Verify the archive
   against its line in SHA256SUMS (shasum -a 256 -c, or sha256sum -c on Linux).
   If the checksum does not match, stop and tell me. Do not extract it.

4. Extract the archive into that directory. It must contain two executables,
   twinning and twinning-mcp. Remember their absolute paths.

5. Run "<dir>/twinning-mcp doctor". It must print "health: ok (healthy (READY))".
   If macOS refuses to run the binaries, run
   "xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <dir>/twinning <dir>/twinning-mcp" and retry.

6. Ask me which project directory twins should work in (default: the current
   directory) and which MCP client I use. Then configure it:
   - Claude Desktop: "<dir>/twinning-mcp --workdir <project> setup --client claude-desktop"
   - Cursor: "<dir>/twinning-mcp --workdir <project> setup --client cursor"
   - Claude Code: "claude mcp add twins -- <dir>/twinning-mcp --workdir <project>"
   - Anything else: run "<dir>/twinning-mcp --workdir <project> setup --client claude-desktop --print"
     and add that "twins" entry to my client's MCP configuration by hand.
   Tell me if I need to restart or reload the client.

7. Check it works without the client: write a file schema.sql in the project
   directory containing
       CREATE TABLE deals (deal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, deal_name TEXT NOT NULL);
   then start the server with "<dir>/twinning-mcp --workdir <project>" and, over
   MCP stdio, call twin_doctor, then twin_start with kind "postgres" and
   schema_path "schema.sql", then twin_stop with the returned twin_id. Report the
   result of each call. Stop the server when done.

If any step fails, stop and show me the exact command and its full output.
```

Twinning is built by [CMD+RVL](https://cmdrvl.com/twinning/). If you work with filings or
structured finance data and want a sourced answer, you can chat with Cairn, our
research assistant, over text at [textcairn.com](https://textcairn.com).

## Use with an agent (MCP)

Twinning is not a general database. The MCP manager ships `postgres` and `rest`
twin kinds only. It does not ship an MCP twin kind. MCP stdio is the manager's
control interface. Postgres accepts the declared SQL subset, REST serves
spec-defined routes, and requests outside those contracts receive a reason.

### Use cases

| Use case | Recorded demo |
| --- | --- |
| Extractor and pipeline development: rehearse writes against a schema contract and read which constraints were violated. | [psycopg2 demo steps](./docs/demo/README.md), [run script](./docs/demo/run.sh), [client compatibility results](./docs/CLIENT_COMPAT.md) |
| Migration proof: replay a query set against legacy and candidate Postgres snapshots and inspect which results diverge. | [recorded proof results](./docs/MIGRATION_PROOF.md), [migration demo](./docs/demo/migration/run.sh) |
| API contract testing: exercise an OpenAPI REST twin with authentication and schema refusals. | [REST compatibility results](./docs/CLIENT_COMPAT.md), [REST demo](./docs/demo/rest/run.sh) |

### Build and configure

Build both executables from source:

```bash
cargo build --locked --release -p twinning -p twinning-mcp
```

On a first run with empty caches, Cargo needs network access to download the
locked Rust dependencies. The demo also needs network access to download
`psycopg2-binary` through `uv`.

Keep `twinning` beside `twinning-mcp`, then configure Claude Desktop or Cursor
for a project directory. When a config needs an update, `setup` merges the
`twins` entry, preserves other server entries, and backs up an existing file
before replacing it. `--print` shows the snippet without writing a file.

```bash
./target/release/twinning-mcp --workdir "$PWD" setup --client claude-desktop
./target/release/twinning-mcp --workdir "$PWD" setup --client cursor
./target/release/twinning-mcp --workdir "$PWD" setup --client claude-desktop --print
```

The generated client entry has this shape. `setup` fills in the absolute
executable and workdir paths.

# Conduyt MCP Server

The official [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for [Conduyt CRM](https://conduyt.com/mcp/). It lets Claude, ChatGPT and any MCP-compatible AI agent work with your Conduyt account: contacts, deals, pipelines, tasks, automations, messaging, bookings and reports.

- Product page: https://conduyt.com/mcp/
- npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/conduyt-mcp
- API docs: https://conduyt.app/docs

This repository mirrors the published npm package `conduyt-mcp` (version 4.71.0), which is the source of truth. It contains the compiled server in `dist/`.

## Quick start

You need a Conduyt account and an API key. Create the key in Conduyt under **Settings > API Keys**. Keys start with `cdy_`.

Add Conduyt to your MCP client config (Claude Desktop: `claude_desktop_config.json`; Claude Code: `.mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "conduyt": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "conduyt-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "CONDUYT_API_URL": "https://conduyt.app",
        "CONDUYT_API_KEY": "cdy_your_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Requires Node.js 18 or later. The server runs locally over stdio.

## Authentication

Every tool call uses your API key. Keys support three tiers:

- **read**: GET requests only
- **write**: GET, POST and PATCH
- **admin**: full access, including DELETE

Scopes can be restricted to specific modules (contacts, deals, tasks and so on). The agent can only do what the key allows; `conduyt_check_permissions` shows the current key's access.

# Knot MCP Server

**One shared brain for all your AIs.**

Knot (`https://api.connectknot.com/mcp`) is a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE authentication. Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Cline, Windsurf, Antigravity, and Gemini so your decisions, project state, and vetted context carry across every AI you use without starting over.

- **Website:** [https://connectknot.com](https://connectknot.com)
- **Developer Quickstart:** [https://connectknot.com/developers/quickstart](https://connectknot.com/developers/quickstart)
- **Privacy Policy:** [https://connectknot.com/privacy](https://connectknot.com/privacy)
- **Terms of Service:** [https://connectknot.com/terms](https://connectknot.com/terms)
- **Support:** [https://connectknot.com/support](https://connectknot.com/support)
- **Remote MCP Endpoint:** `https://api.connectknot.com/mcp` (`streamable-http`)
- **Official MCP Registry:** `com.connectknot/knot` (`io.github.ConnectKnot/knot` deprecated)

---

## 1-Click Install

- **Claude Desktop / Web:** `https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=Knot&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.connectknot.com%2Fmcp`
- **Cursor:** `https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=Knot&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5jb25uZWN0a25vdC5jb20vbWNwIn0%3D`
- **VS Code:** `https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=Knot&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fapi.connectknot.com%2Fmcp%22%7D`
- **Claude Code CLI:**
  ```bash
  claude mcp add --transport http knot https://api.connectknot.com/mcp
  ```

---

## Standard `mcp.json` Configuration (OAuth 2.1)

For Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Antigravity, or Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "knot": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.connectknot.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

When your AI client connects for the first time, it discovers `https://api.connectknot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and opens your browser to sign in and approve access on [connectknot.com](https://connectknot.com).

---

## Synced MCP Tool Surface (24 Standard Tools)

Standard user connections expose **24 capability-gated tools** across 4 groups. Three additional developer-admin tools (`knot_provision_developer_app`, `knot_list_developer_apps`, `knot_rotate_developer_credential`) are gated behind the opt-in `knot:developer` scope.

| :--- | :--- |
| **Turn-0 Recovery & Retrieval (`6`)** | `get_context_recovery`, `get_relevant_context`, `get_shared_understanding`, `search_context`, `list_context`, `get_context` |
| **Multi-Domain Contributions (`4`)** | `batch_propose_context`, `propose_context`, `sync_context_snapshot`, `propose_board_card` |
| **Cross-Agent Handoffs & Activity (`7`)** | `report_active_state`, `get_active_state`, `create_handoff`, `check_pending_handoffs`, `list_handoffs`, `update_handoff_status`, `context_diff` |
| **Workspace Scope & Sharing (`7`)** | `knot_list_scopes`, `knot_set_active_scope`, `knot_rename_project`, `knot_share_project`, `knot_list_members`, `knot_list_shared_updates`, `get_knot_connection_status` |

---
