# [vedetta-mcp](https://vedetta.dethboy.com)

Pay-per-call market intelligence for MCP clients (Claude, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, and others).

Vedetta sells crypto sentiment reads, sentiment-vs-price divergence verdicts, and live analyst answers over x402 — USDC on Base, one micropayment per paid request. No signup, no API key on paid routes: payment is authentication.

**Product shape (gateway 2.14.1):** FREE tools (`200 OK`, IP rate-limited): `route`, `track-record`, `korra-calls`, `korra-news`, `korra-lean`. Paid funnel `feed`/`snapshot` at **$0.01**; history **$0.01**, screener **$0.03**, live desk **$0.09**. Hosted `/mcp` (if used) stays Bearer-token gated.

This package is a **stdio MCP server**. You bring a dedicated low-balance wallet (`EVM_PRIVATE_KEY`) for paid tools. The server settles each micropayment locally. Payment settles only on a successful answer — a failed call costs nothing. Free tools never require a wallet. Directory inspectors (Glama / Smithery) get all **23** tools from `tools/list` with empty env.

**Descriptive market analysis only — not financial advice.**

Site: https://vedetta.dethboy.com · OpenAPI: https://vedetta.dethboy.com/openapi.json · Agent card: https://vedetta.dethboy.com/vedetta.md

## Install

Node 20+. Wallet needs USDC on Base only for paid tools. A few dollars covers hundreds of calls.

One-liner (no wallet — free funnel works; paid tools return the 402 offer):

```bash
npx -y vedetta-mcp@latest
```

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add vedetta -e EVM_PRIVATE_KEY=0xYOUR_KEY -- npx -y vedetta-mcp@latest
```

Claude Desktop / Cursor (`claude_desktop_config.json` or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vedetta": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "vedetta-mcp@latest"],
      "env": { "EVM_PRIVATE_KEY": "0xYOUR_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

Gemini CLI: clone/install this repo as an extension (`gemini-extension.json`). Cline Marketplace: see `llms-install.md`. Cursor plugin: `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` + `mcp.json`.

Without `EVM_PRIVATE_KEY` the server still starts — free tools work; paid tools return the live 402 offer so you can inspect cost before funding a wallet. The key never leaves your machine.

## Worked example

Start free: audit + cache check, then decide whether a paid live read is worth it.

```
vedetta_track-record
  asset: BTC

vedetta_snapshot
  asset: BTC
```

Same over HTTP (free funnel returns **200**):

```bash
curl -sS "https://vedetta.dethboy.com/v1/route?task=btc+sentiment"
curl -sS "https://vedetta.dethboy.com/v1/korra/calls?asset=BTC"
curl -sS "https://vedetta.dethboy.com/v1/korra/news?asset=BTC"
curl -sS "https://vedetta.dethboy.com/v1/korra/lean?asset=BTC"
```

Cheapest paid path: funnel `vedetta_snapshot`/$0.01 → `vedetta_history` ($0.01) / `vedetta_screener` ($0.03) → live `vedetta_consensus` / `vedetta_ask` ($0.09).

## Price table

Live 402 offer is authoritative for paid routes. Server refuses any offer above the listed cap. Free tools never pay.

| Tool | What it does | Price | Latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vedetta_feed` | Desk post stream | $0.01 | instant |

Other live desks (`equity`, `macro`, `pulse`, `theme`, `trend`, `news-read`, `house-view`, `event`, `odds`, `social`, `narrative`) are $0.09. Full catalog: https://vedetta.dethboy.com/registry.json

## Manual installation and configuration 

**Prerequisites** 

Before building and running Devart MCP Server for MySQL, ensure the following components are installed:

* [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0)
* **ADO.NET connection** — **Devart.AI.McpServer.AdoNet.MySql.csproj** Devart dotConnect for MySQL (installed automatically via NuGet during build)
* **ODBC connection** — **Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc.MySql.csproj** [Devart ODBC Driver for MySQL](https://www.devart.com/odbc/MySQL/download.html) (requires manual download and installation)

**Step 1: Clone the repository**

Clone the project repository and navigate to the project directory:

1\. Open **Command Prompt**.

2\. Enter the following command:

```cmd
git clone https://github.com/devart-ai-connectivity/devart-mcp-server-mysql.git
cd devart-mcp-server-mysql
```

**Step 2: Build the MCP Server from source**

You can build Devart MCP Server for MySQL from source using either of the supported database connectivity technologies: ADO.NET or ODBC.

* To build the MCP server with ADO.NET, run the following command:

```cmd
dotnet publish Devart.AI.McpServer.AdoNet/Devart.AI.McpServer.AdoNet.MySql/Devart.AI.McpServer.AdoNet.MySql.csproj -c ReleaseMySql /p:TargetFramework=net8.0
```
The Devart dotConnect for MySQL NuGet package is downloaded and restored automatically.

* To build the MCP server with ODBC, select the command based on the bitness of your data source.

For 64-bit data source, run the following command:

```cmd
dotnet publish Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc/Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc.MySql/Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc.MySql.csproj -c ReleaseMySql -r "win-x64" /p:TargetFramework=net8.0
```

For 32-bit data source, run the following command:

```cmd
dotnet publish Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc/Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc.MySql/Devart.AI.McpServer.Odbc.MySql.csproj -c ReleaseMySql -r "win-x86" /p:TargetFramework=net8.0
```
>**Note**
>
>The target platform must match the bitness of your ODBC data source.

**Step 3: Configure the database connection for the MCP Server**

1\. Create an `mcpserver.json` configuration file in the directory containing the built MCP Server executable.

2\. In the file, configure the database connection.

* Configure a connection with ADO.NET.

Add the following configuration to the `mcpserver.json` file:

```json
{

      "Name": "my_mysql",
      "ConnectionString": "Server=localhost;Port=3306;User Id=your_user;Password=your_password;Database=your_database;License Key=your_license_key;",
      "ProtocolType": "stdio"
    }
  ]
}
```

* Configure a connection with ODBC.

Add the following configuration to the `mcpserver.json` file:

```json
{
  "Connections": [
    {
      "Name": "my_mysql",
      "DsnName": "your_dsn_name",
      "ProtocolType": "stdio"
    }
  ]
}
```

* Configure a connection with ODBC using a connection string.

Add the following configuration to the `mcpserver.json` file:

```json
{
  "Connections": [
    {
      "Name": "my_mysql",
      "ConnectionString": "Driver={Devart ODBC Driver for MySQL};Server=localhost;User ID=mysql;Password=your_password;Database=your_database;",
      "ProtocolType": "stdio"
    }
  ]
}
```
where:

* `Name` — The connection name.

* `ConnectionString` (applies to ADO.NET) — A database-specific connection string used to establish a connection to the target database.

* `DsnName` (applies to ODBC) — The name of your data source.

* `ProtocolType` — A transport protocol. The possible options are: `stdio` or `http`.

* `HttpPort` (required if `ProtocolType` is set to `http`) — The port number for the `http` protocol. 

**Step 4: Run the MCP server**

After you configure the MCP Server, you can start it.

* To start the server with ADO.NET, run the following command:

```cmd
Devart.AI.McpServer.AdoNet.MySql.exe run my_mysql

readme.markdown:
# MCP server for didlogic

The official [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server
for [didlogic](https://didlogic.com). It connects Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor,
VS Code and any other MCP client to your didlogic account, so you can manage
phone numbers, SIP accounts, routing, SMS, calls and billing by asking in
plain language.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Auth:** OAuth sign-in, or a didlogic API key
- **Coverage:** the full didlogic public API v1 and v2, within your account's
  permissions and settings

This is a hosted service: there is nothing to install or run. This
repository holds its documentation and registry metadata.

## What you can do

Everything the [didlogic public API](https://docs.didlogic.com/docs/openapi-spec)
offers, including:

- **Phone numbers** — browse countries, cities and regions, search available
  numbers, buy them, change their settings and release them
- **Inbound routing** — add, change and remove the destinations a number
  forwards to
- **SIP accounts** — create, update and delete SIP accounts and manage their
  allowed IP addresses
- **Calls** — call history and statistics, recordings, call price quotes and
  ASR reports
- **Click2Call** — place, check and cancel click-to-call calls
- **SMS** — send messages and read the history
- **Billing** — balance and transaction history
- **Compliance** — KYC documents and identities, number risk checks and HLR
  lookups

What is available to you is exactly what your account and its API key allow.
Every request acts as your account and on its balance: buying a number,
sending an SMS or placing a call is charged at once. Assistants are instructed
to describe a paid or destructive action and wait for your confirmation before
they run it.

## How it works

The server does not expose one tool per API operation. It gives the assistant
three tools and the API's own specification:

1. `search` finds the operations that match a task
2. `get_schema` returns the exact arguments of the ones chosen
3. `execute` runs a short script that calls them and returns only the answer

So the assistant can loop over pages, combine several calls and add up the
results in one step, and the server always covers the API as it is today.
See [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md) for details.

## Setup

You need a didlogic account. If your client uses an API key rather than OAuth,
create one in the customer portal under
[API & Webhooks](https://app.didlogic.com/app/api-webhooks).

### Claude Desktop

Either:

- download the extension from
  [mcp.didlogic.com/didlogic.mcpb](https://mcp.didlogic.com/didlogic.mcpb)
  (also attached to each [release](../../releases)), open it, and paste your
  API key, or
- go to **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, enter
  `https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp`, and sign in with didlogic.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http didlogic https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` and sign in.

### ChatGPT

Add a custom connector (developer mode) with the URL
`https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp` and OAuth authentication, then sign in.

### Cursor and other `mcpServers` clients

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "didlogic": {
      "url": "https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

If the client does not support OAuth, send your API key instead:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "didlogic": {
      "url": "https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

In `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "didlogic": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.didlogic.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Example prompts

- "What's my balance, and how much did I spend on calls last month?"
- "Find me a London number and tell me what it costs before buying it."
- "Forward my US number to my SIP account `office`."
- "Show yesterday's missed calls on my German numbers."
- "Create a SIP account for the Berlin office and allow only 203.0.113.10."
- "Send an SMS to +44 7700 900123 saying the meeting moved to 3 pm."
- "Which countries have the worst answer rate this week?"

More in [docs/examples.md](docs/examples.md).

## Security

- The server holds no credentials of its own. It forwards your OAuth token or
  API key with each request, and didlogic decides what it may do.
- Treat the API key like a password: it can spend your balance. Revoke it in
  [API & Webhooks](https://app.didlogic.com/app/api-webhooks) at any time.
- To report a vulnerability, write to [support@didlogic.com](mailto:support@didlogic.com).

## Known limitations

- Uploading KYC documents needs the assistant to send the file's contents.
  Claude can do this with files you attach; ChatGPT currently cannot, so upload
  documents in the customer portal there.

## Links

- Server and setup page: <https://mcp.didlogic.com>
- MCP server guide: <https://docs.didlogic.com/docs/guides/apps-developer-tools/mcp-server>
- API getting started: <https://docs.didlogic.com/docs/api/get-started>

# DirectIQ MCP Server

Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, and any other [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client to your **DirectIQ** account. Manage contacts, lists, and tags, see how your campaigns performed, and send transactional email in plain language.

DirectIQ is an email marketing and transactional email platform for small businesses, with fast human support and pay-as-you-go pricing. → [directiq.com](https://www.directiq.com)

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (remote, hosted by DirectIQ, nothing to install)
- **Auth:** DirectIQ API key in the `x-api-key` header, or `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (OAuth coming soon)
- **Server card:** `https://mcp.directiq.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`
- **Registry name:** `com.directiq.mcp/directiq`

> This repository holds the public documentation, registry metadata, and client configuration for the hosted DirectIQ MCP server at `mcp.directiq.com`, operated by DirectIQ. There is nothing to install or build.

## Quick start

1. **Get an API key:** log in to the [DirectIQ dashboard](https://app.directiq.com), then go to **Settings → API Keys** and copy or generate a key. No account yet? [Sign up free](https://app.directiq.com/identity/signup/start).
2. **Add the server to your client:** see the snippets below.
3. **Try a prompt:** *"Give me an overview of my DirectIQ account."*

## Client setup

### Cursor
[Add to Cursor](https://www.directiq.com/mcp/cursor/). This link opens Cursor with the config filled in. Replace `YOUR_DIRECTIQ_API_KEY` with your key.

Or add it manually to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "directiq": {
      "url": "https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "YOUR_DIRECTIQ_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)
Add to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code prompts for the key and stores it securely:
```json
{
  "inputs": [
    { "type": "promptString", "id": "directiq_api_key", "description": "DirectIQ API key", "password": true }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "directiq": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "${input:directiq_api_key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http directiq https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp --header "x-api-key: YOUR_DIRECTIQ_API_KEY"
```

### Claude Desktop
Until OAuth ships, use the `mcp-remote` bridge in `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "directiq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp", "--header", "x-api-key:${DIRECTIQ_API_KEY}"],
      "env": { "DIRECTIQ_API_KEY": "YOUR_DIRECTIQ_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Windsurf
`~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "directiq": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "YOUR_DIRECTIQ_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### OpenAI Codex
`~/.codex/config.toml`, after setting `export DIRECTIQ_API_KEY=...`:
```toml
[mcp_servers.directiq]
url = "https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp"
env_http_headers = { "x-api-key" = "DIRECTIQ_API_KEY" }
```

### Any other MCP client
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| URL | `https://mcp.directiq.com/mcp` |
| Header | `x-api-key: <your DirectIQ API key>` |

readme.markdown:
# Driflyte MCP Server

MCP Server for [Driflyte](http://console.driflyte.com).

The Driflyte MCP Server exposes tools that allow AI assistants to query and retrieve topic-specific knowledge from recursively crawled and indexed web pages.
With this MCP server, Driflyte acts as a bridge between diverse, topic-aware content sources (web, GitHub, and more) and AI-powered reasoning, enabling richer, more accurate answers.

## What It Does

- **Deep Web Crawling**: Recursively follows links to crawl and index web pages.
- **GitHub Integration**: Crawls repositories, issues, and discussions.
- **Extensible Resource Support**: Future support planned for Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Docs/Drive, Confluence, JIRA, Zendesk, Salesforce, and more.
- **Topic-Aware Indexing**: Each document is tagged with one or more topics, enabling targeted, topic-specific retrieval.
- **Designed for RAG with RAG**: The server itself is built with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in mind, and it powers RAG workflows by providing assistants with high-quality, topic-specific documents as grounding context.
- **Designed for AI with AI**: The system is not just for AI assistants — it is also designed and evolved using AI itself, making it an AI-native component for intelligent knowledge retrieval.

## Usage & Limits

- **Free Access**: Driflyte is currently free to use.
- **No Signup Required**: You can start using it immediately — no registration or subscription needed.
- **Rate Limits**: To ensure fair usage, requests are limited by IP:
  - **`100` API requests** per **`5` minutes** per **IP address**.
- Future changes to usage policies and limits may be introduced as new features and resource integrations become available.

## Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- An AI assistant (with MCP client) like Cursor, Claude (Desktop or Code), VS Code, Windsurf, etc ...

## Configurations

### CLI Arguments

Driflyte MCP server supports the following CLI arguments for configuration:
- `--transport <stdio|streamable-http>` - Configures the transport protocol (defaults to `stdio`).
- `--port <number>` – Configures the port number to listen on when using `streamable-http` transport (defaults to `3000`).

## Quick Start

This MCP server (using `STDIO` or `Streamable HTTP` transport) can be added to any MCP Client 
like VS Code, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf Github Copilot via the `@driflyte/mcp-server` NPM package.

### ChatGPT

- Navigate to `Settings` under your profile and enable `Developer Mode` under the `Connectors` option.
- In the chat panel, click the `+` icon, and from the dropdown, select `Developer Mode`. 
  You’ll see an option to add sources/connectors.
- Enter the following MCP Server details and then click `Create`:
  - `Name`: `Driflyte`
  - `MCP Server URL`: `https://mcp.driflyte.com/openai`
  - `Authentication`: `No authentication`
  - `Trust Setting`: Check `I trust this application`

See [How to set up a remote MCP server and connect it to ChatGPT deep research](https://community.openai.com/t/how-to-set-up-a-remote-mcp-server-and-connect-it-to-chatgpt-deep-research/1278375) 
and [MCP server tools now in ChatGPT – developer mode](https://community.openai.com/t/mcp-server-tools-now-in-chatgpt-developer-mode/1357233) for more info.

### Claude Code

Run the following command.
See [Claude Code MCP docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp) for more info.

#### Local Server
```bash
claude mcp add driflyte -- npx -y @driflye/mcp-server
```

#### Remote Server
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http driflyte https://mcp.driflyte.com/mcp
```

### Claude Desktop

#### Local Server
Add the following configuration into the `claude_desktop_config.json` file.
See the [Claude Desktop MCP docs](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers) for more info.
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "driflyte": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@driflyte/mcp-server"]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Remote Server
Go to the `Settings` > `Connectors` > `Add Custom Connector` in the Claude Desktop and add the new MCP server with the following fields: 
- Name: `Driflyte` 
- Remote MCP server URL: `https://mcp.driflyte.com/mcp`

### Copilot Coding Agent

Add the following configuration to the `mcpServers` section of your Copilot Coding Agent configuration through 
`Repository` > `Settings` > `Copilot` > `Coding agent` > `MCP configuration`.
See the [Copilot Coding Agent MCP docs](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/copilot/how-tos/agents/copilot-coding-agent/extending-copilot-coding-agent-with-mcp) for more info.

#### Local Server
```json
{

    "driflyte": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@driflyte/mcp-server"]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Remote Server

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "driflyte": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.driflyte.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Cursor

Add the following configuration into the `~/.cursor/mcp.json` file (or `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project folder).
Or setup by 🖱️[One Click Installation](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=driflyte&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyIteSIsIkBkcmlmbHl0ZS9tY3Atc2VydmVyIl19).

readme.markdown:
# Echo Memory

**Shared memory for AI agents, as a graph in your own database.** What Claude Code learns,
Cursor and Codex can recall. Every fact records who wrote it and when, and the server
never calls a model to store one.

<sub>Every line above is real output, captured from these commands against a throwaway
database. The transcript is at
[`.github/branding/demo-transcript.txt`](.github/branding/demo-transcript.txt).</sub>

> Your agents start every session from zero. The usual fix is a notes file you paste into
> context, which grows until it is mostly irrelevant to whatever you are asking. Echo
> Memory is the other shape: facts connected to each other, and a query that returns the
> few that matter. On the author's own 325 fact store that is **96.7% less context** for
> the same answer, with the answer still present 87.2% of the time across 1,190 queries
> the harness derived from their own answers.

```
write_episode                          query_memory
  billing ──uses──▸ Razorpay             "how do we take payments"
    │ written by claude-code               ▸ billing uses Razorpay, not Stripe
    │ supersedes ──▸ Stripe                  written by claude-code, 3 days ago
    └ no model invoked                     ▸ 1,372 tokens, not 41,838
```

## Install

**Requires:** Python 3.11+ and Docker (for the database).

```bash
pipx install echo-mem
echo-memory quickstart
```

`quickstart` starts the database, applies the schema, and prints the `claude mcp add`
line that registers it, filled in with the port it actually used. The Postgres image is
published, so nothing compiles.

Or use the hosted service and run no database at all:

```bash
pipx install echo-mem
echo-memory connect <key>          # a key from https://app.echo-mem.com
```

Then once per machine, so an agent knows *when* to record and recall rather than only
that the tools exist:

```bash
echo-memory install --global
```

> **Restart your client afterwards.** An MCP server is a long lived process that holds
> the code and config it started with, and an editable install does not change that.

> **The PyPI name is `echo-mem`, not `echo-memory`.** That name belongs to an unrelated
> hosted product. The import package and the CLI are both `echo_memory` / `echo-memory`;
> only the distribution name differs.

## Upgrading

```bash
pipx upgrade echo-mem
echo-memory init-db                # apply any new migrations
echo-memory reindex                # rebuild what the new code derives
```

Both steps, in that order, and neither is optional on a store that predates the version
you just installed.

**Skipping `init-db` fails loudly.** A read against a schema older than the code raises an
undefined column, which is the good case: it stops rather than answering from something it
half understands.

**Skipping `reindex` fails silently, which is worse.** Derived data that the new code reads
differently is still the old data, and nothing errors. Concretely, on an upgrade to 0.5.3
the lexical corpus statistics are treated as stale until rebuilt, so BM25 stays off and
your queries keep ranking by `ts_rank` while the setting reports as on. `reindex` rebuilds
the embeddings and those statistics together. `echo-memory health` tells you afterwards.

## Usage

```bash
echo-memory status                 # what each scope holds, and which agents have written
echo-memory health                 # a score, what is weak, and what to do about it
echo-memory dashboard --serve      # the graph, in a browser, localhost only

echo-memory why <fact_id>          # the full audit trail for one fact
echo-memory recall "<question>"    # query the store from a terminal
echo-memory export                 # everything, as JSON

echo-memory install --for cursor   # wire one client, project scoped
echo-memory adopt                  # wire every MCP client on the machine, each with its own id

echo-memory infer-causal-hints     # type the facts whose own sentence states a cause (dry run)

echo-memory eval                   # retrieval quality against your own store
echo-memory eval --context         # what a recall costs against injecting everything
echo-memory eval --context --sweep # the same, as a curve across corpus size
echo-memory eval-external locomo <path>       # LoCoMo, the corpus the published figures use
echo-memory eval-external longmemeval <path>  # LongMemEval, the same
echo-memory calibrate              # is entity resolution trustworthy on your data
echo-memory benchmark              # write, query and digest latency
echo-memory judge                  # retrieval scored on questions written before the answers
echo-memory judge-external         # QA accuracy for a finished eval-external run
```

Operating a store, rather than using one:

```bash
echo-memory graph                  # a scope's graph, as text or JSON
echo-memory merge                  # fold one node into another, once confirmed to be one entity
echo-memory unmerge                # take back an alias a node absorbed from a different entity
echo-memory reattribute            # set the project on facts written before projects were recorded
echo-memory distil                 # read facts out of a session the harness already recorded
echo-memory bootstrap              # import the work that already exists on this machine
echo-memory analyse                # first run comprehension pass for an existing project
echo-memory reconcile              # re-notice memory files the capture hook missed
echo-memory pending                # memory files noticed but not yet in the graph
echo-memory install-hooks          # register every capture hook in ~/.claude/settings.json
echo-memory skill                  # print the usage instructions, for a client with no config file
echo-memory trial                  # record and review v1a exit criteria observations
```

Answering for the data, which is the part a compliance review asks about:

```bash
echo-memory forget                 # erase facts out

…

readme.markdown:
# ExactMelt MCP app

ExactMelt values metals and coins inside ChatGPT, Claude and other MCP
clients. Enter weight, purity, quantity or rolls, compare a buyer's offer,
exchange gold and silver, or build a mixed worksheet. Every result links to a
prefilled PDF report on [exactmelt.com](https://exactmelt.com).

- Website: https://exactmelt.com
- Documentation: https://exactmelt.com/app
- Privacy: https://exactmelt.com/privacy
- Terms: https://exactmelt.com/terms

This repository documents the hosted connector. It does not contain the
website or its code.

## Connect

- Endpoint: `https://exactmelt.com/api/mcp`
- Transport: Streamable HTTP
- Authentication: none (no account, sign-in or API key)

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "exactmelt": { "url": "https://exactmelt.com/api/mcp" } } }
```

In ChatGPT, add it as a custom app/connector with no authentication. In
Claude, open Customize → Connectors → Add custom connector and enter the URL.

## Tools

All tools are read-only.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `calculate_melt_value` | Precious-metal melt value, fine content, unit rates and an optional buyer-offer comparison |
| `calculate_coin_value` | Coin melt value and fine-metal content by quantity, standard rolls or measured grams |
| `find_coins` | Coin presets with issue years, specifications and current melt value per coin |
| `get_coin` | One coin preset with its specifications and a quantity-one melt calculation |
| `calculate_exchange` | Gold-to-silver or silver-to-gold exchange weight at current quotes |
| `calculate_penny_nickel` | Penny or nickel alloy metal value at the base-metal prices you enter |

## Try asking

- "What's my 14K ring worth, 5.2 grams?"
- "Calculate the melt value of 10 Morgan dollars."
- "Exchange 1 troy ounce of gold for silver at current spot."

## Report an issue

Open an issue in this repository or email abishop1933@gmail.com.

## License

The documentation files in this repository are MIT licensed (see
[LICENSE](LICENSE)). The ExactMelt website, its content, data and brand are
not covered by this license.

# Fahali MCP Server

Market-intelligence MCP server that ships **uncertainty-aware intelligence with provenance** on
every response. Fahali runs an ensemble of independent detection engines across ~2,000 live crypto and US equity/ETF instruments
in real time — public-market absorption patterns, liquidity anomalies, crash precursors, regime shifts — and
detections are tracked against realized market outcomes in a signal→outcome ledger.

> **Informational only — not financial advice.** Fahali detects anomalies; it does not tell you
> or your agent what to buy or sell.

## Tools

### Markets & verdict
| Tool | What it returns | Minimum tier |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `fahali_get_market_decision` | Primary market-wide judgment: what changed, why it matters, horizon, evidence, conflicts, and invalidation | Professional |
| `fahali_get_symbol_decision` | Primary binding judgment for exactly one named instrument | Professional |
| `fahali_get_market_verdict` | Audit-compatible canonical verdict path retained for existing integrations | Professional |
| `fahali_get_market_snapshot` | Live prices, changes, asset class for all instruments | Free |
| `fahali_get_market_regime` | HMM 4-regime detection: bullish/bearish/neutral/high_vol | Professional |
| `fahali_get_market_sentiment` | Sentiment history with score, source, direction | Free |
| `fahali_get_highest_conviction_signals` | Priority risk clusters with risk conviction separated from directional conviction | Free |
| `fahali_daily_brief` | Yesterday vs today market intelligence diff (alert deltas, regime, intel reference) | Free teaser / Professional |

### Risk & crash
| Tool | What it returns | Minimum tier |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `fahali_get_market_risk_score` | Global 0-100 market-risk context from the canonical detection snapshot; not participant or portfolio risk | Professional |
| `fahali_get_flash_crash_risk` | Uncalibrated early-warning strength and triggers; probability/action withheld unless calibrated | Professional |
| `fahali_get_portfolio_risk` | Risk score, VaR, drawdown, per-position breakdown | Elite |
| `fahali_analyze_custom_portfolio` | Stateless risk, canonical direction reconciliation, and covariance coverage for a supplied book; binding action withheld | Elite |
| `fahali_run_shock_test` | Natural-language scenario stress test with capital at risk | Free |

### Detection activity & flow proxies
| Tool | What it returns | Minimum tier |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `fahali_get_detection_activity` | Per-symbol detection counts and bullish-versus-bearish alert-type balance; this is alert activity, not executed trade flow | Professional |
| `fahali_get_unusual_money_movement` | Participant-agnostic, candle-derived buy-versus-sell volume imbalance with conflicts and freshness explicit | Professional |
| `fahali_get_microstructure_proxy` | Absorption observations derived from public aggregate trades and order-book snapshots, with source and limitations explicit | Professional |
| `fahali_get_capital_flow` | Measured 60-minute USD buy-vs-sell imbalance for requested symbols, or the strongest available readings. Candle-derived proxy; zero detector score does not erase measured flow | Professional |
| `fahali_get_forecast` | Crash/pump/neutral probabilities with a p10/p50/p90 uncertainty cone over the registered horizon | Professional |
| `fahali_get_lead_time` | Per engine: measured hours of warning ahead of correct calls, misses included. **Quote `headline`** — selected by recall among strata clearing the publication floor with positive lift. Never cherry-pick; always name the class and horizon | Free |
| `fahali_get_market_briefing` | Full executive market analysis for today; PARTIAL when subsystems disagree | Professional |

### Contagion & correlation
| Tool | What it returns | Minimum tier |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `fahali_get_contagion_map` | Contagion graph with tail-dependence edges and clusters | Elite |
| `fahali_get_correlation_matrix` | Requested-book Pearson matrix from the canonical 45-day covariance artifact, with pair observations and coverage | Free |

### Portfolio & alerts
| Tool | What it returns | Minimum tier |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `fahali_get_portfolio_metrics` | Sentiment momentum, cascade risk, liquidity stress, leverage | Professional |
| `fahali_get_realtime_alerts` | Unified detection feed from the active fleet right now | Professional |

### Persistent monitoring, history & delivery
| Tool | What it returns | Minimum tier |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| `fahali_watch_portfolio` | Durable portfolio + mandate + thresholds; evaluates immediately and continuously | Elite |
| `fahali_list_portfolio_watches` | Existing watches, sources, mandates, cadence and latest verdict IDs | Elite |
| `fahali_update_portfolio_watch` | Update positions or mandate and immediately see the new judgment | Elite |
| `fahali_get_portfolio_decision` | Binding HOLD/WATCH/REDUCE/EXIT judgment with what, why, when and invalidation | Elite |
| `fahali_get_watch_delta` | What changed since the previous immutable judgment and why | Elite |
| `fahali_get_verdict_history` | Cursor- and time-queryable immutable replay, including `as_of` | Elite |
| `fahali_get_verdict_by_id` | One permanent judgment with its evidence and content hashes | Elite |
| `fahali_subscribe_risk` | Signed webhook/callback, Slack, Teams, account email or registered push delivery | Elite |
| `fahali_list_risk_subscriptions` | Delivery configuration and health without exposing secrets | Elite |
| `fahali_update_subscription` | Pause, resume, filter or rotate a delivery target | Elite |
| `fahali_unsubscribe_risk` | Stop delivery while preserving its audit trail | Elite |

The monitor stores only user-scoped positions, mandate and evidence references. Callback
configuration is encrypted. Delivery is deduplicated through a durable outbox, retried afte

readme.markdown:
QueryWeaver (Text2SQL)

**REST API · MCP · Graph-powered** 

QueryWeaver is an **open-source Text2SQL** tool that converts plain-English questions into SQL using **graph-powered schema understanding**. It helps you ask databases natural-language questions and returns SQL and results.

Connect and ask questions: [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-%235865F2.svg?&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/b32KEzMzce)

## Get Started

### Docker

> 💡 Recommended for evaluation purposes (Local Python or Node are not required)
```bash
docker run -p 5000:5000 -it falkordb/queryweaver
```

Launch: http://localhost:5000

---

### Use an .env file (Recommended)

Create a local `.env` by copying `.env.example` and passing it to Docker. This is the simplest way to provide all required configuration:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env to set your values, then:
docker run -p 5000:5000 --env-file .env falkordb/queryweaver
```

### Alternative: Pass individual environment variables

If you prefer to pass variables on the command line, use `-e` flags (less convenient for many variables):

```bash
docker run -p 5000:5000 -it \
  -e APP_ENV=production \
  -e FASTAPI_SECRET_KEY=your_super_secret_key_here \
  -e GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your_google_client_id \
  -e GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your_google_client_secret \
  -e GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=your_github_client_id \
  -e GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=your_github_client_secret \
  -e AZURE_API_KEY=your_azure_api_key \
  falkordb/queryweaver
```

> Note: QueryWeaver supports multiple AI providers. You can use `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `AZURE_API_KEY`. See the [AI/LLM configuration](#aillm-configuration) section for details.

> For a full list of configuration options, consult `.env.example`.

## Memory TTL (optional)

QueryWeaver stores per-user conversation memory in FalkorDB. By default these graphs persist indefinitely. Set `MEMORY_TTL_SECONDS` to apply a Redis TTL (in seconds) so idle memory graphs are automatically cleaned up.

```bash
# Expire memory graphs after 1 week of inactivity
MEMORY_TTL_SECONDS=604800
```

The TTL is refreshed on every user interaction, so active users keep their memory.

## MCP server: host or connect (optional)

QueryWeaver includes optional support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP). You can either have QueryWeaver expose an MCP-compatible HTTP surface (so other services can call QueryWeaver as an MCP server), or configure QueryWeaver to call an external MCP server for model/context services.

What QueryWeaver provides
- The app registers MCP operations focused on Text2SQL flows:
   - `list_databases`
   - `connect_database`
   - `database_schema`
   - `query_database`

- To disable the built-in MCP endpoints set `DISABLE_MCP=true` in your `.env` or environment (default: MCP enabled).
- Configuration

- `DISABLE_MCP` — disable QueryWeaver's built-in MCP HTTP surface. Set to `true` to disable. Default: `false` (MCP enabled).

Examples

Disable the built-in MCP when running with Docker:

```bash
docker run -p 5000:5000 -it --env DISABLE_MCP=true falkordb/queryweaver
```

Calling the built-in MCP endpoints (example)
- The MCP surface is exposed as HTTP endpoints. 

### Server Configuration

Below is a minimal example `mcp.json` client configuration that targets a local QueryWeaver instance exposing the MCP HTTP surface at `/mcp`.

```json
{
   "servers": {
      "queryweaver": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "http://127.0.0.1:5000/mcp",
         "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Bearer your_token_here"
         }
      }
   },
   "inputs": []
}
```

## REST API 

### API Documentation

Swagger UI: https://app.queryweaver.ai/docs

OpenAPI JSON: https://app.queryweaver.ai/openapi.json

### Overview

QueryWeaver exposes a small REST API for managing graphs (database schemas) and running Text2SQL queries. All endpoints that modify or access user-scoped data require authentication via a bearer token. In the browser the app uses session cookies and OAuth flows; for CLI and scripts you can use an API token (see `tokens` routes or the web UI to create one).

Core endpoints
- GET /graphs — list available graphs for the authenticated user
- GET /graphs/{graph_id}/data — return nodes/links (tables, columns, foreign keys) for the graph
- POST /graphs — upload or create a graph (JSON payload or file upload)
- POST /graphs/{graph_id} — run a Text2SQL chat query against the named graph (streaming response)

Authentication
- Add an Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>`

Examples

1) List graphs (GET)

curl example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
   https://app.queryweaver.ai/graphs
```

Python example:

```python
import requests
resp = requests.get('https://app.queryweaver.ai/graphs', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {TOKEN}'})
print(resp.json())
```

2) Get graph schema (GET)

curl example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
   https://app.queryweaver.ai/graphs/my_database/data
```

Python example:

```python
resp = requests.get('https://app.queryweaver.ai/graphs/my_database/data', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {TOKEN}'})
print(resp.json())
```

3) Load a graph (POST) — JSON payload

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   -d '{"database": "my_database", "tables": [...]}' \
   https://app.queryweaver.ai/graphs
```

Or upload a file (multipart/form-data):

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F "file=@schema.json" \
   https://app.queryweaver.ai/graphs
```

4) Query a graph (POST) — run a chat-based Text2SQL request

The `POST /graphs/{graph_id}` endpoint accepts a JSON body with at least a `chat` field (an array of messages). The endpoint streams processing steps and the final SQL back as server-sent-message chunks delimited by a special boundary used by the frontend. For simple scripting you can call it and read the final JSON object from the streamed messages.

# Faxette plugins

Send a fax from Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot. The plugin adds Faxette's MCP server and a `send-a-fax` skill: your agent finds the official fax number, uploads your files and gives you a link to Faxette's status page, where you check the fax and pay to send it. If you're signed in, it can instead send the fax from your Faxette credit once you agree to the price. In an organization, it can also read the faxes your office received, block a sender, and send as the organization on its plan or card. You pay per fax, with no subscription. You don't need an account; if you have one, sign in when your app asks and your faxes stay in it.

Faxette faxes to the US, Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico, Costa Rica, the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Montenegro, Ukraine and the Isle of Man.

## Install

Claude Code:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
claude plugin install faxette@faxette
```

Codex:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
```

Then open `/plugins` in Codex, switch to the Faxette marketplace and install Faxette. Start a new session to use it.

GitHub Copilot CLI:

```sh
copilot plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
copilot plugin install faxette@faxette
```

VS Code finds plugins you install with Copilot CLI. Without the CLI, run **Chat: Open Customizations**, add the `goosegods/faxette-plugins` marketplace under **Browse → Configure Marketplaces**, and install Faxette.

Then ask, for example: "Please fax referral.pdf to Dr. Lee's office."

## Only the connectors

Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP clients can connect directly, without the skill, at `https://mcp.faxette.com/mcp`. It faxes to the US, Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico, Costa Rica, the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Montenegro, Ukraine and the Isle of Man.

Setup steps for each app are on [faxette.com/mcp](https://faxette.com/mcp).

## What's inside

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `plugins/faxette/skills/send-a-fax/SKILL.md` | How the agent finds the number, uploads files and hands over the status page |
| `plugins/faxette/.mcp.json` | The MCP server, for Claude Code |
| `plugins/faxette/mcp.json`, `plugin.json` | The same plugin in the Agent Plugins format, for Codex and GitHub Copilot |
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | The Claude Code and GitHub Copilot marketplace |
| `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | The Codex marketplace |
| `registry/server.json` | The server's entry in the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) |

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_capabilities` | Each copy's countries, languages, file limits and prices |
| `lookup_fax_number` | Searches Faxette's checked directory for an office's fax number, with its official source |
| `create_document` | Reserves an upload for one file (PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC, up to 20 MB) and returns a URL to PUT it to |
| `create_fax` | Creates the fax, optionally with text or Markdown printed as pages and a cover page, and returns its `status_url`, where the person checks it and pays |
| `get_fax_status` | Reads a fax from its `status_url`: status, pages, price, payment and attempts |
| `resend_fax` | Resends a failed fax, optionally to a corrected number, with the same payment |
| `get_fax_report` | A delivery report for a finished fax |
| `get_account` | Shows which Faxette account is signed in. Needs sign-in |
| `get_faxes` | Lists the account's faxes, 25 at a time, newest first, with a status filter. Needs sign-in |
| `get_fax` | One of the account's faxes, with its documents' file names, history and the quote to approve. Needs sign-in |
| `open_fax_review` | Shows the exact PDF that will be faxed, in apps that can show interactive screens, or as a review link. Needs sign-in |
| `send_fax` | Sends one of the account's faxes, paid from its credit, once the person approves that exact fax and price. For an organization's fax, pays with its plan or holds the amount on its card. Needs sign-in |
| `get_organizations` | The organizations the person let the app use, with each one's plan and fax numbers. Needs sign-in |
| `get_inbound_faxes` | Lists the faxes an organization received, 25 at a time, newest first, with an unread filter. Needs sign-in |
| `get_inbound_fax` | One received fax, with a link to its PDF for 5 minutes. Marks it read. Needs sign-in |
| `read_inbound_fax` | A received fax's pages as images, up to 10, to read or summarize it. Marks it read. Needs sign-in |
| `get_blocked_senders` | Lists the numbers an organization blocked, 25 at a time. Needs sign-in |
| `block_sender` | Blocks a number for the organization: its future faxes are deleted as they arrive, and nobody is emailed. Needs sign-in |
| `unblock_sender` | Lets a blocked number's faxes reach the organization again. Needs sign-in |

Signing in is optional. The connector asks your app to sign you in the first time a tool needs it, through `www.faxette.com`, which sends European accounts on to `eu.faxette.com`. When you connect, you choose which of your organizations the app can use; reconnect to change that. Disconnect an app any time in Settings → Connected apps.

Nothing is sent or charged without the person's agreement. Guests pay on the status page, which shows the fax number, documents and price first. Signed in, the agent can send a fax from the person's credit: it shows them the exact PDF and price and waits for their yes before calling `send_fax`, and Faxette refuses the send if the fax or its price changed since.

## Privacy and support

- Files you send go straight from your computer to Faxette's file storage: `create_document` returns a short-lived upload link and the skill uploads the file to it. Everything else goes through Faxette's MCP servers.
- Privacy policy: [faxette.com/legal/privacy](https://faxette.com/legal/privacy)
- Terms: [faxette.com/legal/terms](https://faxette.com/legal/terms)
- Support

# FERS: structural analysis in Python

FERS: structural finite-element analysis (3D frames, trusses, plates, Eurocode 3
checks) for engineers and AI agents. This is its Python SDK and the `fers`
command. The solver is a compiled engine that runs on your machine, with no
account and no network call: free for non-commercial use up to 100 members.
This SDK is open source (BSD-3-Clause) at
[github.com/Jeroen124/FERS_core](https://github.com/Jeroen124/FERS_core); the
engine's licence is under [Licence](#licence).

It computes linear and second-order (P-Delta) static analysis, natural
frequencies, elastic buckling load factors (α_cr), response-spectrum seismic
analysis, and EN 1993-1-1 steel member checks, flexural and lateral-torsional
buckling included. A model is JSON in and JSON out, written from Python, by the
`fers` command, or by an AI agent through the
[FERS MCP server](https://ferscloud.com/mcp), the Claude Code plugin or the
agent skill.

```bash
pip install FERS
```

```python
from fers_core import check_beam

# IPE200 in S235, simply supported over 6 m, 10 kN/m. SI units: m, N, Pa.
# check_beam adds an EN 1993-1-1 member check on a ULS combination of 1.35 x the load.
model = check_beam(6.0, "IPE200", udl=10_000.0)
model.settings.analysis_options.include_member_deflected_shape = True
model.run_analysis()

beam = model.resultsbundle.loadcases["Q"].member_results["1"]
x_frac, (_, dy, _) = beam.member_displacement_peak
ec3 = model.unity_check_results()[0]
print(f"M {beam.local_minimums.mz / 1e3:.1f} kNm, sag {dy * 1e3:.1f} mm at x/L {x_frac:.2f}")
print(f"EC3 utilization {ec3['max_utilization']:.2f}")
```

```text
M -45.0 kNm, sag -41.8 mm at x/L 0.50
EC3 utilization 2.85
```

The sag is 41.3 mm of bending (5wL⁴/384EI) plus 0.4 mm of shear deformation,
which the engine includes. The beam fails: the ULS moment of 60.75 kNm exceeds
its bending resistance of 51.9 kNm, and with nothing restraining its compression
flange, lateral-torsional buckling takes the utilization to 2.85.

- **Agents and scripts:** `fers solve`, `fers check` and `fers validate` take a
  model JSON file, print one line (or `--json`) and say in their exit code
  whether the numbers can be used; see [From the terminal and from coding
  agents](#from-the-terminal-and-from-coding-agents). `fers skill --install .`
  gives a coding agent the FERS skill, and MCP clients can use the
  [FERS MCP server](https://ferscloud.com/mcp). In Claude Code, both come as one
  plugin: `/plugin install fers --marketplace Jeroen124/FERS_core`.
- **Extras:** plots (`pip install "FERS[plot]"`), section properties meshed from
  your own dimensions (`"FERS[sections]"`) and DXF import (`"FERS[dxf]"`);
  `"FERS[all]"` installs everything 0.1.x did. Catalogue sections (`IPE200`,
  `HEB300`, `UB 457x191x67`, `W14X30`, ...) need no extra.
- **Licence:** the SDK is BSD-3-Clause; the engine it installs is free for
  non-commercial use ([Licence](#licence)).

## Solving a model

Building a model by hand, create the `FERS` object first, then its nodes,
members and loads. Creating a `FERS` restarts the id counters, so a node made
before it would share an id with one made after it, and the solver refuses
node ids that do not run from 1 without gaps.

## Reading results

`run_analysis()` puts the results on `model.resultsbundle`. Load cases and load
combinations are keyed by name. Within each, nodes and members are keyed by
their id as a string, because results round-trip through JSON.

```python
case = model.resultsbundle.loadcases["Load"]    # or .loadcombinations["ULS 1"]

case.displacement_nodes["5"].dy                  # dx dy dz rx ry rz warp
case.reaction_nodes["1"].nodal_forces.fy         # fx fy fz mx my mz bw
beam = case.member_results["4"]
beam.local_maximums.mz, beam.local_minimums.mz   # envelope along the member
beam.local_start_forces.fy                       # end forces, member axes
```

`start_node_forces`, `end_node_forces`, `maximums` and `minimums` are in the
global frame; the `local_*` forces, `section_forces` and `internal_force_series`
are in the member's own axes, with `mz` the strong-axis moment. Read a frame's
moments from the local ones: outside the XY plane the global `mz` is not the
bending moment, and in a frame in the YZ plane it reads 0.

Since 0.1.98, `member_results` and `displacement_nodes` are read-only tables
rather than dicts of objects. That is what keeps a large result small in
memory. They read like dicts: `[]`, `get`, `in`, `len`, `.items()`, and
iteration in the solver's order. Each lookup builds a fresh object, and nothing
in it can be changed:

```python
beam.local_maximums.mz = 0.0                     # AttributeError: read-only
editable = case.member_results.copy()            # a plain dict of editable objects
editable["4"].local_maximums.mz = 0.0            # fine
```

`section_forces`, `internal_force_series` and `member_displacements` come back
as tuples. To test for a table, use `isinstance(x, collections.abc.Mapping)`,
not `dict`. `reaction_nodes` and `plate_results` are plain dicts, as before.

### Saving and loading

```python
from fers_core import FERS

model.save_to_json("beam.json")                  # the model and its results
model = FERS.from_json("beam.json")
```

`FERS.from_json` reads any file the solver or the SDK wrote, one entry at a
time. A typical result needs less memory than its file to load, and at most
about twice the file's size; before 0.1.98 it needed 15 to 20 times. For a
large model, let the solver write the file itself. The result then never
passes through Python as one string:

```python
model.run_analysis_to_file("beam_results.json")
solved = FERS.from_json("beam_results.json")
```

`fers_core/examples/809_Reading_Results.py` runs all of this end to end.

Saving a loaded model writes back everything the solver reads, with the same
ids. That includes what the file defines but nothing uses yet, such as a section
an editor keeps in its library. Nodes, members and the rest created

readme.markdown:
# Figma MCP Server Guide

The Figma MCP server brings Figma directly into your workflow by providing important design information and context to AI agents generating code from Figma design files.

> [!NOTE]
> Rate limits apply to Figma MCP server tools that read data from Figma. Some tools, such as those that write to Figma files, are exempt from the rate limits.
> 
> Users on the Starter plan or with View or Collab seats on paid plans will be limited to up to 6 tool calls per month.
> 
> Users with a [Dev or Full seat](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/27468498501527-Updates-to-Figma-s-pricing-seats-and-billing-experience#h_01JCPBM8X2MBEXTABDM92HWZG4) on the [Professional, Organization, or Enterprise plans](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273-Figma-plans-and-features) have per minute rate limits, which follow the same limits as the Tier 1 [Figma REST API](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/rate-limits/). As with Figma’s REST API, Figma reserves the right to change rate limits.

For the complete set of Figma MCP server docs, see our [developer documentation](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/). By using the Figma MCP server and the related resources (including these skills), you agree to the [Figma Developer Terms](https://www.figma.com/legal/developer-terms/). These skills are currently available as a Beta feature.

## Features

- **Write to the canvas** (remote server only): Create and modify native Figma content directly from your MCP client. With the right skills, agents can build and update frames, components, variables, and auto layout in your Figma files using your design system as the source of truth.

    **Note:** We're quickly improving how Figma supports AI agents. The write to canvas feature will eventually be a usage-based paid feature, but is currently available for free during the beta period.

- **Generate placeholder images**: When source, captured, or library images are unavailable, agents can use `generate_image` after asking permission and disclosing Figma AI credit usage. Generated images are uploaded with `upload_assets` and applied to the design.

- **Generate code from selected frames**

  Select a Figma frame and turn it into code. Great for product teams building new flows or iterating on app features.

- **Extract design context**

  Pull in variables, components, and layout data directly into your IDE. This is especially useful for design systems and component-based workflows.

- **Code smarter with Code Connect**

  Boost output quality by reusing your actual components. Code Connect keeps your generated code consistent with your codebase.

  [Learn more about Code Connect →](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/23920389749655-Code-Connect)

- **Generate Figma designs from web pages** *(rolling out)*

  Capture, import, or convert a web page into a Figma design directly from your AI coding agent.

## Installation & Setup

### Connect to the Figma MCP server

Different MCP clients require slightly different setups. Follow the instructions below for your specific client to connect to the Figma MCP server.

#### VS Code

1. Use the shortcut `⌘ Shift P` to search for `MCP:Add Server`.
2. Select `HTTP`.
3. Paste the server url `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp` in the search bar. Then hit `Enter`.
4. When you're prompted for a server ID, enter `figma`.
5. Select whether you want to add this server globally or only for the current workspace. Once confirmed, you'll see a configuration like this in your `mcp.json` file:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "figma": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

6. Open the chat toolbar using `⌥⌘B` or `⌃⌘I` and switch to **Agent** mode.
7. With the chat open, type in `#get_design_context` to confirm that the Figma MCP server tools are available. If no tools are listed, restart VS Code.

> [!NOTE]
> You must have [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) enabled on your account to use MCP in VS Code.
>
> For more information, see [VS Code's official documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers).

#### Cursor

The recommended way to set up the Figma MCP server in Cursor is by installing the Figma Plugin, which includes MCP server settings as well as Agent Skills for common workflows.

Install the plugin by typing the following command in Cursor's agent chat:

```
/add-plugin figma
```

The plugin includes:

- MCP server configuration for the Figma MCP server
- Skills for implementing designs, connecting components via Code Connect, and creating design system rules
- Rules for proper asset handling from the Figma MCP server

<details>
<summary>Manual setup</summary>

1. Open **Cursor → Settings → Cursor Settings**.
2. Go to the **MCP** tab.
3. Click **+ Add new global MCP server**.
4. Enter the following configuration and save:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "figma": {
      "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

For more information, see [Cursor's official documentation](https://docs.cursor.com/context/model-context-protocol).

</details>

#### Claude Code

The recommended way to set up the Figma MCP server in Claude Code is by installing the Figma Plugin, which includes MCP server settings as well as Agent Skills for common workflows.

Run the following command to install the plugin from Anthropic's official plugin marketplace.

```bash
claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official
```

Learn more about Anthropic's [Claude Code Plugins](https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-plugins) and [Agent Skills](https://claude.com/blog/skills).

readme.markdown:
# mcps

**MCP servers that let an AI assistant do a company's everyday work.** Most are
for services people use anywhere, such as Google Workspace, Notion, Bitwarden,
Porkbun, Expo, the app stores and European banks; a second line is for
companies in Romania, to file with ANAF, follow the trade register, invoice
through Oblio and read the National Bank's rates.

Each server connects an MCP client, such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, VS Code
or Cursor, to one service. They are built on one toolkit, so every tool says
what it can change: `read` (it changes nothing), `write` (it changes something
in your account) or `money` (it moves money, makes or unmakes a legal or fiscal
document, or commits you in a comparable way, such as a bank consent). Your
client asks you before each `money` call.

[foreverworks.github.io/mcps](https://foreverworks.github.io/mcps/) presents the servers by who they are for, each with its documentation.

Under each server's name: how settled it is, then how many tools it has and the most they can do. **Stable**: in daily use, and its tools keep their shape. **Beta**: in use, and new or still growing, or reading web pages its service may change. **Experimental**: rests on an interface its owner may change without notice, or covers part of the service.

## For companies in Romania

The paperwork a company in Romania, and the people who run it, do online: e-invoices and declarations with ANAF, filings at the trade register, invoicing, and the National Bank's exchange rates. Each README ends with the other servers we found for that service, and what this one adds.

| Server | What it does |
|---|---|
| [ ANAF e-Factura](servers/anaf-efactura)<sub>Stable20 tools, including **money**</sub> | Read, check and file a Romanian company's e-invoices and e-Transport declarations with ANAF. |
| [ ANAF SPV](servers/anaf-spv)<sub>Beta16 tools, including **money**</sub> | Download what ANAF posts to your SPV inbox, request documents, and validate or file declarations. |
| [ BNR exchange rates](servers/bnr)<sub>Stable5 tools, read-only</sub> | Look up the National Bank of Romania's rate for any day, and convert amounts to and from RON. |
| [ Oblio](servers/oblio)<sub>Stable17 tools, including **money**</sub> | Issue and track a Romanian company's invoices on Oblio, with totals computed as ANAF checks them. |
| [ ONRC trade register](servers/onrc)<sub>Beta9 tools, read and write</sub> | Follow your filings at Romania's trade register, with their documents, fee notes and invoices. |

## For everyone

Servers for services people use anywhere. We built each one because the servers we found did less, or there were none; each README's last section names them and says what this one adds.

| Server | What it does |
|---|---|
| [ App Store and Google Play](servers/app-stores)<sub>Beta7 tools, read and write</sub> | Read and answer App Store and Google Play reviews, and see TestFlight feedback and crash logs. |
| [ Bitwarden](servers/bitwarden)<sub>Stable17 tools, read and write</sub> | Give your assistant its own Bitwarden vault for logins, passwords, 2FA codes and passkeys. |
| [ Expo Application Services](servers/eas)<sub>Beta23 tools, including **money**</sub> | Find out why an Expo build, workflow run or store submission failed, and roll out updates. |
| [ Enable Banking](servers/enable-banking)<sub>Stable10 tools, including **money**</sub> | Read, search and export statements and balances from banks across Europe, without moving money. |
| [ Google Workspace](servers/google)<sub>Stable115 tools, read and write</sub> | Search and work in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides across several Google accounts. |
| [ Home Assistant](servers/home-assistant)<sub>Beta10 tools, read and write</sub> | Read your Home Assistant's states, areas and history, and run its actions, approving locks first. |
| [ Notion](servers/notion)<sub>Stable27 tools, read and write</sub> | Search, read and write your Notion workspaces, with pages as Markdown and typed database queries. |
| [ Porkbun](servers/porkbun)<sub>Beta113 tools, including **money**</sub> | Register domains and manage DNS, hosting and mail at Porkbun, with every purchase confirmed first. |
| [ Trademark search](servers/trademarks)<sub>Beta6 tools, read-only</sub> | Check whether a name is already a registered or pending trademark in the US or the EU. |
| [ TypeSafe](servers/typesafe)<sub>Beta3 tools, read-only</sub> | Get calibrated yes or no answers, choices and scores from TypeSafe's Jev, for one item or 1000 rows. |

## Extras

These run from a clone of this repository and are not published to npm, the MCP Registry or as desktop bundles. Each README has the install steps and what the server needs.

| Server | What it does |
|---|---|
| [ Bolt Food receipts](servers/bolt-food)<sub>Experimental8 tools, read-only</sub> | Read your Bolt Food orders as itemised receipts matched to card charges, through an unofficial API. |
| [ Device broker](servers/devices)<sub>Experimental10 tools, read and write</sub> | Share your own Android emulators, iOS simulators and desktops between AI agents, in fair turns. |
| [ Glovo receipts](servers/glovo)<sub>Experimental8 tools, read-only</sub> | Read your Glovo orders as itemised receipts matched to card charges, through an unofficial API. |
| [ Printer and scanner](servers/printer)<sub>Experimental10 tools, read and write</sub> | Print, scan and check paper and toner on a network printer, with greys corrected for that printer. |
| [ Local RAG](servers/rag)<sub>Beta10 tools, read and write</sub> | Index your PDFs, scans and documents locally, and search them with hybrid retrieval and a reranker. |
| [ Smart home](servers/smart-home)<sub>Experimental7 tools, read and write</sub> | Press the buttons of a TV, heater or fan remote by name through a BroadLink IR blaster. |

## Shared packages

|---|---|
| [mcp-kit](packages/mcp-kit) | Stdio and HTTP transports with per-client tokens,

# @getplexa/mcp — Plexa MCP server

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that gives any MCP client
(Claude Desktop, Cursor, your own agent) two economic-safety tools from **[Plexa](https://getplexa.com)** —
the x402-native **economic-safety layer for trading agents** — paid per call in USDC, no accounts:

| Tool | Wraps | Price | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plexa_quote` | `POST /v1/quote` | $0.02 | **Executable** fill price under size (not mid/spot), price impact (bps), realizable depth, per-leg route, worst-case slippage, confidence — from canonical on-chain quoters on Base, Polygon & Arbitrum. |
| `plexa_pretrade_check` | `POST /v1/pretrade/check` | $0.05 | Two levels. **`verdict`**: `avoid` only when a listed trap is *proven* on-chain at that block (no pool to exit into · the counter-asset pot is under 5% of your size, and the pot is a hard upper bound on what a sale can return · the token's own trading gate is off), `clear` otherwise — `clear` means *no provable trap*, **not** "safe". **`risk_profile`**: age, holder concentration, liquidity depth incl. `exitLiquidityUsd`, oracle availability, transfer limits — as data you weigh, not as a rating. Plus reasons, confidence and an executable quote. (Base-only today.) |

It is a **thin client of the public API** (`https://api.getplexa.com`) — it pays a `402` automatically,
signs the USDC authorization **locally** with your wallet, and never sees your key. The liquidity engine
stays behind the API.

---

## Why

A generic wallet guard answers *"can I sign this transaction?"*. It can't answer the **economic**
question an automated trader actually needs: *what price will this swap really fill at under my size,
and is this token a trap (rug / honeypot / thin liquidity)?* Plexa answers both. This package puts those
answers one tool-call away inside any MCP-speaking agent.

---

## Install

Nothing to install — point your MCP client at the package via `npx`. It is fetched and run on demand.

### Claude Desktop

Add to `claude_desktop_config.json` (**Settings → Developer → Edit Config**):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "plexa": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@getplexa/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "PLEXA_BASE_URL": "https://api.getplexa.com",
        "AGENT_WALLET_KEY": "0x<your funded wallet private key>",
        "CHAIN": "base"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or **Settings → MCP → Add**) — the same `mcpServers` block as above.

Restart the client. You should see the `plexa_quote` and `plexa_pretrade_check` tools available.

---

## Configuration

All configuration is via environment variables (set in the `env` block of your MCP config):

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `PLEXA_BASE_URL` | `https://api.getplexa.com` | The public API. The real URL — not a secret. |
| `AGENT_WALLET_KEY` | *(none)* | **Required to pay.** Funded wallet private key — pays per call and signs locally. Plexa never receives it. Without it, tools return a clear `402`. |
| `CHAIN` | `base` | `base` \| `polygon` \| `arbitrum` (aliases `matic`, `arb`, `arbitrum-one` and CAIP-2 `eip155:8453`/`137`/`42161` also work; case is normalized). The chain your wallet is funded on; quotes and payment default to it. `plexa_pretrade_check` is Base-only today — other chains answer 422. |

**Funding.** Use a **dedicated, low-balance wallet** with a little USDC on `CHAIN` to pay per call
(quotes $0.02, checks $0.05). The wallet signs an EIP-3009 USDC authorization per request; Plexa returns
the result only after the payment settles on-chain (**settle-before-serve**).

> Your key is a secret. Prefer your MCP client's secret storage if it has one. Never commit it.

---

## How payment works (x402 in MCP)

MCP has no native payment. This server acts as an **x402 client**: it wraps `fetch`, so when Plexa
replies `402 Payment Required` it reads the payment requirements, signs a USDC authorization with your
wallet (locally), and retries. The signed authorization is the only thing that leaves your machine —
**never the key**. Payment is made on `CHAIN`, so you fund **one wallet on one chain**.

If no `AGENT_WALLET_KEY` is set, the tools return an honest `402` error explaining a funded wallet is
needed — they never fabricate a result.

---

## Example

Once configured, just ask your agent naturally — it will call the tools:

> *"Before I buy this token `0x…` on Base, check it with Plexa and get me an executable quote for $500."*

The agent calls `plexa_pretrade_check` (verdict + reasons) and `plexa_quote` (executable price under
$500), pays $0.05 + $0.02 in USDC automatically, and answers with real on-chain economics.

## What comes back

Beyond `verdict` / `triggers` / `risk_profile` / `liquidityCoverage`, every pre-trade
response carries six blocks of context. Live capture, WETH, **2026-08-20T14:46:29Z**, Base block
**50223921** — the `note` string each block carries is long and is cut here, nothing else is:

readme.markdown:
# SPM Agent Connectors

Public connector package for SPM - Structured Project Memory.

SPM turns project knowledge into durable, shareable, governed and internally
smart project memory for AI agents. This repository contains only the public
connector surface: the authenticated remote MCP configuration, installable
bundles for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and OpenClaw, browser authorization
helpers, lifecycle adapters, examples and security guidance.

The SPM application, backend, billing system, private console, memory engine and
infrastructure are not included in this repository.

## Hosted MCP Endpoint

Human setup and inspection guide:

```text
https://getspm.com/agents
```

```text
https://getspm.com/v1/mcp
```

Official MCP Registry descriptor:

```text
server.json
```

Registry name:

```text
com.getspm/spm
```

The endpoint is public for discovery, but authenticated for use. A client needs:

- an SPM account;
- an organization and at least one project;
- a trial or paid plan;
- an SPM token authorized for one project, a selected project set or the
  projects the user may access in an organization.

## What Agents Can Do

Connector profiles expose the agent-facing SPM surface:

- use durable project memory across chats, runs and tools;
- resolve the active project without confusing it with other authorized
  projects;
- list authorized projects and compose cross-project context only when the
  user explicitly requests it;
- work with smart memory packs that preserve requirements, current decisions,
  completed work, source-backed context and temporal signals;
- query temporal project memory;
- request scoped context packs;
- verify context pack provenance and hashes;
- query context graphs and boundaries;
- run policy-aware preflight checks;
- report completed actions, tests, evidence and decisions;
- submit agent lifecycle turns to LLM-first memory triage with source
  provenance, when the client supports lifecycle hooks.
- choose selective, complete redacted, summaries-only or metadata-only source
  capture independently from the memory that triage promotes for future use;
- inspect and verify an append-ordered capture journal without exposing retained
  conversation bodies to agent tools.
- propose a source-grounded project-memory bootstrap when no authorized project
  matches, request only the specific authorized evidence still needed, then wait
  for the user to create, link or skip it in SPM;
- continue an authorized project in another agent or device through a
  short-lived one-time handoff that carries references rather than memory bodies
  or credentials;
- compare body-free workspace manifests before a handoff: Git identity,
  revision and local-state hash; non-Git file or document snapshots; remote
  version references; or memory-only work;
- refresh workspace manifests automatically at session start, before user
  turns and after completed work when the client supports lifecycle hooks,
  making stale observations and out-of-band changes visible without uploading
  local file bodies;
- distinguish metadata-only source observations from material evidence and
  request an authorized source handoff when current content is required.

## Typical Use Cases

- Coding agents receive the project memory they should actually use before
  changing code: requirements, current decisions, tests, constraints and
  completed work.
- Delivery teams turn scattered project knowledge into scoped packs for
  engineers, clients, partners or support without exposing the whole project.
- Partners or external collaborators receive bounded memory with source,
  expiry, revocation, provenance and audit evidence.
- Agent workflows preserve memory after the task by reporting decisions, tests
  and evidence back to SPM.

## What Agents Cannot Do

The hosted MCP connector does not expose:

- billing or checkout;
- invoice payment;
- customer portal creation;
- destructive tenant administration;
- raw secrets;
- global operator tools.

This boundary is intentional. Agents receive the memory tools they need without
being given commercial or destructive administrative powers.

## Codex

Install the Codex plugin from this repository marketplace:

```text
.agents/plugins/marketplace.json
```

Or configure Codex manually:

```toml
[mcp_servers.spm]
url = "https://getspm.com/v1/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "SPM_CODEX_MCP_TOKEN"
startup_timeout_sec = 30
tool_timeout_sec = 120
```

Authorize Codex for all projects the signed-in organization user may access:

```bash
python3 plugins/spm-codex/scripts/auth_spm_codex.py \
  --project-id <authorization-project-id> \
  --access-mode organization \
  --write-env ~/.spm/codex.env
source ~/.spm/codex.env
```

Verify:

```bash
python3 plugins/spm-codex/scripts/doctor_spm_codex.py
```

Run the functional remote MCP smoke:

```bash
python3 plugins/spm-codex/scripts/smoke_spm_remote_mcp.py \
  --project-id <authorized-project-id>
```

The smoke uses the same `SPM_CODEX_MCP_TOKEN` as Codex and requires an
explicit authorized project id (or `SPM_SMOKE_PROJECT_ID`). It initializes the
hosted MCP endpoint, verifies the project-resolution, multi-project,
agent-session and memory tool surface, creates a small project-scoped smoke
memory event, reads temporal state, creates and verifies a context pack, queries
the context graph, runs agent preflight and reports post-action evidence. It
never prints the token and the hosted connector strips raw event bodies from
returned context.

For a non-mutating token check, use:

```bash
python3 plugins/spm-codex/scripts/smoke_spm_remote_mcp.py \
  --project-id <authorized-project-id> --read-only
```

## Claude Code, Cursor And OpenClaw

The repository includes native client bundles:

- `plugins/spm-claude`
- `plugins/spm-cursor`
- `plugins/spm-openclaw`

Clients that only support MCP can use the same remote endpoint and bearer
token. The generic authorization helper is
`scripts/agent-connectors/authorize_spm_agent.py`. See also:
