readme.markdown:
# GitHubCard MCP server

Let your AI assistant create [GitHubCard](https://githubcard.com) images: profile
and repository cards for READMEs, link previews and social posts, with live
GitHub data.

- **Hosted:** `https://githubcard.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Nothing to install.
- **Local:** `npx -y @ghcardhq/ghcard mcp` (stdio), from the
  [`ghcard` CLI](https://github.com/ghcardhq/ghcard). It can also edit a README on
  your disk.

Ask things like:

> Make a GitHubCard for my profile and add it near the top of my README.
>
> Create a dark card for `vercel/next.js` I can use as a link preview.
>
> Use the compact repo template, but with a `#1e3a5f` background and without the
> language widget.

## Get an API key

Creating cards needs a free API key. Sign in at
[githubcard.com/dashboard](https://githubcard.com/dashboard) and create one under
**API keys**. It looks like `ghc_live_…`.

Without a key, the server still lists templates, palettes, widget types, and
template designs, so you can try it before signing up.

## Setup

Replace `ghc_live_…` with your key in the examples below.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http githubcard https://githubcard.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ghc_live_…"
```

There is also a Claude Code plugin that adds the server together with a
GitHubCard skill: see [ghcardhq/skills](https://github.com/ghcardhq/skills).

### Claude Desktop

Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector**, URL
`https://githubcard.com/mcp`. Custom headers are not available there yet, so to
pass your key, use the local server in `claude_desktop_config.json` instead:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "githubcard": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@ghcardhq/ghcard", "mcp"],
      "env": { "GHCARD_API_KEY": "ghc_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Cursor

`~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "githubcard": {
      "url": "https://githubcard.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ghc_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

`.vscode/mcp.json` (VS Code asks for the key once and stores it securely):

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "id": "githubcard-key",
      "type": "promptString",
      "description": "GitHubCard API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "githubcard": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://githubcard.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:githubcard-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Windsurf

`~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "githubcard": {
      "serverUrl": "https://githubcard.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ghc_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex CLI

`~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.githubcard]
url = "https://githubcard.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "GHCARD_API_KEY"
```

Then export `GHCARD_API_KEY=ghc_live_…` in your shell.

### Gemini CLI

Install the extension from this repository. Gemini CLI asks for the optional
API key during setup and stores it as a sensitive setting:

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/ghcardhq/githubcard-mcp
```

### Any other client

Remote: Streamable HTTP at `https://githubcard.com/mcp`, header
`Authorization: Bearer ghc_live_…`.

Local (stdio): command `npx`, args `["-y", "@ghcardhq/ghcard", "mcp"]`, env
`GHCARD_API_KEY`. Add `--allow-file-writes` to the args to enable
`update_readme`. Needs Node.js 20 or later.

## Tools

| Tool | Key | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_card` | yes | Create (or reuse) a card for a user, `owner/repo`, or GitHub URL. Returns SVG/PNG links and Markdown/HTML embed snippets. Uses one unit of the daily quota |
| `validate_card` | yes | Dry run of `create_card`: checks ids, Pro features and custom designs, uses no quota |
| `list_templates` | no | Layouts, filterable by scope (profile/repo), Free plan and widget types |
| `list_palettes` | no | Background palettes |
| `list_components` | no | Widget types a card can contain |
| `get_template_design` | no | A template's layout as an editable design document. Pass `subject` for a repo template |
| `get_card_design` | yes | The design document of one of your cards |
| `list_cards` | yes | Cards you have created |
| `delete_card` | yes | Delete a card; its links stop working |
| `get_usage` | yes | Your plan and today's remaining quota |
| `update_readme` | local only | Insert or update the card in a Markdown file. Only with `ghcard mcp --allow-file-writes` |

`create_card` is idempotent: the same inputs return the same card and link. Card
images always show current GitHub data, so there is no need to recreate them.

Failed calls return `isError: true` with a stable `code`, a `retryable` flag
and a `hint` telling the model what to do next.

## Limits

| Plan | Cards per day |
| --- | --- |
| Free | 100 |
| Pro | 5000 |

The quota resets at 00:00 UTC. Failed calls are not counted. Free cards carry a
small watermark. See [pricing](https://githubcard.com/~pricing).

## Links

- [githubcard.com](https://githubcard.com): the editor and gallery
- [ghcardhq/ghcard](https://github.com/ghcardhq/ghcard): the CLI and local MCP server
- [ghcardhq/skills](https://github.com/ghcardhq/skills): Claude Code plugin and skill
- [`server.json`](server.json): the entry in the
  [MCP registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io), as `com.githubcard/mcp`

## License

MIT

# GoAI Moat — AI Visibility MCP (thin relay)

Multi-model **AI visibility audit** for any website or brand — ChatGPT (consumer app), Perplexity, and Grok, plus GEO/SEO health and a 0–100 score with benchmark percentile.

**Thin relay by design**: this MCP holds **no API keys, no billing logic, and makes no direct upstream calls**. It forwards your request (with your `api_key` / `license_key` / `email`) to the GoAI Moat server, which holds all credentials and enforces access and quota. The MCP is only the request-initiating interface.

## Tools

- `audit_ai_visibility(url, api_key=..., license_key=..., email=...)` — full audit: multi-model AI mentions + GEO/SEO health + 0–100 score + benchmark percentile + prioritized issues.
- `check_ai_mentions(brand, api_key=..., email=...)` — quick check: what ChatGPT / Perplexity / Grok say about a brand.
- `check_license(license_key, email=...)` — activate a license and receive your api_key.

## Pricing

- **Free**: 3 audits per email.
- **Subscription**: `$98/month`. Activate via `check_license`.

## Run locally (stdio)

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python server.py
```

No credentials are needed here — authentication, quota, and the actual audit all live on the GoAI Moat server. The server returns a clear error if your api_key/license/email is missing or exhausted.

## Hosted endpoint

```
https://ai-visibility.mcp.goaimoat.com/mcp
```

## License

MIT

readme.markdown:
# Goldsky Docs MCP server

A remote MCP server that lets AI assistants search and read the [Goldsky documentation](https://docs.goldsky.com). Goldsky provides onchain data for apps and finance teams: Feeds (REST APIs for wallet balances and transfers, token prices, Polymarket prediction-market data, and block data, payable per request with x402), prebuilt onchain datasets, Turbo pipelines, Subgraphs, Mirror, and Edge RPC across 150+ chains.

- Endpoint: `https://docs.goldsky.com/mcp`
- Transport: Streamable HTTP
- Authentication: none. No API key or account is needed.
- MCP Registry name: `com.goldsky/docs`

The server reads public documentation only. It does not access your Goldsky account, wallets, or data. To use the products the docs describe, create a Goldsky account and API key at [app.goldsky.com](https://app.goldsky.com).

This repository holds the listing README only. The server is hosted by Goldsky.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search_goldsky` | Searches the Goldsky docs and returns matching pages with titles and links. |
| `query_docs_filesystem_goldsky` | Reads full doc pages, including code samples and API references. |
| `submit_feedback` | Reports a problem with a docs page (missing, wrong, or out of date). |

## Configure

### VS Code and GitHub Copilot

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json` in your workspace, or run **MCP: Add Server** from the command palette:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "goldsky-docs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://docs.goldsky.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http goldsky-docs https://docs.goldsky.com/mcp
```

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "goldsky-docs": {
      "url": "https://docs.goldsky.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Other clients

Any client that supports remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP can connect to `https://docs.goldsky.com/mcp` with no authentication. See [docs.goldsky.com/mcp-server](https://docs.goldsky.com/mcp-server) for more clients.

## Use

Ask your assistant a Goldsky question. It calls the docs tools and answers with links to the pages it used. Examples:

- "How do I get a wallet's token balances with Goldsky Feeds?"
- "How do I get a wallet's Polymarket positions with Goldsky Feeds?"
- "How do I send a Turbo pipeline's output to a Postgres database?"
- "How do I migrate my subgraph from The Graph to Goldsky?"
- "How much does Goldsky Edge RPC cost?"

## Related

- [goldsky-agent](https://github.com/goldsky-io/goldsky-agent): the Goldsky plugin for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI. It adds skills for building pipelines, subgraphs, and RPC setups, and includes this docs server.
- [Goldsky docs](https://docs.goldsky.com)
- Support: [docs.goldsky.com/getting-support](https://docs.goldsky.com/getting-support)

Returns booking counts per UTC day for one gym, whatever their status, for any window of at most 31 days (the next 7 by default); counting stops at 100. Not for counting cancellations or seeing which members are booked.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of one of the user's gyms, as the gym list returns it (24 lowercase hex characters)

inputs.name: startTime
inputs.description: Start of the range as an ISO 8601 date-time; defaults to now

inputs.name: endTime
inputs.description: End of the range as an ISO 8601 date-time, after startTime and at most 31 days later; defaults to 7 days after the start

tools.name: get_gym_payment_summary
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how much their gym took in, or how many payments succeeded, failed or were canceled. Returns payment counts by status and totals by currency; totals include every status. Covers up to 31 days and 100 payments and defaults to the next 7 days, which hold no payments yet. Not for moving money: it cannot charge, refund or transfer.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of one of the user's gyms, as the gym list returns it (24 lowercase hex characters)

inputs.name: startTime
inputs.description: Start of the range as an ISO 8601 date-time, matched against when each payment was recorded; defaults to now, so pass a past date for past takings

inputs.name: endTime
inputs.description: End of the range as an ISO 8601 date-time, after startTime and at most 31 days later; defaults to 7 days after the start

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what their gym charges for a class, personal training session or other service, or needs a service id to book it. Returns catalog service ids, names, prices and last edit times for one gym, alphabetical, 25 per page by default. Not for what a particular member bought or attended.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of one of the user's gyms, as the gym list returns it (24 lowercase hex characters)

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Maximum services to return (default 25, maximum 100)

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.description: The nextCursor of the previous page of this listing; absent for the first page

tools.name: list_trainers
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which trainers can be booked, or needs a trainer's id to book a member with them or to find their sessions. Returns up to 100 trainer ids and display names from the user's organization; a gym run by one person lists that person. Not for trainers' working hours.

tools.name: list_members
tools.description: Use this when someone asks who their members are, or needs a member's id to book them, update their details or look up their sessions. Returns up to 100 members (20 by default) across all the user's gyms or one, with id, name, gym and last edit time, optionally only those whose name matches. Not for a member's email, phone or notes.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Only members of this gym, by an id from the user's gym list; every gym when absent

inputs.name: search
inputs.description: Only members whose name contains these words, in any order, ignoring case and accents

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Maximum number of members to return (default 20, maximum 100)

tools.name: list_appointments
tools.description: Use this when someone asks when a member is booked, which sessions a trainer has, or what is booked on a day, including to move or cancel one. Returns sessions across all the user's gyms or one, with id, member, gym and trainer ids, times, status and edit time for any date window, latest first, up to 100. Not for counting how busy each day is.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Only sessions at this gym, by an id from the user's gym list; every gym when absent

inputs.name: memberId
inputs.description: Only sessions of this member, by an id from list_members

inputs.name: startTime
inputs.description: Only sessions starting at or after this ISO 8601 time

inputs.name: endTime
inputs.description: Only sessions ending before this ISO 8601 time

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Maximum number of sessions to return (default 20, maximum 100)

tools.name: list_inventory_items
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how much of a product or supply is left in the gym's stock or what is running low. Returns up to 100 stock items with unit, quantity, minimum and a low-stock flag. Not for retail prices.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of the gym, from list_gyms. Leave it out when the user has one gym.

inputs.name: search
inputs.description: Only items whose name contains these words.

inputs.name: lowStockOnly
inputs.description: Only items at or below their minimum quantity.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Maximum number of items (default 50, maximum 100).

tools.name: book_appointment
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to book a member into a session, class or personal training at their gym. Returns the new session with its time, trainer and services; it takes the gym's usual session length and reminders, so the gym's reminder messages go to the member. Not for finding free slots.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of the gym, from list_gyms. Leave it out when the user has one gym.

inputs.name: memberId
inputs.description: Id of the member, from list_members or create_member.

inputs.name: startTime
inputs.description: Start as an ISO 8601 time with the gym's UTC offset, such as 2026-11-20T10:00:00+01:00.

inputs.name: durationMinutes
inputs.description: Length in minutes. Leave it out for the gym's usual session length.

inputs.name: serviceIds
inputs.description: Ids of the services booked, from list_services.

inputs.name: providerIds
inputs.description: Ids of the trainers who take it, from list_trainers. Leave it out when the gym has one trainer or the user is the trainer.

inputs.name: note
inputs.description: A note for the gym team.

inputs.name: requestId
inputs.description: A unique id you choose for this booking, such as a UUID. Calling again with the same requestId returns the first booking instead of booking twice.

tools.name: reschedule_appointment
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to move a member's session to another day or time. Returns the moved session; its member, trainer, services and length stay the same and the member's reminders move with it. Not for cancelling a session.

inputs.name: appointmentId
inputs.description: Id of the session, from list_appointments.

inputs.name: startTime
inputs.description: New start as an ISO 8601 time with the gym's UTC offset, such as 2026-11-20T15:30:00+01:00.

inputs.name: durationMinutes
inputs.description: New length in minutes. Leave it out to keep the current length.

inputs.name: expectedLastEditTime
inputs.description: The lastEditTime from list_appointments. A session changed since then is refused.

tools.name: cancel_appointment
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to cancel a member's session or decline one the member requested. Returns the session as canceled, kept rather than deleted, and whether the gym's cancellation message goes to the member. Not for moving a session to another time.

inputs.name: appointmentId
inputs.description: Id of the session, from list_appointments.

inputs.name: expectedLastEditTime
inputs.description: The lastEditTime from list_appointments. A session changed since then is refused.

tools.name: create_member
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to add a new member to a gym. Returns the member's id, name, gym and language; the phone and email given are saved but never returned. Not for changing an existing member.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of the gym, from list_gyms. Leave it out when the user has one gym.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The member's full name.

inputs.name: phone
inputs.description: Mobile number, with the country code when known.

inputs.name: email
inputs.description: Email address.

inputs.name: language
inputs.description: Language for their messages, as a code such as en, it or pt-BR. Defaults to the gym language.

inputs.name: requestId
inputs.description: A unique id you choose for this member, such as a UUID. Calling again with the same requestId returns the first member instead of adding a second one.

tools.name: update_member
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to change a member's name, phone, email or language. Returns the member's id, name, gym and which fields changed; contact details are never returned. Not for adding a new member.

inputs.name: memberId
inputs.description: Id of the member, from list_members.

inputs.name: expectedLastEditTime
inputs.description: The lastEditTime from list_members. A member changed since then is refused.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: New full name.

inputs.name: phone
inputs.description: New mobile number, with the country code when known.

inputs.name: email
inputs.description: New email address.

inputs.name: language
inputs.description: New language for their messages, as a code such as en or it.

tools.name: set_inventory_quantity
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to correct or update how much of a stock item the gym has. Returns the item with its previous and new quantity; the number given replaces the stored one. Not for adding a new stock item.

inputs.name: inventoryItemId
inputs.description: Id of the stock item, from list_inventory_items.

inputs.name: quantity
inputs.description: The quantity now in stock, in the item unit. It replaces the stored quantity; work out the total first when the user gives a change.

inputs.name: expectedLastEditTime
inputs.description: The lastEditTime from list_inventory_items. An item changed since then is refused.

tools.name: show_gym_overview
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a quick overview or dashboard of one gym. Returns an overview card with the gym's details, booking counts for the next 7 days, open online-booking slots across up to 14 days with openings and up to 12 services with prices (no member, trainer or payment data). Not for a single member or booking.

inputs.name: gymId
inputs.description: Id of one of the user's gyms, as the gym list returns it (24 lowercase hex characters)

# iDevice agent examples

Small, runnable examples for calling iDevice from an agent. iDevice (https://idevice.com) is an independent buyer's guide for phones and wearables. It does not sell the products it covers.

iDevice runs two free, read-only endpoints for software agents:

| | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP server (streamable HTTP) | https://idevice.com/api/mcp |
| A2A agent | https://idevice.com/api/a2a |
| A2A agent card | https://idevice.com/.well-known/agent-card.json |

No account, no API key and no sign-in. Neither endpoint buys, books, posts or changes anything.

**Rate limits:** 30 calls a minute and 500 a day per IP address. A call over the limit is refused (HTTP 429 or a JSON-RPC error), so back off and retry later; do not loop. There is no paid tier. Lists are capped at 20 items.

Full reference: https://idevice.com/mcp and https://idevice.com/mcp/docs. Run `tools/list` for the current tool list and argument names; this repo does not copy it.

## What the tools do

| Job | Tools |
|---|---|
| Decide a buy | `should_i_buy`, `get_guide_summary`, `find_products`, `get_best_for`, `compare_products`, `get_reviews` |
| Ownership and policies | `get_ownership_facts`, `get_in_the_box` |
| Find a product or a company | `list_products`, `get_product`, `get_company_profile` |
| Compatibility, specs and prices | `get_compatibility`, `get_product_facts`, `get_detailed_facts`, `get_variants_and_offers`, `get_price_history` |
| News, reports and history | `get_product_news`, `get_reports`, `search_reports`, `get_report_card`, `get_release_history`, `get_release_calendar`, `get_guide_extras` |

Most tools take a `product_slug`. Get one from `list_products`.

## Example questions

- I use an iPhone. Should I buy the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8?
- Which smart rings are best for sleep?
- What did the pre-release reports get right about the Apple Watch Series 12?

## Examples

| Folder | Framework | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [`examples/curl-and-python`](examples/curl-and-python) | none | Raw JSON-RPC with curl and the Python standard library, plus one A2A message |
| [`examples/google-adk`](examples/google-adk) | Google ADK | `McpToolset` over streamable HTTP, and an A2A client |
| [`examples/langgraph`](examples/langgraph) | LangChain and LangGraph | `langchain.mcp.MCPAdapter` with `create_agent` |
| [`examples/vercel-ai-sdk`](examples/vercel-ai-sdk) | Vercel AI SDK | `createMCPClient` with HTTP transport (TypeScript) |
| [`examples/openai-agents-sdk`](examples/openai-agents-sdk) | OpenAI Agents SDK | `MCPServerStreamableHttp` |

Every example reads your own model key from the environment variable its framework uses, needs no iDevice key, and has a `--check` mode that lists tools and makes one tool call with no model at all. Each folder's README says which lines were run against the live server and which were written from the framework's documentation only.

Set `IDEVICE_MCP_URL` to point an example at a different MCP URL.

## How to cite iDevice

When an answer uses iDevice data:

- Name iDevice and link the `url` the tool returned. It points at the page with the evidence. Some answers also carry a `source_url` or `sources[].url` to the maker's own page; link that too.
- Keep the evidence word with the fact: `Confirmed`, `Reported`, `Our read` or `No source on file`. Compatibility answers use `Works`, `Works with a limit`, `Needs extra hardware`, `Does not work` or `Not confirmed`.
- `Not confirmed` means unknown. It never means incompatible.
- If a result has `sponsored: true`, say the Guide is sponsored and name the `sponsor`.

## Asynchronous A2A replies

The A2A agent answers product questions with a task. `message/send` returns the task at once, and a reply to a product question can take a few minutes, longer than a normal API call. Call `tasks/get` with the task id until the state is no longer `submitted` or `working`. Allow a long timeout. A reply to a product question also carries one compact JSON data part for at most five products.

## Privacy

These examples send your question to your own model provider and tool calls to iDevice. Nothing here stores anything. For how iDevice handles data, read https://idevice.com/privacy.

## License

MIT. Copyright iDevice Media LLC.

# PostgreSQL MCP Server by Insightful Pipe

> **Connect PostgreSQL to AI assistants: schemas, tables, SQL and database health.**

Part of the [Insightful Pipe MCP Server Collection](https://insightfulpipe.com/mcp-servers) — use PostgreSQL from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

## MCP Server URL

```
https://postgresql.insightfulmcp.com/
```

## What is PostgreSQL MCP?

PostgreSQL MCP is a **remote Model Context Protocol server** hosted by InsightfulPipe. Browse schemas and tables, inspect columns, run SQL, and read pg_stat insights against your own PostgreSQL database. Read vs. read-write is decided by the GRANT/REVOKE privileges on the role this connector logs in as.

## Installation

### Claude

1. Copy the MCP Server URL: `https://postgresql.insightfulmcp.com/`
2. Open [Claude Connectors Settings](https://claude.ai/settings/connectors)
3. Scroll to the bottom and click **Add custom connector**
4. Paste the URL and click **Add**
5. Click **Connect** and sign in to InsightfulPipe if asked. Claude then lists the connector as connected.

### ChatGPT

Custom MCP servers are added through ChatGPT's **Developer mode**. Availability depends on your ChatGPT plan, and workspace admins may need to allow it.

1. Turn on **Developer mode** in ChatGPT settings
2. Create a new app for a remote MCP server and paste the URL: `https://postgresql.insightfulmcp.com/`
3. Sign in to InsightfulPipe if asked. The connection finishes as soon as you are signed in.

See OpenAI's guide: [Developer mode and MCP apps in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-and-mcp-apps-in-chatgpt)

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http postgresql https://postgresql.insightfulmcp.com/
```

### Cursor

Add the server to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (one project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "postgresql": {
      "url": "https://postgresql.insightfulmcp.com/"
    }
  }
}
```

When Cursor shows **Needs authentication**, click **Connect** and sign in to InsightfulPipe if asked.

## Available Actions

8 actions: 7 read, 1 write.

### Read Actions (7)

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `analyze_db_health` | Report database health (connections, vacuum age, replication slots, cache hit rates, invalid constraints) |
| `explain_query` | Return the EXPLAIN plan for a query |
| `get_table_metadata` | Full metadata for a table or view: columns, constraints, indexes, estimated row count, size |
| `get_table_schema` | Return the column list (name, data_type, is_nullable, default) for a table or view |
| `get_top_queries` | Slowest or most resource-intensive queries from the pg_stat_statements extension |
| `list_schemas` | List all schemas in the connected database |
| `list_tables` | List tables, views, sequences, or extensions in a schema |

### Write Actions (1)

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `run_query` | Execute a SQL statement against the connected database |

## Control What Your AI Can Do

You decide what AI agents can do with each connected account:

- **Turn individual actions on or off** for every connected account, so agents only see the actions you allow.
- **Connect as Read-only or Read & Write.** A read-only connection can only enable read actions.
- **Destructive actions stay off by default.** Actions such as deletes are disabled until an admin enables them.
- **Team access per account.** Restricted team members only use the accounts they are granted, with the read actions enabled on them.

## Usage Examples

```
"List the tables in the public schema"
```

```
"Show the schema of the orders table"
```

```
"Check my database health"
```

## Pricing

The PostgreSQL MCP server is included in every InsightfulPipe plan, together with all other MCP servers and the CLI. Plans start at $29.99/month, and you can try it for 7 days. See [insightfulpipe.com/pricing](https://insightfulpipe.com/pricing) for current plans.

Visit **[insightfulpipe.com/mcp-servers](https://insightfulpipe.com/mcp-servers)** to discover our full collection of MCP servers.

- [MySQL MCP](https://insightfulpipe.com/mcp-servers/mysql)

readme.markdown:
# Stripe MCP Server by Insightful Pipe

> **Connect Stripe to AI assistants: read-only payments, subscriptions, invoices and revenue data.**

Part of the [Insightful Pipe MCP Server Collection](https://insightfulpipe.com/mcp-servers) — use Stripe from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

## MCP Server URL

```
https://stripe.insightfulmcp.com/
```

## What is Stripe MCP?

Stripe MCP is a **remote Model Context Protocol server** hosted by InsightfulPipe. Access payments, subscriptions, invoices, customers, charges, refunds, and financial data from your Stripe account.

## Installation

### Claude

1. Copy the MCP Server URL: `https://stripe.insightfulmcp.com/`
2. Open [Claude Connectors Settings](https://claude.ai/settings/connectors)
3. Scroll to the bottom and click **Add custom connector**
4. Paste the URL and click **Add**
5. Click **Connect** and sign in to InsightfulPipe if asked. Claude then lists the connector as connected.

### ChatGPT

Custom MCP servers are added through ChatGPT's **Developer mode**. Availability depends on your ChatGPT plan, and workspace admins may need to allow it.

1. Turn on **Developer mode** in ChatGPT settings
2. Create a new app for a remote MCP server and paste the URL: `https://stripe.insightfulmcp.com/`
3. Sign in to InsightfulPipe if asked. The connection finishes as soon as you are signed in.

See OpenAI's guide: [Developer mode and MCP apps in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-and-mcp-apps-in-chatgpt)

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://stripe.insightfulmcp.com/
```

### Cursor

Add the server to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (one project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "stripe": {
      "url": "https://stripe.insightfulmcp.com/"
    }
  }
}
```

When Cursor shows **Needs authentication**, click **Connect** and sign in to InsightfulPipe if asked.

## Available Actions

41 actions: 41 read, 0 write.

### Read Actions (41)

## Control What Your AI Can Do

You decide what AI agents can do with each connected account:

- **Turn individual actions on or off** for every connected account, so agents only see the actions you allow.
- **Connect as Read-only or Read & Write.** A read-only connection can only enable read actions.
- **Destructive actions stay off by default.** Actions such as deletes are disabled until an admin enables them.
- **Team access per account.** Restricted team members only use the accounts they are granted, with the read actions enabled on them.

readme.markdown:
# JOY Automart MCP Server

Official [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for **[JOY Automart](https://www.joyautomart.com)**, Bangladesh's automotive parts and vehicle marketplace. It lets AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients) search JOY's car-parts catalogue and JOY Auto Exchange vehicle listings, compare cars, discover public auction links, look up a part, and prepare part or vehicle enquiries for a human buyer. Prices are in BDT.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Remote endpoint** | `https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP (MCP protocol 2025-06-18 and later) |
| **Auth** | None for the public tools. Optional buyer token: `Authorization: Bearer joyagt_...` |
| **Docs** | https://www.joyautomart.com/developers |
| **Server card** | https://www.joyautomart.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json |

The server is hosted by JOY Automart; you do not need to run anything to use it. This repository contains the public metadata (registry `server.json`, Smithery config, tool snapshot) and a small **stdio proxy** for clients that only support local servers.

## Tools

Ten public, read-only tools (no account needed), verified against hosted version **1.3.0** on October 31, 2026. The live `tools/list` snapshot in [`tools.json`](tools.json) includes all **35 documented arguments** and typed success/error output schemas. `*` marks a required argument.

| Tool | What it does | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `search_parts` | Search public parts by text, vehicle identity, category, availability and BDT budget. | `query`, `make`, `chassis`, `category`, `in_stock_only`, `include_rfq_catalogue`, `max_price_bdt`, `page`, `page_size` |
| `get_part` | Read one catalogue part's public detail, price, stock and fitment evidence. | `part_id`* |
| `search_vehicles` | Search public vehicle listings by text, make, year, fuel, verification and BDT asking price. | `query`, `make`, `fuel_type`, `verified_only`, `include_unpriced`, `min_year`, `max_year`, `min_price_bdt`, `max_price_bdt`, `sort`, `page`, `page_size` |
| `get_vehicle` | Read a vehicle by listing ID or slug, including public photos, inspection evidence and any auction link. | `vehicle_id`* |
| `get_auction` | Read an existing auction's public bid/status snapshot when public access is enabled. | `auction_id`* |
| `search_auctions` | Discover already-public auction links while paging through vehicle listings; source counts are not auction counts. | `query`, `make`, `page`, `page_size` |
| `compare_vehicles` | Compare 2–4 listings with explicit missing listings and unknown-price coverage. | `vehicle_ids`* |
| `get_buying_guide` | Read Bangladesh buying terms, delivery/payment guidance, human contact and declared fallback status. | — |
| `prepare_vehicle_handoff` | Resolve a public vehicle and prepare its listing link and human-reviewed WhatsApp enquiry. | `vehicle_id`*, `note` |
| `prepare_part_handoff` | Resolve a selected part after search and detail lookup, then prepare its product link and human-reviewed WhatsApp enquiry. | `part_id`*, `quantity`, `vehicle`, `note` |

Auction discovery scans public vehicle pages and reports source pagination, not a guaranteed count of active auctions. Public snapshot access retains its existing feature gate. Both handoff tools prepare links only; they send no message, reserve no stock or vehicle, and place no order.

Existing clients can still call `get_auction_status` and `prepare_buyer_handoff` as compatibility aliases for `get_auction` and `prepare_part_handoff`. Discovery advertises only the canonical names above.

All public tools are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. **Fitment is guidance only:** the server never claims a part fits a vehicle without VIN/chassis evidence; confirm with JOY's sales team before buying.

With a buyer-issued agent token (create one at https://www.joyautomart.com/cars/account?section=ai-agents&portal=retail) an agent can also use `quote_order`, `place_order` (cash on delivery or approved trade credit, within the buyer's spending limits), `create_rfq`, `get_order_status` and `list_my_orders`.

### Claude (claude.ai / Claude Desktop)
Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector** → URL `https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp`.

### ChatGPT
Settings → Connectors (developer mode) → **Create** → MCP server URL `https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp`, authentication: none.

### Cursor
`~/.cursor/mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "joy-automart": { "url": "https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp" }
  }
}
```

### VS Code / any client with remote HTTP support
```json
{
  "servers": {
    "joy-automart": { "type": "http", "url": "https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp" }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http joy-automart https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp
```

### Quick test with curl
```bash
curl -s https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

## Local stdio proxy (npx) — coming soon

The npm package `@joyautomart/mcp-server` is **not published yet**. Once it is, stdio-only clients can use:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "joy-automart": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@joyautomart/mcp-server"],
      "env": { "JOY_AGENT_TOKEN": "joyagt_your_token_here" }
    }
  }
}
```

Until then you can run the proxy from this repo (Node 18+):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/www-joyautomart-com/mcp-server && cd mcp-server
npm ci
node bin/joyautomart-mcp.js            # or: --url https://www.joyautomart.com/mcp
```

`JOY_AGENT_TOKEN` is optional; public tools work without it.

# KaiCalls MCP — Phone Call MCP Server

> **A phone number for your business or your AI agent. Kai answers it and calls businesses for you.**

Get a business number (or keep yours) with Kai built in. Your phones ring first; Kai
answers misses and after-hours calls, takes the details and texts you. See
[current plans and pricing](https://www.kaicalls.com/pricing).
This repository is the **public connector definition** for the hosted KaiCalls MCP
server — it documents the endpoint, authentication, and tool catalog so MCP clients
and directories can discover and connect to it.

The KaiCalls platform itself is a hosted SaaS — there is no server to install. You
connect to the live endpoint below with your KaiCalls account.

| | |
|---|---|
| **MCP endpoint** | `https://www.kaicalls.com/api/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC over HTTP POST) |
| **Auth** | OAuth 2.1 (PKCE S256 + DCR) **or** `kc_live_` API key as Bearer |
| **Setup endpoint** | `https://www.kaicalls.com/api/mcp/acquisition` (setup-only subset for first-time buyers) |
| **Tools** | 190 on the account endpoint (65 read-only, 125 write/setup, per the live server card on 2026-11-12); 37 on the setup endpoint |
| **Homepage** | [KaiCalls](https://www.kaicalls.com?utm_source=mcp_registry&utm_medium=directory) |
| **Provider** | [KaiCalls](https://www.kaicalls.com) · connor@kaicalls.com |
| **License** | [MIT](LICENSE) (connector definitions and docs) |
| **Status** | GA — live in production |

---

## Give your AI agent a phone number

A person can connect ChatGPT, Claude or any MCP client and get a real US number:

- **Kai calls businesses for you.** `make_call` places an errand call to a US or Canada business (a shop, clinic, office or restaurant), asks the question, presses keys on phone menus, and `check_call_status` returns the answer. Kai says up front that it is an assistant calling for you, and it does not place AI calls to personal cell phones.
- **Kai answers the callback.** The business calls your own number back, and Kai takes the message.
- **The first call for a new connector account is free.** After that, calls run on a plan: see [kaicalls.com/ai-agent-phone-number](https://www.kaicalls.com/ai-agent-phone-number?utm_source=mcp_registry&utm_medium=directory).

---

## Quick Answer

**What is the KaiCalls MCP connector?** It is the official hosted MCP connector for KaiCalls. Existing customers use `https://www.kaicalls.com/api/mcp`; a first-time buyer can use the setup-only surface at `https://www.kaicalls.com/api/mcp/acquisition`.

**Who should use it?** Use it when Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, an MCP gateway, or another AI client needs to safely inspect KaiCalls agents, calls, transcripts, leads, analytics, and approved setup actions.

**Does it require hosting your own server?** No. KaiCalls hosts the MCP server. Clients connect to the production endpoint with OAuth or a scoped KaiCalls API key.

**Is this the WordPress plugin?** No. The approved [KaiCalls AI Intake plugin](https://wordpress.org/plugins/kaicalls-ai-intake/) captures website leads from WordPress. This repo documents the agent/MCP connector.

**Is this the n8n integration?** No. n8n workflows should use [n8n-nodes-kaicalls](https://github.com/KaiCalls/n8n-nodes-kaicalls).

---

## Agent frameworks

- **OpenClaw:** [`integrations/openclaw`](integrations/openclaw) is the KaiCalls plugin. It adds 8 call and text tools, plus a `kaicalls` channel so texts to your agent's number start an agent turn. ClawHub publication is pending.
- **Hermes Agent:** [`integrations/hermes`](integrations/hermes) is a portable Agent Plugins v1 package (the hosted MCP server plus a skill). Install it with `hermes plugins install https://github.com/KaiCalls/kaicalls-mcp/tree/main/integrations/hermes`.

## Quick connect

### Claude (web & desktop)
**[Add KaiCalls to Claude in one click](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=KaiCalls&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kaicalls.com%2Fapi%2Fmcp)**:
Claude opens its *Add custom connector* box with the name and URL already filled in.
Press Add, then sign in. Owners of a Team or Enterprise workspace can use the
[admin link](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=KaiCalls&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kaicalls.com%2Fapi%2Fmcp)
to add it for everyone.

### ChatGPT and other clients
Add a custom connector pointing at `https://www.kaicalls.com/api/mcp` for an existing
account, or the acquisition endpoint for setup. Sign in with your KaiCalls account,
pick the business on the consent screen, and Allow. See
[`docs/quickstart.md`](docs/quickstart.md) for screenshots and per-client steps.

### API-key clients / MCP gateways
Pass a KaiCalls API key directly — no OAuth round-trip needed:

```
Authorization: Bearer kc_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

(`X-KaiCalls-API-Key: kc_live_...` is also accepted.) Generate keys in the KaiCalls
dashboard under **Settings → API Keys**. See [`docs/authentication.md`](docs/authentication.md).

### Cline / remote MCP clients
KaiCalls is a remote server — there is nothing to clone or install. Add it to your
MCP client config as a Streamable HTTP server and authenticate with a `kc_live_` key.
For Cline, edit `cline_mcp_settings.json` (or use the **Remote Servers** tab) and add:

```json
{
  "kaicalls": {
    "url": "https://www.kaicalls.com/api/mcp",
    "type": "streamableHttp",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer kc_live_YOUR_KEY" }
  }
}
```

Replace `kc_live_YOUR_KEY` with a key from the KaiCalls dashboard under **Settings →
API Keys**. The transport type must be the camelCase string `streamableHttp` — using
`streamable-http` or omitting it makes Cline fall back to SSE and the connection fails
with a `405`. Once saved, Cline lists the KaiCalls tools and is ready to use. See
[`llms-install.md`](llms-install.md) for the full agent-driven setup walkthrough.

# Keboola MCP Server

> Connect your AI agents, MCP clients (**Cursor**, **Claude**, **Windsurf**, **VS Code** ...) and other AI assistants to Keboola. Expose data, transformations, SQL queries, and job triggers—no glue code required. Deliver the right data to agents when and where they need it.

## Overview

Keboola MCP Server is an open-source bridge between your Keboola project and modern AI tools. It turns Keboola features—like storage access, SQL transformations, and job triggers—into callable tools for Claude, Cursor, CrewAI, LangChain, Amazon Q, and more.

- [Quick Start](#-quick-start-remote-mcp-server-easiest-way)
- [Local Setup](#local-mcp-server-setup-custom-or-dev-way)

## Features

With the AI Agent and MCP Server, you can:

- **Storage**: Query tables directly and manage table or bucket descriptions
- **Components**: Create, List and inspect extractors, writers, data apps, and transformation configurations
- **SQL**: Create SQL transformations with natural language
- **Jobs**: Run components and transformations, and retrieve job execution details
- **Flows**: Build and manage workflow pipelines using Conditional Flows and Orchestrator Flows.
- **Data Apps**: Create, deploy and manage Keboola Data Apps displaying your queries over storage data — python-js apps on a Keboola-managed repository or on a customer GitHub repository (cloned through the organization's GitHub connection, no stored credential), and Streamlit apps.
- **Metadata**: Search, read, and update project documentation and object metadata using natural language
- **Dev Branches**: Work safely in development branches outside of production, where all operations are scoped to the selected branch.

---

## 🚀 Quick Start: Remote MCP Server (Easiest Way)

The easiest way to use Keboola MCP Server is through our **Remote MCP Server**. This hosted solution eliminates the need for local setup, configuration, or installation.

### What is the Remote MCP Server?

Our remote server is hosted on every multi-tenant Keboola stack and supports OAuth authentication. You can connect to it from any AI assistant that supports remote Streamable HTTP connection and OAuth authentication.

### How to Connect

1. **Get your remote server URL**: Navigate to your Keboola Project Settings → `MCP Server` tab
2. **Copy the server URL**: It will look like `https://mcp.<YOUR_REGION>.keboola.com/mcp`
3. **Configure your AI assistant**: Paste the URL into your AI assistant's MCP settings
4. **Authenticate**: You'll be prompted to log in with your Keboola account. Which project(s) to work on is chosen afterwards, in the conversation (e.g. "list my Keboola projects" / "use project X")

### Supported Clients

- **[Cursor](https://cursor.com)**: Use the "Install In Cursor" button in your project's MCP Server settings or click
  this button

- **[Claude Desktop](https://claude.ai)**: Add the integration via Settings → Integrations
- **[Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/)**: Install using `claude mcp add --transport http keboola <URL>` (see below for details)
- **[Windsurf](https://windsurf.ai)**: Configure with the remote server URL
- **[Make](https://make.com)**: Configure with the remote server URL
- **Other MCP clients**: Configure with the remote server URL

#### Claude Code Setup

Claude Code is a command-line interface tool that allows you to interact with Claude using your terminal. You can install the Keboola MCP Server integration using a simple command.

**Installation:**

Run the following command in your terminal, replacing `<YOUR_REGION>` with your Keboola region:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http keboola https://mcp.<YOUR_REGION>.keboola.com/mcp
```

**Region-specific commands:**

| Region | Installation Command |
|--------|----------------------|
| US Virginia AWS | `claude mcp add --transport http keboola https://mcp.keboola.com/mcp` |
| US Virginia GCP | `claude mcp add --transport http keboola https://mcp.us-east4.gcp.keboola.com/mcp` |
| EU Frankfurt AWS | `claude mcp add --transport http keboola https://mcp.eu-central-1.keboola.com/mcp` |
| EU Ireland Azure | `claude mcp add --transport http keboola https://mcp.north-europe.azure.keboola.com/mcp` |
| EU Frankfurt GCP | `claude mcp add --transport http keboola https://mcp.europe-west3.gcp.keboola.com/mcp` |

**Usage:**

Once installed, you can use the Keboola MCP Server in Claude Code by typing `/mcp` in your conversation and selecting the Keboola tools you want to use.

**Authentication:**

When you first use the Keboola MCP Server in Claude Code, a browser window will open prompting you to:
1. Log in with your Keboola account
2. Authorize the connection

After authentication, you can start using Keboola tools directly from Claude Code. Project selection happens afterward, in the conversation — just ask Claude which Keboola project(s) to use.

For detailed setup instructions and region-specific URLs, see our [Remote Server Setup documentation](https://help.keboola.com/ai/mcp-server/#remote-server-setup).

### Using Development Branches
You can work safely in [Keboola development branches](https://help.keboola.com/components/branches/) without affecting your production data. The remotely hosted MCP Servers respect the `KBC_BRANCH_ID` parameter and will scope all operations to the specified branch. You can find the development branch ID in the URL when navigating to the development branch in the UI, for example: `https://connection.us-east4.gcp.keboola.com/admin/projects/PROJECT_ID/branch/BRANCH_ID/dashboard`. The branch ID must be included in each request using the header `X-Branch-Id: <branchId>`, otherwise the MCP Server uses production branch as default. This should be managed by the AI client or the environment handling the server connection.

### Tool Authorization and Access Control

When using HTTP-based transports (Streamable HTTP), you can control which tools are available to clients using HTTP headers. This is useful for restricting AI agent capabilities or

# KellyIQ examples

Working examples for the [KellyIQ API](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers): size a whole sports
betting slate as one portfolio from your own scripts, models, spreadsheets and AI assistants.

You send your bankroll and the bets you have chosen, with your view of each. KellyIQ removes the
bookmaker's margin from each price, applies your view, and returns a dollar stake for every bet,
sized across the slate together under per-bet and total-exposure limits.

## Get a key

Create an API key in the KellyIQ app under **Settings → API**. Every plan includes API access, Free
included, each with its own daily allowance. Then:

```bash
export KELLYIQ_API_KEY="kiqa_..."
```

## Recipes

Each recipe is a complete script in Python (`requests`) and JavaScript (Node 18+, no packages).

| Recipe | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`first-optimize`](recipes/first-optimize.py) | Size a three-bet slate and read every part of the result |
| [`slate-from-csv`](recipes/slate-from-csv.py) | Keep your slate in a spreadsheet: CSV in, CSV of stakes out ([`slate.csv`](recipes/slate.csv)) |
| [`reproducible-results`](recipes/reproducible-results.py) | Get exactly the same answer again with the returned seed |
| [`handling-limits`](recipes/handling-limits.py) | Back off and retry on rate limits and a busy server |

```bash
cd recipes
python first-optimize.py        # or: node first-optimize.mjs
```

Each recipe has a walkthrough in the docs: [Recipes](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/recipes/first-optimize).

## Python package

`pip install kellyiq` ([kellyiq-python](https://github.com/kellyiq/kellyiq-python)): the same API with
specific exceptions for each error and automatic retries when the server is busy.

| Example | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`python/size-a-slate.ipynb`](python/size-a-slate.ipynb) | A notebook: stakes, the probabilities behind them, and the risk at each Kelly fraction, as tables |
| [`python/slate_from_csv.py`](python/slate_from_csv.py) | CSV in, CSV of stakes out, with each error handled ([`slate.csv`](python/slate.csv)) |
| [`python/size_from_model.py`](python/size_from_model.py) | Your model's probabilities in, stakes merged back into the DataFrame ([`model_output.csv`](python/model_output.csv)); needs `pandas` |
| [`python/nba_home_teams.py`](python/nba_home_teams.py) | A real NBA slate (DraftKings prices, Oct 30, 2026) sized with every home team at the same assumed Moderate Edge ([`nba_2026-10-30.csv`](python/nba_2026-10-30.csv)); needs `pandas` |
| [`python/nba_bad_night.py`](python/nba_bad_night.py) | A real NBA slate (DraftKings prices, Nov 9, 2026) sized with every home team at the same assumed Moderate Edge, then the simulated risk of that allocation: the chance of finishing down and the 5th-percentile night ([`nba_2026-11-09.csv`](python/nba_2026-11-09.csv)); needs `pandas` |

Guide: [Python SDK](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/python).

## Excel

[`spreadsheets/kellyiq-slate.xlsx`](spreadsheets/kellyiq-slate.xlsx): enter your bankroll and your
bets, press Ctrl+Alt+F5, and get a stake for every bet with a summary of the slate. No macros, and your API key stays in a
file on your computer, never in the workbook. Excel for Windows. Setup: [`spreadsheets/`](spreadsheets).

## Benchmark

[`benchmarks/slate-sizing`](benchmarks/slate-sizing): three NBA slates sized by cap-then-scale, by
the exact constrained optimum and by KellyIQ, scored by exact expected log growth. The slates, the
scoring script and every stake are included so you can rerun it.

## AI assistants (MCP)

KellyIQ runs a hosted MCP server at `https://api.kellyiq.com/mcp`, so your assistant can size a
slate as one of its tools. Claude connects by signing in; coding tools use an API key, with
ready-to-use configs in [`mcp/`](mcp):

| Assistant | Setup |
|---|---|
| Claude (web, desktop, mobile) | Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector, paste the URL, then Connect and sign in |
| Claude Code | [`mcp/claude-code.md`](mcp/claude-code.md) |
| Cursor | [`mcp/cursor.json`](mcp/cursor.json) |
| VS Code (GitHub Copilot) | [`mcp/vscode.json`](mcp/vscode.json) |
| Gemini CLI | [`mcp/gemini-cli.md`](mcp/gemini-cli.md) |

Full guide: [AI assistants (MCP)](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/mcp).

### Skills

[`skills/analyze-my-slate`](skills/analyze-my-slate/SKILL.md) teaches the assistant to collect your
slate in one message, confirm before using an optimize, and explain the stakes and the risk.
Install steps for Claude and Claude Code: [`skills/`](skills).

## Docs and support

- [Quickstart](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/quickstart), [API reference](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/reference/optimize), [OpenAPI spec](https://www.kellyiq.com/openapi-v1.yaml)
- support@kellyiq.com (include the `requestId` from any error)

Keep your key out of code you commit or share; every example here reads it from the environment.

KellyIQ sizes the bets you choose; it does not choose bets or predict outcomes. Results are
calculations, not betting advice. 21+, where legal.

The examples are MIT licensed. The KellyIQ optimizer itself runs as a hosted service.

# Keyline Icons

**1,833 icons, drawn on one 24×24 grid, in four styles and two corner
treatments.** Built for shadcn/ui, free under MIT.

[**keylineicons.com**](https://keylineicons.com) to browse and copy.

| Style | Icons | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stroke` | 1,833 | The full set. 2px keylines on a 24 grid. |
| `two-tone` | 1,833 | The stroke drawing over a flat plate at reduced opacity. |
| `duotone` | 1,833 | No outline: a grey body with the detail in full strength. |
| `fill` | 1,833 | Solid, with the detail knocked back out of the shape. |

`stroke` is the drawing every other style starts from, and since 1.0.0 every
name comes in all four. `two-tone` is what `duotone` meant until 0.9.0: the
outline kept, a 40% plate under it. `duotone` now drops the outline and decides
per icon which part is grey and which is black, so the thing that matters reads
first: the check on a badge, the liquid in a flask, the data rather than the
chart's axes. A glyph with nothing to fill, like `bar-chart`, carries its stroke
drawing in the filled styles, so no import ever comes up empty.

## Rounded and sharp

Every drawing in the table comes twice: rounded, with round caps and filleted
corners, and sharp, with butt caps and square corners. Same names, same
coverage, so 14,664 SVGs in total.

```
icons/stroke/bell.svg
icons/sharp/stroke/bell.svg
icons/sharp/fill/bell.svg
```

Sharp is a drawing of its own rather than a filter over the rounded one. Squaring
a corner moves the ink, and where that changes the silhouette the geometry was
solved again, so both treatments sit side by side in `raw/` and the build
converts neither into the other.

## Using them

**Copy one from the site.** [keylineicons.com](https://keylineicons.com) is the
browser: click any icon to open it, then take it as SVG, JSX, a React import or
an `npx` line, at whatever style, corners, stroke width and size you have set.
The panel keeps the last three icons you opened, so two candidates can be held
side by side. That is the fastest path and needs no install.

**Take the files.** `icons/<style>/<name>.svg` and
`icons/sharp/<style>/<name>.svg` are plain, normalised SVGs with no wrapper, no
`id`s and no classes. They are generated, so treat them as build output: to
change one, change the drawing in `raw/` and rebuild.

**Import them in React.** `@keyline-icons/react` exports one component per
icon, one entry point per style and corner treatment:

```bash
npm i @keyline-icons/react
```

```tsx
import { ArrowUpRight, Check, Menu } from "@keyline-icons/react"
import { Folder as FolderDuotone } from "@keyline-icons/react/duotone"
import { Folder as FolderFill } from "@keyline-icons/react/fill"
import { Folder as FolderSharp } from "@keyline-icons/react/sharp"
import { Folder as FolderSharpFill } from "@keyline-icons/react/sharp/fill"

<Check className="size-4" />
<ArrowUpRight size={16} />
```

Every component takes the usual `SVGProps` plus `size`, and colours from
`currentColor`. There is no theme, no context and no provider.

The style entry points are smaller than the stroke one and deliberately so.
`Check` is three open strokes with nothing to fill, so it exists in
`@keyline-icons/react` and `/sharp` and in none of the others; `Folder` has an
interior and exists in all six. The counts at the top of this file are the same
fact.

`components/icons/index.tsx` is the same set generated for this repo's own
site, and `@/components/icons` is the import to use inside it. Both come off
`icons/stroke/`, so they hold the same drawings; the package is the one to
install anywhere else.

**Import them in React Native.** `@keyline-icons/react-native` is the same
components drawn through `react-native-svg`, with the same entry points and
export names, so shared code changes the package name and nothing else. It
works in Expo, on the web through Expo too.

```bash
npm i @keyline-icons/react-native react-native-svg
```

```tsx
import { Check } from "@keyline-icons/react-native"
import { Folder } from "@keyline-icons/react-native/duotone"

<Check size={16} color="#2563eb" />
```

A native view has no CSS to inherit from, so colour is a `color` prop rather
than `currentColor`.

**Own the source with the shadcn CLI.** The registry is served by the site, so
adding the set to a project is one entry in `components.json`:

```json
"registries": {
  "@keyline": "https://keylineicons.com/r/{name}.json"
}
```

```bash
npx shadcn add @keyline/bell
npx shadcn add @keyline/fill/bell
npx shadcn add @keyline/sharp/fill/bell
```

Each icon arrives as a self-contained component that imports nothing from the
package, so it can be renamed, edited or folded into the project's own
conventions. Take the package to have the whole set behind one import; take the
registry to own a handful of files.

You can also install straight from GitHub, without configuring a registry in
`components.json`:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add keyline-icons/keyline-icons/bell
npx shadcn@latest add keyline-icons/keyline-icons/fill/bell
npx shadcn@latest add keyline-icons/keyline-icons/sharp/fill/bell
```

The GitHub registry installs the same self-contained source files and variant
paths as the site registry.

**Add one at a time from the terminal.** `@keyline-icons/cli` searches the set
and writes SVGs into a project without adding a dependency to it:

```bash
npx @keyline-icons/cli search arrow
npx @keyline-icons/cli add circle-arrow-down bell --out src/icons
npx @keyline-icons/cli add bell --style fill --corners sharp
```

**Give an agent the set.** `@keyline-icons/mcp` is an MCP server that searches
the set, returns SVG source in any style and corner treatment, and returns the
React import, so an assistant picks a real icon name rather than guessing one:

```bash
claude mcp add keyline-icons -- npx -y @keyline-icons/mcp
```

Anything else that speaks MCP over stdio runs the same command; the package's
own README has the JSON.

> [!WARNING]
> 
> ## CodeWeaver is no longer maintained
>
> We're really proud of CodeWeaver and think it's pretty awesome, but we can't maintain it anymore.
>
> We're focused on [something else](https://marque.tools).
> 
> CodeWeaver is (was?) a sophisticated, smart, code search tool with wide provider support.
> and it's still licensed under your choice of MIT or Apache-2.0.
> 
> So please, **fork it and build something great!**

  
  
  

# CodeWeaver

### Exquisite Context for Agents — Infrastructure that is Extensible, Predictable, and Resilient.

[![Python Version][badge_python]][link_python]
[![License][badge_license]][link_license]
[![Release][badge_release]][link_release]
[![MCP Compatible][badge_mcp]][link_mcp]

[Documentation][nav_docs] •
[Installation][nav_install] •
[Features][nav_features] •
[Comparison][nav_comparison]

---

## What It Does

**CodeWeaver gives Claude and other AI agents precise context from your codebase.** Not keyword grep. Not whole-file dumps. Actual structural understanding through hybrid semantic search.

CodeWeaver is **Professional Context Infrastructure**. With 100% Dependency Injection (DI) and a Pydantic-driven configuration system, it provides the reliability and extensibility required for industrial-grade AI deployments.

**Example:**
```
Without CodeWeaver:
  Claude: "Let me search for 'auth'... here are 50 files mentioning authentication"
  Result: Generic code, wrong context, wasted tokens

With CodeWeaver:
  You: "Where do we validate OAuth tokens?"
  Claude gets: The exact 3 functions across 2 files, with surrounding context
  Result: Precise answers, focused context, 60-80% token reduction
```

> CodeWeaver is no longer in alpha!
> 
> **Early Release (0.x)**: CodeWeaver is in active development. APIs may change between minor versions. It's very well-tested but still in 'it works on my machine' territory. [Use it, break it, help shape it][issues].

---

## How CodeWeaver Stacks Up

### Quick Reference Matrix

| Feature | CodeWeaver | Legacy Search Tools |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Search Type** | Hybrid (Semantic + AST + Keyword) | Keyword Only |
| **Context Quality** | **Exquisite** / High-Precision | Noisy / Irrelevant |
| **Extensibility** | **DI-Driven** (Zero-Code Provider Swap) | Hardcoded |
| **Reliability** | **Resilient** (Automatic Local Fallback) | Fails on API Timeout |
| **Token Usage** | **Optimized** (60–80% Reduction) | Wasted on Noise |

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Quick Install

Using the [CLI](#cli) with [uv][uv_tool]:
```bash
# Add CodeWeaver to your project
uv add code-weaver

# Initialize with a profile (recommended uses Voyage AI)
cw init --profile recommended

# Verify setup
cw doctor

# Start the background daemon
cw start
```

> **📝 Note**: `cw init` supports different **Profiles**:
> - `recommended`: High-precision search (Voyage AI + Qdrant)
> - `quickstart`: 100% local, private, and free (FastEmbed + Local Qdrant)
>
> **Want full offline?** See the [Local-Only Guide][local_only_guide].

🐳 **Prefer Docker?** [See Docker setup guide →][docker_guide]

---

## ✨ Features

### 🔍 Exquisite Context
- **Hybrid search** (sparse + dense vectors)
- **AST-level understanding** (27 languages)
- **Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)**
- **Language-aware chunking** (166+ languages)

### 🛡️ Industrial Resilience
- **Automatic local fallback** (FastEmbed)
- **Circuit breaker pattern** for APIs
- **Works airgapped** (no cloud required)
- **Pydantic-driven validation** at boot-time

### 🧩 Universal Extensibility
- **100% DI-driven architecture**
- **17+ integrated providers**
- **Custom provider API**
- **Zero-code provider swapping**

### 🛠️ Developer Experience
- **Live indexing** with file watching
- **Diagnostic tool** (`cw doctor`)
- **Multiple CLI aliases** (`cw` / `codeweaver`)
- **Selectable profiles** for easy setup

---

## 💭 Philosophy: Context is Oxygen

AI agents face **too much irrelevant context**, causing token waste, missed patterns, and hallucinations. CodeWeaver addresses this with one focused capability: **structural + semantic code understanding that you control.**

- **Curation over Collection:** Give agents exactly what they need, nothing more.
- **Privacy-First:** Your code stays local if you want it to.
- **Infrastructure over Tooling:** Built to be the reliable foundation for your AI stack.

📖 [Read the detailed rationale →][why_codeweaver]

# Lawstronaut MCP 2.0

Connect [lawstronaut](https://mcp.lawstronaut.com) to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and any AI agent that speaks the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). Connect your AI to 115+ million laws and court cases!

 [Authentication](#Authentication) . [Setup](#setup) · [Tools](#tools)

---

## What is this?

Lawstronaut is the infrastructure layer that connects AI agents and software to millions of legal documents across 150+ jurisdictions, structured legal data, continuously updated, and ready to use via MCP.

## Authentication

Production MCP server: **`https://mcp.lawstronaut.com`**

Transport: **MCP over Streamable HTTP** (`POST /`).

Public server card (tool listing, no auth):  
`https://mcp.lawstronaut.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`

---

Lawstronaut MCP supports **Bearer token** and **OAuth 2.0** (`client_id` + `client_secret`). A paid subscription is required.

| Method | Best for | Tool listing | Tool calls |
|--------|----------|--------------|------------|
| Bearer token | CLI, scripts, clients without OAuth | No auth required | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| OAuth 2.0 | Cursor, VS Code, Claude, publishing platforms | No auth required | OAuth access token (auto-managed by client) |

### Get client ID, secret, or bearer token

1. Visit [lawstronaut.com](https://lawstronaut.com) and purchase a subscription.
2. Log in to the [developer portal](https://dev-portal.filerskeepersapi.co/).
3. Open **MCP server access** from the Home menu.
4. Create a **client ID** + **client secret** (OAuth) or a **bearer token**.

### Option A — Bearer token

Use the bearer token from **MCP server access**:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <your-token>
```

Set it in your environment:

```bash
export LAWSTRONAUT_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN="your-token-here"
```

Example configs: `cursor-mcp.json`, `vscode-mcp.json`, `claude-code.mcp.json`.

### Option B — OAuth 2.0 (client_id + client_secret)

Use the `client_id` and `client_secret` created under **MCP server access** in the [developer portal](https://dev-portal.filerskeepersapi.co/).

| Endpoint | URL |
|----------|-----|
| MCP server | `https://mcp.lawstronaut.com` |
| Authorization | `https://mcp.lawstronaut.com/oauth/authorize` |
| Token | `https://mcp.lawstronaut.com/oauth/token` |
| OAuth discovery | `https://mcp.lawstronaut.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Protected resource | `https://mcp.lawstronaut.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` |

**Flow:** `response_type=code` → redirect with `code` → exchange at `/oauth/token` with `grant_type=authorization_code`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `code`, and `redirect_uri`.

Clients that support MCP OAuth discovery only need the server URL — they handle the flow using your registered `client_id` / `client_secret`.

Example configs: `cursor-mcp-oauth.json`, `vscode-mcp-oauth.json`.

---
## Setup
Pick your client, paste the config, and authenticate with your lawstronaut account. Most clients open a browser window for OAuth the first time an agent uses a lawstronaut tools.

## Cursor

**Bearer token**

1. Copy `cursor-mcp.json` to `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global).
2. Export `LAWSTRONAUT_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN`.
3. Restart Cursor. Check **Output → MCP Logs** if connection fails.

**OAuth**

1. Copy `cursor-mcp-oauth.json` to `.cursor/mcp.json`.
2. Complete the OAuth sign-in when Cursor prompts you (uses your registered `client_id` / `client_secret`).

Docs: [Cursor MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp).

---

## VS Code (GitHub Copilot agent / MCP)

**Bearer token**

1. Copy `vscode-mcp.json` to `.vscode/mcp.json`, or merge into your [user MCP config](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/reference/mcp-configuration).
2. Run **MCP: List Servers** and enter your bearer token when prompted.

**OAuth**

1. Copy `vscode-mcp-oauth.json` to `.vscode/mcp.json`.
2. Sign in through VS Code when prompted.

Docs: [MCP configuration reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/reference/mcp-configuration).

---

## Claude Code (CLI)

**Bearer token — CLI**

```bash
export LAWSTRONAUT_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN="your-token-here"

claude mcp add --transport http lawstronaut-mcp https://mcp.lawstronaut.com \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $LAWSTRONAUT_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN"
```

**Bearer token — project file**

Copy `claude-code.mcp.json` to `.mcp.json` in your project root.

**OAuth**

Add the server URL only and complete OAuth when prompted:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http lawstronaut-mcp https://mcp.lawstronaut.com
```

Docs: [Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

---

## Claude Desktop (Anthropic app)

Claude Desktop is oriented toward **stdio** MCP servers. For this HTTP server, use **Cursor**, **VS Code**, or **Claude Code**, or any host that supports remote Streamable HTTP MCP.

Go to **Customize**, **Connectors**, click "**+**", **Add Custom Connector**, and fill the dialog:

---

## Other hosts (Continue, Zed, custom agents, etc.)

Any client that supports **MCP Streamable HTTP** can connect with:

- **URL:** `https://mcp.lawstronaut.com`
- **Bearer:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **OAuth:** use discovery at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with your `client_id` / `client_secret`

---

## Tools

- **list_jurisdictions** — List every country and state in the authenticated subscription (name, iso, type, documents_count). Call first to get valid ISO codes. Takes no parameters.

- **list_domains** — List top-level legal domains (id, domain_id, domain). Pass `domain_id` to `list_subdomains`.
  - `domain`: Filter by domain name (string, optional)
  - `limit`: Number of results to return (number, optional)
  - `next_id`: Next ID to paginate the results (number, optional)

- **list_subdomains** — List subdomains under one domain. Pass `subdomain_id` to `list_categories`.
  - `domain_id`: Filter by Domain ID (string, required)
  - `subdomain`: Filter by subdomain name (string, o

# Linkbreakers agent skills

The single source of truth for everything [Linkbreakers](https://linkbreakers.com) exposes to AI agents: skills, agent instructions, plugin manifests and a machine-readable discovery index.

Linkbreakers is lead capture infrastructure for the physical world. Every QR code or link runs a workflow (forms, conditions, password gates, multi-link pages, contact cards) that turns an anonymous scan into an identified visitor.

## Install the skills

Any agent supported by the [skills CLI](https://skills.sh) (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini, Cline and more):

```bash
npx skills add linkbreakers-com/agent-skills
```

### Claude Code plugin

Bundles the skills and the hosted Linkbreakers MCP servers:

```
/plugin marketplace add linkbreakers-com/agent-skills
/plugin install linkbreakers@linkbreakers
```

### Other Agent Plugins clients

This repository is an [Agent Plugin](https://agent-plugins.org/specification): `plugin.json`, `skills/` and `mcp.json` at the root.

## Skills

| Skill | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [create-tracked-qr-code](skills/create-tracked-qr-code/SKILL.md) | Create a link with a dynamic, tracked QR code (or one that opens a PDF, image or video) and change its destination later |
| [build-lead-capture-workflow](skills/build-lead-capture-workflow/SKILL.md) | Add forms, conditions and pages to a link and wire every branch |
| [read-visitors-and-leads](skills/read-visitors-and-leads/SKILL.md) | List, filter, sort and export captured visitors, events and funnels |
| [send-leads-to-webhooks](skills/send-leads-to-webhooks/SKILL.md) | Push scans and leads to a CRM or backend in real time |
| [identify-visitors-on-your-site](skills/identify-visitors-on-your-site/SKILL.md) | Tie a QR scan to a later signup or purchase with the lbid and identify API |
| [manage-custom-domains](skills/manage-custom-domains/SKILL.md) | Serve links from a branded domain and debug its DNS and certificate |
| [use-linkbreakers-cli](skills/use-linkbreakers-cli/SKILL.md) | Install and script the `linkbreakers` CLI |
| [connect-linkbreakers-mcp](skills/connect-linkbreakers-mcp/SKILL.md) | Connect an assistant to the Linkbreakers MCP server with OAuth |

## Linkbreakers for agents

| Surface | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Agent instructions | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) |
| Docs index for LLMs | https://linkbreakers.com/llms.txt |
| MCP server (your workspace, OAuth) | `https://mcp.linkbreakers.com` |
| Docs MCP server (no auth) | `https://linkbreakers.com/mcp` |
| REST API | `https://api.linkbreakers.com`, reference at https://linkbreakers.com/help/api |
| OpenAPI spec | https://api.linkbreakers.com/internal/openapi/api/v1/api.swagger.json |
| CLI | `brew install linkbreakers-com/tap/linkbreakers` (tap: https://github.com/linkbreakers-com/homebrew-tap), docs at https://linkbreakers.com/cli |
| SDKs | TypeScript (`npm i linkbreakers`), Python (`pip install linkbreakers`), Go, Java, Rust: https://linkbreakers.com/help/article/linkbreakers-developer-ecosystem-overview |

## discovery.json

[`discovery.json`](discovery.json) is the machine-readable index of all of the above, validated by [`schema/discovery.schema.json`](schema/discovery.schema.json). linkbreakers.com reads it at runtime from:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linkbreakers-com/agent-skills/main/discovery.json
```

Its `skills[]` array is generated from the `skills/` folders:

```bash
node scripts/build-discovery.mjs          # regenerate
node scripts/build-discovery.mjs --check  # what CI runs
```

## Contributing

Add a folder under `skills/` with a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter has `name` (same as the folder) and `description`, regenerate `discovery.json`, and open a pull request. Ground every step in the real API: check the OpenAPI spec rather than guessing.

## License

# GitHub Followers and Following Export MCP Server

An MCP server for the Mamba Labs GitHub Followers and Following Export actor on Apify. Export the followers and following lists of public GitHub accounts as flat rows.

## What's Inside

- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
- [Example prompts](#example-prompts)
- [Tool](#tool)
- [Inputs](#inputs)
- [Pricing](#pricing)
- [Full actor documentation](#full-actor-documentation)
- [License](#license)

## What it does

Give GitHub usernames or profile URLs. For each one you get a row per follower or followed account, with login, name, company, location, bio, profile URL, and user ID, and a free report row per list that states the count GitHub declares and whether the list was read to the end.

All of the work runs on Apify. This package is a thin client that starts the actor run, waits for it, and hands back the dataset rows.

## Quick start

You need Node.js 18 or newer and an Apify account with an API token.

Add this to your Claude Desktop config (`claude_desktop_config.json`), Cursor, or any MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mamba-github-followers-following-export": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@mambalabsdev/mcp-github-followers-following-export"
      ],
      "env": {
        "APIFY_TOKEN": "your-apify-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart the client. The `export_github_followers_following` tool appears.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- An Apify API token from [console.apify.com/account/integrations](https://console.apify.com/account/integrations), set as `APIFY_TOKEN`. The server lists its tool without a token; a call needs one.

## Example prompts

- "Export who sindresorhus follows on GitHub."
- "Get the first 500 followers of octocat with their locations."
- "Did this export reach the end of the followers list?"

## Tool

`export_github_followers_following`. One tool. Example arguments:

```json
{
  "users": [
    "sindresorhus"
  ],
  "list": "following",
  "max_results_per_list": 20
}
```

## Inputs

Every buyer facing input of the actor. Omitted inputs take the actor's own defaults.

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users` | array | no | Usernames or profile URLs of public GitHub accounts, up to 100 a run. Clay users: wrap a column in a one item list. |
| `list` | string | no | followers, following, or both (default). |
| `max_results_per_list` | number | no | Rows to return per list, from 1 to 100000. Default 1000. Each row is charged. Large lists also need a longer run timeout: about 400 rows a minute. |
| `github_token` | string | no | Optional. Your own GitHub token reads through the REST API at up to 5,000 requests an hour, with login, user ID, and avatar only: no name, company, location, or bio. Never stored or logged. |
| `max_charge_usd` | string | no | Optional. The run stops before a charge that would pass this amount. Summary rows are always returned. |

## Pricing

Pay per event on Apify, billed to your Apify account. Prices in USD.

| Event | Free plan | Bronze | Silver | Gold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user-row`, one follower or followed account returned | $0.002 | $0.0019 | $0.0018 | $0.0017 |
| `apify-actor-start`, per run start | $0.0015 | $0.0015 | $0.0015 | $0.0015 |

List reports, a user with no public account, and refused input are free. Mamba Labs pays the platform costs of the run, Apify proxy traffic included.

## Full actor documentation

[apify.com/mambalabs/github-followers-following-export](https://apify.com/mambalabs/github-followers-following-export)

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
