readme.markdown:
# upGrowth Growth Toolkit (MCP server)

A free, public, read-only [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server with 29 growth marketing tools. Connect it to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI or any MCP client and ask growth maths, SEO and AI-visibility questions in plain language.

- **Endpoint:** `https://upgrowth.in/connected-app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Alias: `https://mcp.upgrowth.in/mcp`
- **Auth:** none. No sign-up, no API key.
- **Data:** your inputs and the answers are never stored. We keep anonymous usage counts (event, tool name, host and a broad client type such as ChatGPT or Claude) in Cloudflare Workers Analytics Engine; no IP addresses. 28 of the 29 tools make no outside calls; `ai_crawler_access_check` fetches only the public `robots.txt` and `llms.txt` of the domain you name.
- **Official MCP Registry:** `in.upgrowth/growth-toolkit`
- **Docs and setup guide:** https://upgrowth.in/growth-toolkit-mcp/
- **Terms:** https://upgrowth.in/growth-toolkit-terms/
- **Version:** 1.4.2

Built and maintained by [upGrowth Digital](https://upgrowth.in/), a growth marketing consultancy in Pune, India.

## Connect it

**Claude (all plans):** Customize > Connectors > "+ Add" > "Add custom connector". Name it upGrowth, paste the endpoint URL, choose "No sign in" under Authentication and click Add. On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds it first under Organization settings > Connectors.

**ChatGPT (web):** Plugins > Add > "Add custom MCP server". Paste `https://mcp.upgrowth.in/mcp` as the server URL, set Authentication to "No authentication", then "Create as a plugin" and "Connect". In a chat, type `@upGrowth`. The ChatGPT address serves 28 tools (the call-booking tool is left out).

**Gemini CLI:** `gemini mcp add --transport http upgrowth https://upgrowth.in/connected-app/mcp`, or add to `~/.gemini/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "upgrowth": { "httpUrl": "https://upgrowth.in/connected-app/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http upgrowth https://upgrowth.in/connected-app/mcp
```

**Any other client:** point it at the endpoint with Streamable HTTP transport.

## Tools

### Ads, payments and unit economics
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `unit_economics` | CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC ratio and payback months |
| `max_affordable_cac` | The most you can pay per customer or per lead |
| `roas_check` | ROAS and break-even ROAS from spend, revenue and margin |
| `ad_budget_planner` | Ad budget needed to hit a customer target |
| `ppc_forecast` | Clicks, conversions, revenue and profit from a PPC budget |
| `acos_check` | Amazon ACoS, TACoS and break-even ACoS |
| `campaign_roi` | Marketing campaign ROI |
| `break_even` | Break-even units and revenue |
| `mdr_charges` | Card or payment gateway MDR, GST on it and net settlement |
| `customer_lifetime_value` | Repeat-purchase CLV, with optional discounting |

### Growth and reporting
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `growth_rate` | Period growth, CAGR and compound monthly growth |
| `period_change` | YoY, MoM or simple % change |
| `ytd_growth` | Year-to-date growth against last year |
| `growth_projection` | Revenue projection and doubling time |
| `ecommerce_metrics` | AOV, conversion rate and revenue per visitor |
| `attrition_rate` | Attrition and churn rate |
| `share_of_voice` | Share of voice across brands |

### SEO and AI visibility
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ai_crawler_access_check` | Whether a site's robots.txt blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and other AI crawlers |
| `robots_txt_generator` | robots.txt that allows or blocks AI crawlers by purpose (training, search, user fetch), never Googlebot |
| `schema_generator` | JSON-LD for FAQ, LocalBusiness, Organization, Article, Product, Person and Breadcrumb |
| `meta_tags_builder` | Title, meta description, Open Graph and Twitter card tags |
| `content_seo_check` | Word count, keyword density and readability of pasted text |
| `seo_roi` | SEO return and break-even traffic |

### Creator and publisher income
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `youtube_earnings` | YouTube earnings estimate and Partner Program watch-hour progress |
| `instagram_earnings` | Instagram creator earnings estimate |
| `engagement_rate` | Engagement rate by followers or reach |
| `website_ad_revenue` | AdSense-style website ad revenue |

### Research and contact
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `find_growth_moves` | Documented 2026 growth moves by Indian companies (fintech, ecommerce, healthtech, SaaS) from upGrowth's [Growth Moves](https://upgrowth.in/growth-moves/) research, each with a source link |
| `book_strategy_call` | Returns a link to book a call with upGrowth |

Every tool is annotated `readOnlyHint: true` and `destructiveHint: false`.

## Example prompts

- "My CAC is Rs 2,000, LTV Rs 9,000 and monthly margin per customer Rs 750. What's my LTV:CAC and payback?"
- "I spent Rs 50,000 on Meta and made Rs 2,10,000 at 40% margin. Am I above break-even ROAS?"
- "Is GPTBot or ClaudeBot blocked on example.com?"
- "Write a robots.txt that blocks AI training bots but allows AI search."
- "Generate LocalBusiness schema for a dental clinic in Pune."
- "Estimate monthly YouTube earnings for 200,000 views at Rs 80 RPM."

## Repository layout

```
src/worker.mjs          Cloudflare Worker (the deployed server, single file, data inlined)
php/mcp.php             Equivalent PHP implementation (same tools, same output)
php/data/               Growth Moves dataset used by find_growth_moves (PHP copy)
tests/smoke.mjs         Smoke test against src/worker.mjs
server.json             Official MCP Registry entry
wrangler.toml           Example Wrangler config
```

## Run it yourself

**Cloudflare Workers:**

```bash
npx wrangler dev          # local
npx wrangler deploy       # set your own routes in wrangler.toml first
```

**PHP 8+:** copy `php/` to any web server and POST JSON-RPC to `mcp.php`.

**Test:**

```bash
node tests/smoke.mjs
```

readme.markdown:
Cairn Memory Keep important context between AI sessions. Change it when things change. English · 繁體中文 See an example · Where to start · Local setup · Hosted setup · Limitations · Privacy **Cairn Memory** is Cairn.ink's open-source AI memory toolkit for Claude Code and Codex, with local MCP tools or cloud automatic memory. Visit [Cairn.ink](https://cairn.ink), install [@cairn-ink/memory on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cairn-ink/memory), or view the [Cairn Memory GitHub repository](https://github.com/Cairn-ink/cairn-memory). Starting a new AI session often means repeating your preferences and project decisions. Cairn provides memory tools to save that context between sessions, inspect the submitted text behind each memory, and update it when things change. ## A preference changes Suppose you save **“Keep my reports short.”** Later, you decide you need detailed reports. You can inspect the old memory and its source text, correct the saved preference, or forget it so it is no longer available for active recall. This is an **illustrated explicit-tool example**, not a chat-client screenshot. The local preview uses tools to save, inspect, correct and forget; it does not automatically read your conversations. - **Inspect the source.** Read the source text stored with a memory. A receipt does not prove that the memory is true or correctly interpreted. - **Correct what changed.** Update the memory at the revision you inspected. - **Forget what should go.** Remove a memory from active recall. [Deletion and backup boundaries](#local-privacy-and-control) apply. A **Source Receipt** is the submitted text attached to a memory. It helps you check what was supplied when the memory was saved or corrected. It is not a verified transcript of the whole conversation or proof of human intent. ## Cairn Memory and Cairn **Cairn Memory** is the open-source toolkit in this repository for saving, inspecting and changing AI memory. **[Cairn](https://cairn.ink)** is the hosted shared memory map for people and AI, where people organize, review and share knowledge. This repository includes local memory tools and connectors to the hosted Cairn service. Each path has its own setup and feature boundaries. Local use does not require a Cairn account; hosted connections require a compatible service and authentication. ## Choose your starting point | You want to… | Start here | What you need | | --- | --- | --- | | Understand the idea before installing | [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) or the [recorded walkthrough](#watch-the-recorded-walkthrough) | No installation or account | | Try the open-source tools on your computer | [Local preview setup](#try-the-local-memory-layer) or [Windows guide](docs/windows-install.md) | Terminal setup; Linux x64 and a bounded native Windows x64 check; no Cairn account | | Use the documented hosted Claude Code or Codex connection | [Hosted setup](#existing-hosted-integration) | A compatible hosted service and authentication; separate from local-preview client support | | Build on the memory layer | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [MCP tools](docs/standalone-mcp.md) | JavaScript or MCP integration work | If you use Claude or Codex but do not usually install tools from a terminal, start with the example and recorded walkthrough. This preview requires setup; check the [tested client paths](docs/promotion-claims.md#supported-paths) before connecting your AI tool. ## Current preview Cairn's open-source memory layer stores memories in your own SQLite file and exposes them through MCP or JavaScript. No Cairn account is needed for local use. **Developer preview.** Installed persistence and a narrow real-model memory loop have [retained evidence](docs/promotion-claims.md). Default extraction still fails our source-support bar; see [known limitations](docs/limitations.md). Save, inspect, correct and forget work without a model key. Semantic recall requires your OpenAI key and sends selected context to that provider. ## Watch the recorded walkthrough [Watch the 36-second model-free demo (MP4)](docs/promotion/demo/cairn-memory-preview.mp4). This records the memory tools running, rather than a conversation in Claude or Codex. “Model-free” means no AI model is called during the walkthrough. For long-conversation results, see the [four-case real-model pilot](docs/evidence/long-history-live-pilot.md). It is an opt-in diagnostic with one failed Cairn answer, not a measurement of long-term default-client recall reliability. [Known limitations](docs/limitations.md)
Open the recorded tool walkthrough (GIF) The demo below records the **model-free loop**: save, restart, inspect, correct and forget. Its recall step reports `model_not_configured`. # FIDE Laws of Chess on Arxo

**Explore a chess arbiter's decision through a pinned model, explicit facts and an inspectable answer.** Ten retained fictional cases cover illegal moves, flag fall, rapid/blitz exceptions, recording and arbiter judgment.

**Node.js 20+ · ESM · canon package 0.1.0 · model 0.1.1 · FIDE edition effective 1 January 2023**

[Start in Node.js](#start-in-nodejs) · [Cases](#choose-a-case) · [Evidence](#inspect-the-evidence) · [Depth](#formalization-depth) · [Submit a case](https://github.com/arxohq/arxo-fide-chess/issues/new) · [Source repository](https://github.com/arxohq/arxo-fide-chess)

This is an independent open-source teaching and research demonstration. For an actual chess ruling, use the authentic FIDE Laws and the competent arbiter. Source text and model scope are pinned; the package does not claim general chess-engine capability or complete formalization.

## Start in Node.js

Requirements: **Node.js 20+**. The example uses ES modules; keep the `.mjs`
extension. This recipe was checked on macOS arm64 with Node.js 20.20.2 on
14 October 2026. No global CLI, Git clone or MCP client is needed for this route.

Create a fresh directory, open a terminal there, then run:

```sh
npm init -y
npm install --ignore-scripts @arxo/canon-fide-chess@0.1.0 @arxo/law@0.4.3
```

Save this as `example.mjs`, then run `node example.mjs`:

```js
import { open } from '@arxo/law';
import { loadModel } from '@arxo/canon-fide-chess/chess';
import { game, white, getCaseInput } from '@arxo/canon-fide-chess/examples/arbiter';

const model = await loadModel();
const chess = await open(model.spec, {
  offline: true,
  local: { packages: { [model.spec]: model.package } },
});

const input = getCaseInput('SecondIllegal');
const loss = await chess.truth('game_lost_by', [game, white], input);
const draw = await chess.truth('game_drawn', [game], input);
console.log(loss.evaluationStatus, loss.truthStatus); // COMPUTED, TRUE_ONLY
console.log(draw.evaluationStatus, draw.truthStatus); // COMPUTED, NEITHER
```

The two output lines are **loss**, then **draw**:

```text
COMPUTED TRUE_ONLY
COMPUTED NEITHER
```

`COMPUTED` means the query was evaluated. `TRUE_ONLY` means it has positive
support and no negative support. `NEITHER` means neither polarity is supported;
it does not establish that the proposition is false.

Now replace only `getCaseInput('SecondIllegal')` with
`getCaseInput('SecondIllegalNoMate')` and run `node example.mjs` again:

```text
REQUIRES_JUDGMENT NEITHER
COMPUTED TRUE_ONLY
```

The second line now establishes a draw. This case supplies the fact that the
opponent cannot checkmate by any legal series. The separate loss query still
requests an arbiter's assessment because other reachable loss grounds remain
unresolved. Read both status fields; `REQUIRES_JUDGMENT` identifies an assessment
the model does not decide on its own.

To try another retained episode, choose a name from [the case table](#choose-a-case).
To propose your own episode, [open an issue](https://github.com/arxohq/arxo-fide-chess/issues/new)
with the case facts, legal date, query, package/runtime versions, output and the
FIDE clause or model rule you think should give a different answer. Use a
fictional or anonymized case.

The SDK executes the rules through `@arxo/law-engine@0.5.3`. Installation alone does not register this distribution in the SDK's automatic canon resolver: keep the explicit `local.packages` handoff above. The loader implements no chess decisions or formulas.

## Use as an MCP server

The separate native MCP wrapper runs the same pinned model over stdio:

```sh
npx -y @arxo/mcp-fide-chess@0.1.0
```

Node.js 20+, Linux x64 or macOS arm64. [Client configuration, HTTP endpoint, inputs and limitations](docs/mcp.md) · [OCI recipe](docs/mcp-release.md) · [npm recipe](docs/mcp-npm-release.md) · [Accepted delivery](docs/mcp-release.md#accepted-delivery--14-october-2026). This MCP delivery is separate from the Node.js route above.

## Choose a case

| `getCaseInput(name)` | Episode | Checked question and result |
|---|---|---|
| `TouchIntentUnknown` | A movable own piece; intentional touch not adjudicated | `must_move_first_touched_piece`: `REQUIRES_JUDGMENT / NEITHER` |
| `FirstIllegal` | One completed illegal move | Loss: `REQUIRES_JUDGMENT / NEITHER`; draw: `COMPUTED / NEITHER` |
| `SecondIllegal` | Two illegal moves under the model's specified closure | Loss: `COMPUTED / TRUE_ONLY` |
| `SecondIllegalNoMate` | Two illegal moves; inability to checkmate established | Draw: `COMPUTED / TRUE_ONLY` |
| `FlagFall` | Flag observed, time control not completed, mate possible | Loss: `COMPUTED / TRUE_ONLY` |
| `FlagFallNoMate` | The same flag; inability to checkmate established | Draw: `COMPUTED / TRUE_ONLY` |
| `RapidFirstIllegal` | Rapid 15+10; first illegal move | Opponent receives 60 seconds; 120-second query is `NEITHER` |
| `BlitzFirstIllegalCompetitive` | Blitz 3+2 under competitive rules B.2 | Opponent receives 120 seconds; 60-second query is `NEITHER` |
| `ShortOfTimeRecording` | Standard chess, no increment, 240 seconds left | `must_record_moves`: `COMPUTED / FALSE_ONLY` |
| `DeviceWarning` | Electronic device evident; arbiter gave a warning | Loss and differing-penalty queries: `COMPUTED / TRUE_ONLY` |

All 18 original case/query expectations are retained and checked. The fixture export provides `caseNames`, `game`, `white`, `black`, `king`, `CaseName` and `getCaseInput(name)`. Each call returns an independent copy; an unknown name throws `RangeError`.

## Facts and arbiter judgments

`getCaseInput` preserves the CLI's canonical assertions, constants, context and options. The loader supplies neither absent facts nor adjudications. The model's explicitly declared closures are part of its rules; they are not a general assumption that a missing fact is false.

For touch-move, use the two declared arguments — player and piece:

```js
import { open } from '@arxo/law';
import { loadModel } from '@arxo/cano

readme.markdown:
# BALLDONTLIE MCP Server

Remote Model Context Protocol server for the BALLDONTLIE sports API. The tool catalog is generated from the vendored public OpenAPI specifications so endpoint methods, paths, parameters, and constraints stay aligned with the API source.

The current generated surface contains 529 tools from 27 specifications: Account, ATP, Bundesliga, college baseball, Counter-Strike, Dota 2, EPL, F1, FIFA World Cup, La Liga, Ligue 1, League of Legends, MLB, MLS, MMA, NBA, NCAAB, NCAAF, NCAAW, NFL, NHL, PGA, Serie A, UCL, Valorant, WNBA, and WTA. `/health` reports the authoritative runtime count and deployed revision.

## Authentication

Every MCP request requires a BALLDONTLIE API key:

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

Initialization, tool listing, authenticated documentation, and API operations that are public outside the MCP validate the supplied key before proceeding. Other tool calls forward only the Authorization header to the corresponding authenticated BALLDONTLIE endpoint.

Public service metadata is limited to `/health` and `/.well-known/mcp-config`. `/api/docs` requires a valid API key.

## Sensitive Account tools

The complete Account API surface is registered, but the following tools are disabled by default:

- `account_signup`
- `account_rotate_api_key`
- `account_change_subscription`
- `account_cancel_subscription`
- `account_create_checkout`
- `account_get_billing_portal`

They can create credentials, change billing state, or return sensitive hosted billing-session URLs. A deployment must set `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_ACCOUNT_TOOLS=true` exactly to enable them. Enabling the flag means those values may intentionally enter the authenticated caller's MCP transcript. Other spellings, casing, or whitespace fail closed.

`account_get_me` remains available but always omits the `api_key` response field.

## MCP request example

```bash
curl https://mcp.balldontlie.io/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "nba_get_teams",
      "arguments": {}
    }
  }'
```

Use `tools/list` to retrieve the current catalog, input schemas, and MCP read-only/destructive annotations.

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm run check:openapi
npm test
npm run build
```

The tests independently compare every generated operation and input against all vendored specifications. They also cover legacy tool-name compatibility, exact array query serialization, path/body dispatch, credential-safe errors and logs, API-key validation limits, and Account safety controls. Tests never call a live Account mutation.

### Updating from the API source

1. Copy `balldontlie-2/marketing/public/openapi.yml` to `openapi.yml`.
2. Copy every `balldontlie-2/marketing/public/openapi/*.yml` file into `openapi/`.
3. Update `scripts/openapi-source.json` to the source API commit.
4. Run `npm run generate:openapi`.
5. Run `npm test` and `npm run build`.

Generated `src/tools/*.ts`, `src/schemas/*.ts`, and registry files are checked in and must not be edited manually. Runtime does not parse YAML and has no production YAML-parser dependency.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port |
| `BACKEND_API_URL` | `https://api.balldontlie.io` | BALLDONTLIE API base URL |
| `API_TIMEOUT` | `30000` | Upstream timeout in milliseconds |
| `ENABLE_DEBUG` | `false` | Logs only method, query-free path, and query-field count |
| `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_ACCOUNT_TOOLS` | `false` | Enables sensitive Account tools only when exactly `true` |
| `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` | `1` in production, `0` otherwise | Validated trusted proxy hop count; only `0` or `1` is accepted |
| `ENABLE_TRACING` | `false` | Enables Datadog tracing when an agent host is configured |

Authorization values, query values, request bodies, raw upstream errors, API-key responses, and hosted billing-session URLs are excluded from server logs and tracing tags.

# Browserless MCP Server

MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for [Browserless.io](https://browserless.io) — expose the Browserless smart scraper API to LLM clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Windsurf.

## Quick Start

Get an API token from [browserless.io](https://browserless.io) (free tier available), then point your MCP client at the hosted server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "browserless": {
      "url": "https://mcp.browserless.io/mcp?token=your-token-here"
    }
  }
}
```

No local install — see [Configuration](#configuration) for per-client snippets.

## Tools

| Tool                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `browserless_smartscraper` | Scrape a single webpage and return its content as markdown or HTML, or AI-extracted JSON and summaries. Handles JavaScript-heavy pages and anti-bot measures automatically. For content across multiple pages, use `browserless_crawl`; to list a site's URLs, use `browserless_map`.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `browserless_search`       | Search the web using Browserless and optionally scrape each result. Supports web, news, and image search with geo-targeting and time filters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `browserless_map`          | Discover and map all URLs on a website. Scans via sitemaps and link extraction. Returns URLs with optional titles and descriptions. Useful for site audits and content discovery.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `browserless_crawl`        | Crawl a website and scrape every discovered page. Supports depth control, path filtering, sitemap strategies, and configurable scrape options. Returns scraped content and metadata for each page.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `browserless_performance`  | Run Lighthouse audits on any URL. Returns category scores inline and saves the full JSON report outside the conversation: a local path (stdio) or authenticated single-use download URL (HTTP). Download to disk and inspect only needed fields with `jq`; files expire after 15 minutes or when the MCP session ends. Optionally filter by category, emulate a mobile or desktop device, supply a custom Lighthouse config, or supply performance budgets. |
| `browserless_function`     | Execute custom Puppeteer JavaScript on the Browserless cloud. The function receives a `page` object and optional `context`; return `{ data, type }` to control the payload and Content-Type.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `browserless_export`       | Export a webpage via the Browserless `/export` API. Fetches the URL and returns its native content (HTML, PDF, image, etc.) with automatic content-type detection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `browserless_agent`        | Drive a persistent browser session via a ReAct loop: snapshot the page, plan, batch interactions (click, type, scroll, evaluate, etc.), and re-snapshot. Uses ref-based selectors derived from snapshots, supports multi-tab workflows, screenshots, captcha solving, live URLs, and file upload/download (captured downloads auto-surface as handles; bytes never enter context).                                                                          |
| `browserless_skill`        | Load an on-demand recipe for a non-trivial page mechanic (shadow DOM, cookie consent, modals, captchas, dynamic content, snapshot misses, screenshots, tabs). Companion to `browserless_agent`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `browserless_profiles`     | List the authentication profiles saved for the current token, with cookie and origin counts. Pass a profile's name as `profile`

# Bugasura MCP Server **Connect AI assistants directly to your test management workspace.** Bugasura MCP Server enables AI tools like Claude, VS Code Copilot, and Cursor to interact with your Bugasura projects—manage test cases, track issues, plan sprints, and more—all through natural language. --- ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 3.5 | What changed | 3.4 | 3.5 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Starting a TestPert sprint from its requirements | `bugasura_testpert_start_skip_testplan` | `bugasura_testpert_start_from_requirements`. Same inputs and behaviour; the old name wrongly suggested it skips the test plan, which it builds | ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 3.3 | What changed | 3.2 | 3.3 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Requirement ↔ test case links | `bugasura_link_unlink_requirement_testcases` with `is_delete` | `bugasura_link_requirement_testcases` and `bugasura_unlink_requirement_testcases` (destructive); both take comma-separated `testcase_ids` | | Coda, Jira, Confluence and Figma imports (10 tools) | Offered on every transport | Local (STDIO) only. They take that service's API token as an argument, so the hosted server no longer lists them and refuses calls to them | ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 3.0 Authentication moved to OAuth 2.0 sign-in. If you're upgrading from 2.x: | What changed | 2.x | 3.0 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Hosted (HTTP) authentication | `X-Bugasura-API-Key` header or `Authorization: Basic ` in the client config | Sign in from the MCP client: it opens the Bugasura login + consent page once, then refreshes tokens silently. No key in any config file. | | `api_key` tool parameter | Present on every tool | Removed. Tools never accept a key; the assistant must not ask for one. | | STDIO (local subprocess) | `BUGASURA_API_KEY` env var | Unchanged — the env var is the only credential source for STDIO. | | Prompt | `setup_api_key` | `connect_bugasura` | | Server requirements (HTTP) | none | `MCP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `BUGASURA_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `BUGASURA_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (see *Deploying the OAuth sign-in*) | ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 2.0 If you're upgrading from 1.x, update your client configuration: | What changed | 1.x | 2.0 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Tool names | `create_issue`, `list_teams`, … | `bugasura_create_issue`, `bugasura_list_teams`, … (prefixed to coexist with other MCP servers) | | Default HTTP endpoint | `/sse` (SSE) | `/mcp` (streamable HTTP) | | List/find responses | `{status, project_list, …}` (upstream shape) | Standard pagination envelope `{status, total, count, offset, items, has_more, next_offset}` — legacy keys remain as extras for one release | 1.x clients pointed at `/sse` must migrate to `/mcp` — SSE has been removed. --- ## Features - 📋 **Test Case Management** - Create, update, delete, and search test cases - 💬 **Test Case Comments** - Add, update, delete, and list comments on test cases with pagination and filtering - 🐛 **Issue Tracking** - Report, manage, and delete bugs with rich context - 💬 **Issue Comments** - Add, update, delete, and list comments on issues with pagination and filtering - 📝 **Requirements Management** - Create, organize, and manage product requirements with folder structure - 📚 **Knowledge Base** - Upload, list, star, and delete documents in a project's knowledge base, with folders created on demand; import from a website, Coda, Jira, Confluence or Figma - 🏃 **Sprint Planning** - Create, update, delete, and manage agile sprints - 🏁 **Test Runs** - Create one-time or scheduled (recurring) runs, edit/rerun/delete them, pick environments and app builds, and add test cases — all by name or ID - 🧪 **Test Data** - Manage a project's test data environments (create, rename, duplicate, delete), their variables and the Globals scope, plus test data files (upload, read, download, delete), app builds and file categories — all by name or ID - 🤖 **Testpert Sprints** - Full AI-driven test enrichment flow: upload specs, answer requirement questions, edit the test plan, and generate test cases automatically - 👥 **Team Collaboration** - Assign work using names or emails (auto-resolves to user IDs) - 👤 **Team Member Management** - Add, update roles, and remove team members using team names or IDs - 🔍 **Smart Discovery** - Find projects and teams without memorizing IDs - 🤖 **Interactive Workflows** - Guided context selection for all operations --- ## Quick Start ### 1. Have a Bugasura account That's all the hosted server needs. On first use your AI tool opens the Bugasura sign-in page in your browser; approve once and you're connected. Tokens refresh automatically for 30 days. An API key is only needed for the local STDIO setup described under *Local Development*. ### 2. Install the MCP Server Add the server URL to your AI tool. No headers, no keys: the client discovers the OAuth sign-in from the server and walks you through it.
Claude Desktop Open Claude Desktop → Settings → Connectors → Add Custom Connector - Name: `Bugasura` - URL: `https://mcp.bugasura.io/mcp` Click **Connect**, sign in to Bugasura, and click **Allow** on the consent page.
VS Code [Install in VS Code](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=bugasura&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A//mcp.bugasura.io/mcp%22%7D), or add to your VS Code MCP config: ```json { "servers": { "bugasura": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.bugasura.io/mcp" } } } ``` VS Code detects the OAuth sign-in and opens the browser the first time a tool is used. name: Camberstack: Google Ads

readme.markdown:
# Camberstack: Google Ads, Search Console, GA4, Merchant Center and Tag Manager MCP server for Claude and ChatGPT

Connect **Google Ads, Search Console (GSC), Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Merchant Center (GMC) and Tag Manager (GTM)** to Claude,
ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client with one Google sign-in, and use them together: the searches you pay for that already rank,
whether ad clicks convert on the landing page, which disapproved products were earning in Shopping, whether the tags behind
your conversions fire where they should. Your AI reads with
read-only tools and can propose changes, from negative keywords to whole Search, Performance Max, Display and
YouTube campaigns, GA4 key events, Merchant Center product fixes and Tag Manager tags. **Nothing changes until you approve a specific
proposal**, and risky changes and deletions Google can't reverse are flagged first. No developer token, API keys
or Google Cloud project. A demo account lets anyone try every tool first.

<sub>Demo account 000-000-0001: sample data for a fictional plumbing business.</sub>

Hosted: **https://camberstack.io/mcp**. Free: every tool and all five services on 1 Google Ads account, with 10 applied
changes every 30 days (reading and proposing are never limited). Plus $7/mo: unlimited changes on 1 account. Pro $15/mo:
up to 5 accounts. Agency $49/mo: up to 25.

**Setup guides, with screenshots and troubleshooting:** [Connect Google Ads to Claude](https://camberstack.io/google-ads-claude) ·
[Connect Google Ads to ChatGPT](https://camberstack.io/google-ads-chatgpt) · [every tool](https://camberstack.io/tools) ·
[Cursor, VS Code and others](https://camberstack.io/#setup)

## Ask it things like

- "Which searches am I paying for that already rank in the top 3 organically?"
- "Which landing pages get ad clicks but no conversions?"
- "Why were my best-selling products disapproved, and what were they earning in Shopping ads?"
- "Find search terms wasting money this month and propose negative keywords."
- "Build a Search campaign for our new service page, paused, with 3 ad groups."
- "Is my Google Ads conversion tag set up right in Tag Manager?"
- "Which Search Console queries on page 2 would be worth the most clicks if they moved up?"

## What it does

- **[Google Ads](https://camberstack.io/):** account overview with what needs attention, any read-only GAQL query, Keyword Planner ideas and
  metrics, and proposals that add negatives, change budgets, bids and targeting, edit ads, or build whole Search,
  Performance Max, Display and YouTube (Demand Gen) campaigns, always created paused.
- **[Search Console](https://camberstack.io/google-search-console-mcp):** site summary, performance by query, page, country or device, rising and falling queries,
  page-2 opportunities, URL inspection, sitemaps.
- **[GA4](https://camberstack.io/google-analytics-mcp):** landing-page and custom reports, properties and streams, key events and Google Ads links.
- **[Merchant Center](https://camberstack.io/google-merchant-center-mcp):** product issues, disapproved products joined with what they earned in Shopping ads, and
  product fixes as overrides that never touch your feed.
- **[Tag Manager](https://camberstack.io/google-tag-manager-mcp):** containers, tags and triggers with tracking problems flagged (a conversion tag on every page,
  no Conversion Linker, retired Universal Analytics), and proposals that add, pause or delete tags and publish.
- **Across them:** searches you pay for that already rank organically, and landing-page speed from real Chrome users.

Every change is a proposal: Camberstack checks it against the live account, dry-runs it with Google where it can,
and shows a plain-English summary. Risky changes are flagged with ⚠, and nothing is applied until you approve.
Full tool reference: [camberstack.io/tools](https://camberstack.io/tools).

## Security and sign-in

You sign in with Google and grant only the services you want: Google Ads, Search Console, Analytics, Merchant
Center or Tag Manager, each addable later from a one-click link. Your Google token is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never
leaves the server; your AI app gets Camberstack's own tokens, stored only as hashes. Disconnecting revokes
Google access and deletes the stored credentials.

Running it yourself, environment variables and implementation notes: [docs/INTERNALS.md](docs/INTERNALS.md).

# CheckFlow MCP Server

The official MCP server for [CheckFlow](https://checkflow.io), the checklist and process software. Connect an AI assistant to your CheckFlow workspace and ask in plain language: start a checklist, tell me what is overdue, fill in this task, turn this procedure into a template.

The server is hosted by CheckFlow. There is nothing to install or run: you add the address below to your MCP client and sign in with your CheckFlow account, or send an API key. This repository holds the documentation and the [`server.json`](server.json) published to the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io); the server's code is not open source.

| | |
|---|---|
| Server address (United States) | `https://api.checkflow.io/mcp` |
| Server address (Europe) | `https://api-eu.checkflow.io/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP, stateless (JSON responses, no sessions, no event stream) |
| Authentication | Sign in with your CheckFlow account (OAuth 2.1, the MCP authorization specification), or an API key in the `X-API-KEY` header |
| Tools | 147, in eight families |
| Resources | 1, the template authoring guide |
| Plans | Every CheckFlow plan, and the 14-day free trial |
| Full documentation | [docs.checkflow.io/docs/mcp/overview](https://docs.checkflow.io/docs/mcp/overview) |

## What you can ask for

| You ask | The assistant |
|---|---|
| "What's on my plate this week?" | Reads your Tasks grid, filtered to tasks due this week. |
| "Start an Invoice Review for INV-2041, due Friday, and assign the approval to Sarah." | Creates the checklist from the Invoice Review template, sets the due date and assigns the task. |
| "Mark the bank details check as done and note that the IBAN was verified by phone." | Fills in the task's fields, adds a comment and completes the task. |
| "Which supplier onboardings have been stuck for more than two weeks?" | Searches checklists and reads their activity. |
| "Turn this procedure document into a template." | Reads the authoring guide, writes a template, validates it, fixes what the validator reports and publishes it. |
| "Add these twelve suppliers to the Suppliers Data Set." | Creates the records in one bulk call. |
| "Set up a checklist every Monday at 9 am for the weekly stock check." | Creates a schedule. |

The assistant runs on its own provider's AI, not CheckFlow's, so it uses none of your workspace's AI credits.

## Two ways to connect

- **Sign in with your CheckFlow account.** The client opens CheckFlow in your browser, you sign in and choose Allow, and the assistant then works as you. There is no key to copy or store. This is the only way to connect claude.ai, Claude Desktop's Connectors screen, the Claude mobile apps and ChatGPT.
- **An API key**, sent in the `X-API-KEY` header. This is for clients that cannot sign in, for an assistant that should act as somebody other than you or as the workspace, and for scripts.

## Before you start

1. **Use your region's address.** Workspaces in the United States use `https://api.checkflow.io/mcp`; workspaces in Europe use `https://api-eu.checkflow.io/mcp`. A request to the other region is refused with `WRONG_REGION`, and the message names the right address.
2. **Check you're allowed to connect.** An Administrator can turn off **Allow AI assistants to connect** on the AI tab of Team Management; it is on unless someone has turned it off. Members need the **AI.Assistant** permission, which new Members are given and an Administrator can grant or remove on the Users tab. Administrators don't need it. Guests can't connect an assistant.
3. **For an API key only:** an Administrator creates keys on the API & Integrations tab of Team Management. For a personal assistant, create a key that acts as you. See [Creating an API key](https://docs.checkflow.io/docs/api-v3/authentication). You don't need a key to sign in.

The examples use the United States address; use the Europe address if your workspace is in Europe.

## Signing in

1. Your browser opens a CheckFlow page that names the assistant asking to connect.
2. Sign in the way you normally do: with your email and password, with Google or Microsoft, or with your company's single sign-on. For single sign-on, enter your workspace's address (for example `acme` for acme.checkflow.io) and CheckFlow sends you to your company's sign-in page.
3. CheckFlow shows what the assistant will be able to do, which workspace it is for and the address it will send you back to. Check them, then click **Allow**.
4. Your browser returns to the assistant, which is now connected.

The assistant works as you, in the workspace you were signed in to. If you belong to more than one workspace, switch to the right one in CheckFlow before you connect; to connect another workspace too, add the server a second time and connect it while that workspace is selected. The connection lasts until you or an Administrator disconnects it, or until it goes unused for 30 days. It also stops working if you leave the workspace or are made a Guest.

## Connect a client

### Claude (web, desktop and mobile)

1. In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, and choose **Add custom connector**.
2. Name it CheckFlow, enter your server address, and add it.
3. Click **Connect** and sign in.

A connector you add on the web is also available in the Claude Desktop and mobile apps. On a Team or Enterprise plan, an Owner may need to add the connector for your organisation before members can connect it.

### ChatGPT

ChatGPT connects to a custom MCP server in developer mode. Follow OpenAI's instructions for connecting a remote MCP server, give it your server address, and choose OAuth as the authentication. ChatGPT finds CheckFlow's sign-in page on its own, so there is nothing else to configure. Then sign in.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http checkflow https://api.checkflow.io/mcp
```

Then, in Claude Code, run `/mcp`, choose `checkflow` and **Authenticate**. Your browser opens so that you can s

# Clipwright clients

Open-source clients for [Clipwright](https://clipwright.io/?ref=github): an API that turns a
script into a short video of an actor speaking it, or a script or a short brief
into a faceless video without an on-camera presenter: narration over an opening
animated clip and image scenes, ending with the narration (select 30–90 seconds;
it runs 25 seconds or more, usually at most a quarter past the selection and 90; a longer narration runs to its end). Your agent quotes the price for free,
starts the render, and gets a video URL back. Clipwright returns the
file; it does not publish anywhere.

| Package | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`@clipwright/mcp-server`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clipwright/mcp-server) | MCP server over stdio for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline and any other MCP host |
| [`@clipwright/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clipwright/cli) | command-line client (`clipwright`, `clipwright-cli`) |
| [`@clipwright/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clipwright/sdk) | TypeScript client |
| [`@clipwright/core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clipwright/core) | shared request and response schemas (zod) |

## Claude Code plugin

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add seocombat/clipwright-mcp
claude plugin install clipwright@clipwright
```

The plugin connects the hosted server at `https://mcp.clipwright.io/mcp` and
adds a skill that tells the agent to quote before it spends credits. Run `/mcp`
in a session, choose `clipwright` and sign in with your Clipwright account: no
key goes into a config file. The same repository is a Cursor plugin
(`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, `mcp.json`).

## n8n

n8n's built-in MCP Client node reaches the hosted server with a key; no community
node is needed. [`n8n/clipwright-ugc.json`](n8n/clipwright-ugc.json) is a workflow
to import: it quotes a script, stops if the quote is above `max_credits`, starts
the render and polls `get_run` every 15 seconds until the run ends. The whole
workflow ran on n8n Cloud on 2026-10-20 and returned the MP4; n8n's OAuth
credential has not been tried with Clipwright yet. Setup:
[`packages/mcp-server/README.md`](packages/mcp-server/README.md#n8n).

## MCP server in one line

```bash
claude mcp add clipwright -e CLIPWRIGHT_API_KEY=cw_... -- npx -y -p @clipwright/mcp-server clipwright-mcp
```

Put your own key from [app.clipwright.io/api-keys](https://app.clipwright.io/api-keys)
in place of `cw_...`. It needs Node.js 20 or newer. Other hosts, the tool list and
the environment variables: [`packages/mcp-server/README.md`](packages/mcp-server/README.md).

Quotes, voices, actors and the balance are free. Renders spend credits: an
account opened by signing up starts with 420 trial credits, enough for one
90-second faceless video. Buy more at
[clipwright.io/pricing](https://clipwright.io/pricing?ref=github).

## Build from source

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm -r build
```

This repository mirrors the client packages of the Clipwright monorepo; each
release is synced here from there. Documentation: [clipwright.io/docs](https://clipwright.io/docs?ref=github).
Privacy: [clipwright.io/privacy](https://clipwright.io/privacy).

MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

readme.markdown:
# Cycloid MCP Server

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides seamless integration with the Cycloid platform, enabling AI assistants to interact with Cycloid's infrastructure management capabilities through natural language.

## Overview

The Cycloid MCP Server bridges the gap between AI assistants and Cycloid's powerful infrastructure automation platform. It enables users to:

- **Discover and explore** available blueprints and service catalogs
- **Create and manage** infrastructure stacks using Cycloid's blueprints
- **Interact naturally** with complex infrastructure workflows through AI assistants
- **Leverage Cycloid's expertise** in infrastructure as code and automation

## Available Tools

- **`CYCLOID_BLUEPRINT_LIST`**: List all available blueprints with their details
- **`CYCLOID_BLUEPRINT_STACK_CREATE`**: Create stacks from blueprints with interactive elicitation
- **`CYCLOID_STACKFORMS_VALIDATE`**: Validate StackForms configuration files
- **`CYCLOID_CATALOG_REPO_LIST`**: List service catalog repositories
- **`CYCLOID_EVENT_LIST`**: List organization events with optional filters (`begin`, `end`, `severity`, `type`)
- **`CYCLOID_PIPELINE_LIST`**: List all pipelines from Cycloid

## Available Resources

- **`cycloid://blueprints`**: Access to blueprint information
- **`cycloid://service-catalogs-repositories`**: Access to service catalog repositories information
- **`cycloid://events`**: Access to recent organization events as JSON
- **`cycloid://pipelines`**: Access to pipeline information

### Event Filters
- **begin/end**: Unix timestamps (strings) delimiting the time window
- **severity**: One or more of `info`, `warn`, `err`, `crit`
- **type**: One or more of `Cycloid`, `AWS`, `Monitoring`, `Custom`

## Architecture

The server uses a dynamic component registration system based on FastMCP's MCPMixin:

- **Automatic Discovery**: Components are automatically discovered from `src/components/`
- **File-based Organization**: Components are organized by feature (`catalogs/`, `stacks/`)
- **Standard Patterns**: Each component follows the pattern `*_tools.py`, `*_resources.py`, `*_handlers.py`, `*_prompts.py`
- **MCPMixin Integration**: Uses FastMCP's built-in `register_all()` method for proper tool/resource registration

## HTTP Transport

The Cycloid MCP Server runs as a web service using HTTP transport. Organization and API key are provided via HTTP headers (`X-CY-ORG` and `X-CY-API-KEY`) for each request, enabling multi-tenant usage.

**Usage:** `python server.py`

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.12 or higher
- [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) package manager (recommended)
- Docker (for production deployment)
- Valid Cycloid API credentials

### Development Setup

```bash
# Clone and setup
git clone <repository-url>
cd cycloid-mcp-server
make setup

# Run development server
make dev-server
```

### Production Setup

#### Using Pre-built Docker Images

The project provides pre-built Docker images via Docker Hub:

```bash
# Pull the latest image
docker pull cycloid/cycloid-mcp-server:latest

# Run the server
docker run -p 8010:8010 cycloid/cycloid-mcp-server:latest
```

#### Building Locally

```bash
# Build Docker image
make build

# Run production server
make prod-server
```

## MCP Configuration

For detailed MCP server configuration examples, see [mcp-examples.md](mcp-examples.md).

## Available Commands

```bash
# Development Environment
make setup          # Setup development environment with uv
make install        # Install dependencies
make help           # Show all available commands
make validate-env   # Validate local environment matches CI

# Development Server
make dev-server     # Run development server using Python virtual environment

# HTTP Server
python server.py  # Run HTTP server

# Production
make build          # Build Docker image
make prod-server    # Run production server using Docker

# Testing and Quality
make test           # Run all tests
make type-check     # Run pyright type checking
make lint           # Run PEP 8 linting with flake8
make format         # Format code with black and isort
make quality-check  # Run all quality checks (tests + type checking + linting)
make simulate-ci    # Validate environment and run quality checks

# Cleanup
make clean          # Clean up development artifacts
make clean-docker   # Clean up Docker artifacts
```

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed development guidelines.

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE file for details.

readme.markdown:
# Foqal MCP

**Connect your AI to Foqal's complete enterprise workflow platform with the Model Context Protocol**

Transform your AI assistant from a conversational tool into a functional extension of your entire organization. Foqal MCP is a remote MCP server that gives your AI direct access to Foqal's powerful workflow tools across support, IT, HR, and operations teams—no complex API integrations required.

## 🚀 What is Foqal MCP?

Foqal MCP is a standardized way to connect AI assistants to Foqal's comprehensive suite of enterprise workflow functionalities. It enables your AI to take real actions like:

- ❇️ Execute automations utilizing many of Foqals integrations with services like Slack, Teams, Okta, Google Admin, etc
- 💬 Create and manage support tickets and service requests
- 📊 Access user information and request history
- 🔄 Update ticket statuses and add comments
- 📋 Create and manage custom forms and workflows
- 🔍 Search knowledge base articles

All through natural language commands—just describe what you want done.

## ⚡ Key Features

- **Complete Workflow Platform** - Manage support, IT, HR, and operations workflows in one place
- **Direct Ticket Access** - Create, update, and manage tickets through natural language
- **Knowledge Base Integration** - Pull answers from your Foqal knowledge base
- **Multiple App Connections** - Access Foqal's integrations with Slack, Teams, Microsoft, Google Workspace, Jira, Zendesk, Okta and more
- **Natural Language** - No complex commands needed
- **Secure by Default** - Authentication, encryption, and rate limiting handled by Foqal
- **Advanced AI Capabilities** - AI Deflection, automated knowledge building, and reporting

## 🔧 Integration and Setup

Foqal MCP integrates with your existing Foqal setup and provides a standardized interface for AI assistants to interact with your workflow systems. The MCP server handles authentication, permissions, and rate limiting to ensure secure and reliable operations.

To set up Foqal MCP:

1. Login to Foqal, navigate to settings → AI section, and find the MCP section.
2. Create an MCP server and configure the permissions, actions, and tools you would like it to have access to.
3. Once you create, you will get a unique MCP server url that you can connect your 3rd party tool with.

## 💻 Use Cases by Department

### Customer Support

- **AI Deflection** - Automatically answer common questions before creating tickets
- **Ticket Management** - Create, update, and resolve support tickets
- **Knowledge Base** - Automatically build knowledge articles from resolved tickets
- **Customer Interaction** - Manage customer communications across channels

### IT Operations

- **Service Desk Management** - Handle IT requests and incidents
- **User Provisioning** - Connect with Okta and other identity providers
- **Asset Management** - Track and manage IT assets
- **Self-Service Portal** - Empower users to resolve common IT issues

### HR Services

- **Employee Onboarding** - Streamline new hire processes
- **Benefits Management** - Handle benefits inquiries and requests
- **Time Off Requests** - Process and track employee time off
- **HR Knowledge Base** - Provide easy access to policies and procedures
- **Integration with HRIS** - Seamless connection to your HRIS

### Operations

- **Workflow Automation** - Create custom automations for repetitive tasks
- **Project Tracking** - Manage operations projects and initiatives
- **Cross-Department Collaboration** - Enable secure participation across teams
- **Reporting and Analytics** - Track performance metrics and trends

## 🔧 Available Tools

Foqal MCP provides access to various tools, including:

- **Ticket Management** - Create, update, and resolve tickets across departments
- **Knowledge Base** - Find, retrieve, and create knowledge articles
- **Integration Access** - Interact with connected third-party systems
- **Automation Builder** - Create and debug workflow automations

readme.markdown:
# FusionAuth API MCP Server (fusionauth-mcp-api)

Using this MCP server requires a FusionAuth API key which is stored in the MCP client configuration. Scope the API key appropriately.

FusionAuth is not responsible for potentially leaking sensitive information.

## Prerequisites

* A running FusionAuth instance
* Node.js

## Configuration

First, set up a limited API key in the FusionAuth instance. Here's documentation on [creating an API key](https://fusionauth.io/docs/apis/authentication#create-an-api-key) and [configuring the correct permissions for an API key](https://fusionauth.io/docs/apis/authentication#api-key-permissions).

Next, configure your MCP client to use the FusionAuth API MCP server.

For example, to add to Claude Desktop, edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` to include the `fusionauth-mcp-api` key below. 

If you don't have any previous MCP servers installed, it would look like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
      "fusionauth-mcp-api": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "@fusionauth/mcp-api"
      ],
      "env": {
        "API_KEY_APIKEYAUTH": "<your fusionauth api key>",
        "API_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:9011",
        "USE_TOOLS": "retrieve,search"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `USE_TOOLS` env variable above essentially restricts the available tools to read-only operations. You can omit this variable to allow full access, but you will need a model that can handle about 200k tokens.

Consult your MCP client's documentation to determine exactly how to add an MCP server to your client.

## Example Prompts

* "which tools do you have access to?" should show you all the FusionAuth API tools
* "how many fusionauth applications do I have?"
* "how many users do I have in my fusionauth instance?"
* "add a user with an email address of test@example.com and a password of 'password'" (requires less restricted tools)

## Restricting Tools

The default MCP Server has a tool for every API endpoint of FusionAuth. Over 300 of them!
However, the tools, descriptions, requests, and responses combine to nearly 200k tokens, 
which can exceed the context window of many MCP clients.

You can restrict which tools this MCP server makes available by setting the USE_TOOLS env 
variable as shown above.

Each tool is defined by its prefix. The default prefixes are:

* `create`
* `delete`
* `patch`
* `update`
* `retrieve`
* `search`

There is also an `other` tool bucket that contains every tool with another prefix. The `all` tool bucket includes all tools and is the default value.

For example, if you don't need to use any `delete` or `patch` methods, the following setting reduces the tool list by 20%.

```
USE_TOOLS="create,update,retrieve,search,other"
```

If you only want to allow read-only operations, use the following configuration:

```
USE_TOOLS="retrieve,search"
```

This also reduces the tool list size by 66%.

## Securing Your MCP Server

There are three different approaches to secure your MCP server and you should combine them to enable secure access to your FusionAuth instance while still meeting your functionality needs. In order of granularity (from coarse to fine-grained):

* Point to the correct instance.
* Enable the correct type of tools. In addition to reducing context window usage, limiting the type of requests your LLM can make can increase security. For instance, if you don't enable the `delete` set of tools, you don't have to worry about the LLM "helping" you by deleting FusionAuth configuration.
* Lock down your API key. This allows fine-grained control beyond the tool choice. The MCP server communicates to FusionAuth using an API key. You can limit that API key to only allow it to act on tenants, applications and users by choosing the [appropriate set of permissions](https://fusionauth.io/docs/apis/authentication#api-key-permissions). 

## Troubleshooting

Verify your API key has the correct permissions for the operation the MCP client is taking.

Check your MCP client logs; these vary by MCP client and platform. For example, `$HOME/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-fusionauth-api-server.log` is the location for Claude Desktop on macOS. Consult your client's documentation for the precise location.

Use the modelcontextprotocol inspector to help determine if the issue is with the MCP server or with your MCP client: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector`. If you want to change the `USE_TOOLS` variable, you cannot dynamically change it and must pass it on the command line. `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector npx @fusionauth/mcp-api -e API_KEY_APIKEYAUTH=... -e USE_TOOLS=create`

## Building Locally

You can also build and run this locally.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/FusionAuth/fusionauth-mcp-api.git
cd fusionauth-mcp-api
cd packages/mcp-api
npm install
npm run build

# optional step to store config information in .env file
cp .env.example .env
# optionally edit .env to set API_BASE_URL and API_KEY_APIKEYAUTH
```

Then, similar to the instructions above, configure your MCP client to use the FusionAuth API MCP server.

For example, to add to Claude Desktop, edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` to include the `fusionauth-mcp-api` key below. If you don't have any previous MCP servers installed, it would look like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fusionauth-mcp-api": {
      "command": "npm",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--silent",
        "--prefix",
        "<path to local git repo>/fusionauth-mcp-api/packages/mcp-api",
        "start"
      ],
      "env": {
        "API_KEY_APIKEYAUTH": "<your fusionauth api key>",
        "API_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:9011",
        "USE_TOOLS": "retrieve,search"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

You can omit the `env` section above if you have configured an `.env` file.

## Publishing

bin/updatemcp.sh
git commit <changed files>
git tag <tag>
git push origin main --tags
npm publish --access public --workspace=packages/mcp-api

name: bettermemory
description: Memory for coding agents, checked against the filesystem and git before it is believed.

readme.markdown:
An MCP memory server for coding agents. Stored facts get checked against
the filesystem and git *before* the model relies on them, so a memory
that has rotted is flagged instead of quoted back at you.

## Install

Claude Code — two slash commands, zero config:

```
/plugin marketplace add 0Mattias/bettermemory
/plugin install bettermemory@bettermemory
```

Anything else that speaks MCP:

```sh
uv tool install bettermemory
bettermemory init --client claude-desktop   # or cursor / cline / claude-code / hermes
```

Restart the client. `bettermemory doctor` exits 0 when it's wired
correctly and prints a one-line fix for anything that isn't.

Try it without installing: `uvx bettermemory try` writes a memory
citing a file, deletes the file, and shows the next search flagging it.
Offline, throwaway store.

## What it does

- Checks memory before believing it. Every hit carries a staleness
  verdict: calendar age, whether the paths it cites still exist, the
  commits landed since it was last confirmed, and how the record
  entered the store (written here, pulled, or placed by hand).
  Declared claims
  (`path`, `path::symbol`, `path::NAME=literal`) are re-checked
  against the working tree; a claim that stops being true blocks the
  stamp instead of riding along.
- Retrieval is deliberate. Memory is a tool call, not an
  injection. Write gates bounce transient state, secret-shaped tokens
  and near-duplicates; claims about *you* are labelled as inferences,
  so they stay distinguishable and correctable.
- The code is the model. Search is deterministic lexical ranking —
  keyword + BM25, fused — over your own vocabulary. No embedding
  models, no downloads, nothing to warm up, same answer every time.
- Plain files. One markdown file per memory. Greppable,
  git-syncable, no cloud, no account. The SQLite index beside the
  files is a derived cache you can delete; `bettermemory reindex`
  rebuilds it.
- Rot gets acted on, not accumulated. Episodes journal per-session
  run-state without polluting durable search; health telemetry and
  curation tools surface what drifted, what went cold, and what
  contradicts what.
- Receipts, not adjectives. The claims above are measured by
  preregistered benchmarks whose frozen result artifacts — misses
  included — live in [bench/][bench] (`results/*.json`, each carrying
  the declared terms it was scored under), and `bettermemory eval`
  scores whether memory actually helped against your own log ([ours
  is published][eval-results]).

## For agents

You were likely handed this link with "set this up." On Claude Code,
the two plugin commands above are the whole install — skip to step 3.
Everywhere else, steps are idempotent and safe to re-run:

1. `uv tool install bettermemory` — or `pipx install bettermemory`,
   or `pip install bettermemory` into a venv. Python 3.11–3.14.
2. `bettermemory init --client claude-code` — likewise
   `claude-desktop`, `cursor`, `cline`, `hermes`. For any other MCP host, plain
   `bettermemory init` prints the canonical `mcpServers` JSON snippet
   plus known config locations. (Continue needs a hand-written YAML
   entry — see [docs/clients.md][clients-continue].)
3. `bettermemory doctor` — exit 0 means correctly wired; every failed
   check prints a one-line fix.
4. Have the user restart the client so the server loads, then confirm
   by asking the model *"what memory tools do you have?"*

Your operating contract — tool signatures, retrieval discipline,
write gates — is [docs/api.md][api]; the server's
`instructions` block delivers the core policy automatically. For the
long-form policy in your system prompt: `bettermemory init
--with-addendum`. Migrating from Claude Code's built-in auto-memory:
`bettermemory ingest` imports those files once.

## Everything else

The rest is written down: mechanics, storage format, the full tool
surface, CLI, configuration and limitations in
[internals][internals]; per-client setup in [clients][clients] and
[installation][installation]; eval methodology in [eval][eval];
postmortems in [incidents][incidents]; release history in
[CHANGELOG][changelog]; dev setup and the compatibility contract in
[CONTRIBUTING][contributing].

MIT licensed — see [LICENSE][license].

# Hedgehood agent kit

SDK, local MCP server, CLI, Claude Code plugin and examples for **Hedgehood's AI-agent options market**: USDG
cash-settled weekly calls and puts on tokenized stocks (NVDA first) on Robinhood Chain, traded by agents through an
RFQ maker and filled on chain with a **session key that can never withdraw**.

> **Non-US only.** The market is for agents and operators outside the United States. Mainnet (chain 4663) lists seven
> V2 markets (NVDA, TSLA, MU, GOOGL, CRCL, MSTR, AMD) settled in real USDG; the testnet (46630) settles in a test token
> with no value. **The kit defaults to the testnet**: pass `--mainnet` (or set `HEDGEHOOD_CHAIN_ID=4663`) to trade real
> funds.

| package | what | install |
|---|---|---|
| [`@hedgehood-io/sdk`](packages/sdk) | viem-based TypeScript SDK: deployments, ABIs, instrument ids, EIP-712 orders, `fillOrderAs` calldata, RFQ client with local quote verification, `closePosition`, one-account view and funding plans across markets (`readAccount`, `planFillFunding`, `planRebalance`), P&L and history readers, x402 USDG payer, ERC-8004 helpers, `VaultClient` for the Stock Yield vaults, `LendingClient` for share lending (lend USDG / borrow against fund shares) | `pnpm add @hedgehood-io/sdk viem` |
| [`@hedgehood-io/mcp`](packages/mcp) | local MCP server (stdio + streamable HTTP) signing with the agent's key; 37 tools (23 market + 6 vault + 8 lending), every write needs `confirm: true` and is a dry run by default | `npx -y @hedgehood-io/mcp` |
| [`@hedgehood-io/cli`](packages/cli) | `hedgehood` binary: `init`, `status`, `join`, `account`, `deposit`, `quote`, `fill`, `close`, `positions`, `pnl`, `history`, `redeem`, `withdraw [--all]`, `rebalance`, `session authorize\|revoke\|status`, `vaults`, `vault status\|deposit\|redeem\|claim\|cancel`, `lend status\|deposit\|withdraw`, `borrow status\|collateral\|take\|repay\|withdraw-collateral` | `npx @hedgehood-io/cli --help` |
| [`skills/hedgehood-options`](skills/hedgehood-options/SKILL.md) | the skill an agent reads: market model, the loop, the Stock Yield vaults, share lending, key hygiene, troubleshooting | `/plugin marketplace add 0xHedgeHood/hedgehood-agent-kit` |
| [`examples/`](examples) | a 30-line "agent buys a weekly call" script and an MCP config snippet | `pnpm tsx examples/buy-weekly-call.ts` |

## Connect an agent in 2 minutes

You keep the account in your own wallet (for example a browser wallet on hedgehood.io). The agent gets a **session key**
with a budget you sign: it can trade, it can never withdraw. Optionally it also gets a small **payment wallet** that
tops up your market balances over x402.

**Agent machine, one command** (Node 20+):

```sh
npx -y @hedgehood-io/cli@latest init --mainnet --account 0xYourWallet --with-payer
# or: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xHedgeHood/hedgehood-agent-kit/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --mainnet --account 0xYourWallet --with-payer
```

It creates `~/.hedgehood/session.key` (and with `--with-payer` `~/.hedgehood/payer.key`), mode 600, only if missing;
prints each address with a QR code, the payment wallet's USDG balance, your authorize link (with its QR code) and the
MCP config for Claude Code, Claude Desktop / Cursor and the hosted read-only server; and saves the non-secret
settings (chain, owner, key paths) to `~/.hedgehood/config.json`, so later `hedgehood` and `hedgehood-mcp` runs need
no flags (flags > environment > that file). Private keys are never printed.

**Owner, once:** open the link on the device with your wallet, or scan its QR code with the wallet's browser:

```
https://hedgehood.io/options/account?agent=<session key address>&chain=4663[&markets=NVDA,TSLA][&maxSpend=100][&days=30]
```

pick the markets, the spend budget and the days, and sign (session keys are per market). Pass `--markets`,
`--max-spend` and `--days` to `init` to prefill them; `--site-url` (or `HEDGEHOOD_SITE_URL`) changes the site; on the
testnet the link says `chain=46630`.

**Done:** `hedgehood init --wait` (or `hedgehood status`) shows per market whether the key is authorized, the budget
left, the expiry and the balance, and prints `READY` with a first quote + buy of one share. `hedgehood status --qr`
prints the QR codes again. (Without a global install, `hedgehood` is `npx -y @hedgehood-io/cli`; or
`npm i -g @hedgehood-io/cli`.)

Funding: you deposit on the site, or send USDG on Robinhood Chain to the payment wallet and let the agent pay a
deposit in (`hedgehood deposit 25 --market NVDA --send`, or the MCP tool `deposit_x402`). The payment wallet needs
**no ETH**: an x402 deposit is an EIP-3009 signature that the facilitator submits. The gateway takes 1 to 1,000 USDG per
deposit and 5,000 per account per day. Week-1 limits: 2 shares per option, 2.5 per underlying, opening premium at
least 5 USDG, quotes in US regular hours.

## Quickstart (testnet, 5 minutes)

```sh
# 1. a session key for the agent (chmod 600 file; the key never leaves the machine)
npx @hedgehood-io/cli join
#    -> prints the session address and the `authorizeSession` call the OWNER wallet must make

# 2. owner wallet (anywhere): authorize the session with a spend budget (here 100 USDG of premium + fees) and deposit tUSDG
cast send <market> 'authorizeSession(address,uint64,uint256,uint256,uint256)' <session> <expiresAt> 3 0 100000000 --rpc-url https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com
#    (scope 3 = trade + cancel; maxShortRisk 0 = the key cannot sell to open; maxSpend 100 USDG raw; or, with the
#    owner key on this machine: `hedgehood session authorize --max-spend 100 [--max-short-risk 60] --send`)
cast send 0x539574139BB4Ac74Fd2183ba0E38ed777E30B58d 'approve(address,uint256)' 0xC289617d613C9865a6595B365DaD88277282e0Ac 100000000 --rpc-url ...
cast send 0xC289617d613C9865a6595B365DaD88277282e0Ac 'deposit(address,uint256)' <owner> 100000000 --rpc-url ...
#    (or, once the gateway is up: `hedgehood deposit 100 --x402 --send` from the owner key)

# 3. trade from the agent mach

readme.markdown: Microsoft MCP Model Context Protocol servers for Microsoft 365. Calendar · Contacts · OneDrive · Outlook · SharePoint — on the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, over stdio or Streamable HTTP. Each server speaks the real MCP protocol and runs over **either transport**: - **stdio** — for local MCP clients that launch the server as a subprocess (Claude Desktop, IDEs, the MCP Inspector). - **Streamable HTTP** — for remote/hosted use, with the Microsoft Graph access token supplied per request via `Authorization: Bearer`. ## Servers | | Server | npm package (and binary) | Tools | | :-: | ----------- | ------------------------- | ----: | | | Calendar | `ms-calendar-mcp` | 9 | | | Contacts | `ms-contacts-mcp` | 7 | | | OneDrive | `ms-onedrive-mcp` | 9 | | | Outlook | `microsoft-outlook-mcp` | 14 | | | SharePoint | `ms-sharepoint-mcp` | 23 | All tools are thin wrappers over the [Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/) `v1.0` API. ## Layout ``` microsoft-mcp/ ├── apps/ # one MCP server per Microsoft 365 product │ ├── calendar/ │ ├── contacts/ │ ├── onedrive/ │ ├── outlook/ │ └── sharepoint/ │ └── src/ │ ├── tools.ts # declarative tool definitions (schema + handler) │ └── index.ts # run({ name, version }, tools) └── packages/ # shared building blocks ├── core/ # MCP server bootstrap + dual transport (stdio / HTTP) ├── graph/ # Microsoft Graph HTTP client ├── validation/ # id / path / query sanitizers └── logger/ # structured JSON logging (stderr-only — stdio-safe) ``` A server is just a list of tools handed to `run()`: ```ts // apps/calendar/src/index.ts import { run } from "@microsoft-mcp/core"; import { tools } from "./tools.js"; void run({ name: "microsoft-calendar", version: "1.0.0", title: "Microsoft Calendar" }, tools); ``` ```ts // a single tool defineTool({ name: "get_event", description: "Get a single calendar event by ID.", inputSchema: { event_id: z.string().describe("Event ID") }, confirmationPolicy: "never", handler: ({ graph }, { event_id }) => { validateId(event_id, "event_id"); return graph.request("GET", `/me/events/${event_id}`); }, }); ``` `confirmationPolicy` (`"always"` for mutating/destructive tools, `"never"` for read-only) is surfaced to clients as MCP `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint` annotations. ## Requirements - Node.js >= 20 - pnpm 10 (`corepack enable`) ## Setup ```bash pnpm install pnpm build # build all servers (turbo) -> apps/*/dist/index.js pnpm check-types # typecheck everything ``` ## Tests & CI ```bash pnpm test # run the vitest suite once pnpm test:watch # watch mode pnpm test:coverage # run with a v8 coverage report (-> coverage/) ``` Tests live next to the code as `*.test.ts` and run on TypeScript source directly (no build step). The shared `packages/*` are covered by unit and integration tests — including a full Streamable-HTTP round-trip against a live server — and CI enforces a coverage floor on them. Each `apps/*` server ships an invariant suite that locks its tool surface (unique snake_case names, valid schemas and confirmation policies). Every push and pull request to `master` runs [CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml): typecheck → build → tests with coverage. The coverage badge is regenerated from the run. ## Authentication You sign in **once** with your Microsoft account; the server then caches a refresh token and acquires access tokens silently from then on — no pasting, no 1-hour expiry. Sign-in uses your own [Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app) app registration (free) so the servers act on your behalf. ### 1. Register an Entra ID app (one time) 1. [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com) → **Microsoft Entra ID** → **App registrations** → **New registration**. Name it anything; pick the **Supported account types** that fit (single-tenant, multi-tenant, and/or personal accounts). 2. **Authentication** → **Add a platform** → **Mobile and desktop applications** → add redirect URI **`http://localhost`**, and set **Allow public client flows** to **Yes** (enables the `--device-code` fallback). 3. **API permissions** → **Add a permission** → **Microsoft Graph** → **Delegated permissions** → add the scopes for the servers you use (then **Grant admin consent** if your tenant requires it): | Server | Delegated scopes | | --- | --- | | Calendar | `Calendars.ReadWrite` | | Contacts | `Contacts.ReadWrite` | | OneDrive | `Files.ReadWrite.All` | | Outlook | `Mail.ReadWrite`, `Mail.Send` | | SharePoint | `Sites.ReadWrite.All` | All servers also use `User.Read`. (`offline_access` is requested automatically for refresh.) 4. Copy the **Application (client) ID**. ### 2. Sign in (one time per machine) Set `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, then run the server's **`login`** command. A browser opens; after you consent, the token is cached under `~/.config/microsoft-mcp/`: ```bash export MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID= npx -y ms-calendar-mcp login # opens the browser npx -y ms-calendar-mcp login --device-code # headless: shows a code to enter ``` From then on the server refreshes tokens automatically. Use a non-default tenant with `MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID` (default `common`). ### Advanced: supply your own token To bypass the built-in flow, supply a pre-acquired Graph token directly: - **stdio:** set `MICROSOFT_ACCESS_TOKEN` (takes precedence over the cached sign-in). Good for quick tests — mint one with `az account get-access-token --resource https://graph.microsoft.com --query accessToken -o tsv`. - **HTTP:** send `Authorization: Bearer ` on each `POST /mcp` request. …

readme.markdown:
# Apiary Memory MCP

## The problem it solves

You explain your project to one AI today. Next week you explain it again to a different one, from scratch — because each tool keeps its own memory, and none of that memory is yours to move.

This is a memory box that sits on your own disk. Any MCP-capable AI can read it. An agent can *propose* what to remember, but nothing is written until you approve it. Switch to another AI next month and the memory stays where it was — it was never the AI's to begin with.

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **What it is** | Local-first personal memory for AI agents, over MCP. Agents can search what you have confirmed and *propose* what to keep — only you can confirm it. Everything lives in one SQLite file on your own disk. |
| **What it is not** | Not a hosted service. No account, no cloud, no telemetry, no daemon. The server runs on *your* machine (`127.0.0.1`), not ours. |
